// ── Module state ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Real AppId of the currently-launched -onlinefix game (0 = none).
static ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
/// True once the game opens a SteamNetworkingSockets P2P connection.
static NETWORKING_SOCKETS_ACTIVE: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
/// Set by `-realappid` on the launch command line; suppresses the P2P
/// appid flip for this launch only.
static SUPPRESS_APPID_FLIP: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

static GAME_NAME_CACHE: Lazy<Mutex<HashMap<AppId_t, String>>> =
    Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));

// ── SpawnProcess int3 callback ──────────────────────────────────────
//
// `strstr`-equivalent search on a NUL-terminated buffer. `needle` must
// not include a trailing NUL; the C++ passes a bare literal.
unsafe fn c_str_contains(haystack: *const i8, needle: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if haystack.is_null() || needle.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    let s = CStr::from_ptr(haystack);
    let hb = s.to_bytes();
    if hb.len() < needle.len() {
        return false;
    }
    hb.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle)
}

fn on_spawn_process_hit(ctx: &mut Context, _site: &Int3Site) {
    // Argument order per the C++:
    //   arg1 pCUser, arg2 pExePath, arg3 pCommandLine, arg4 pWorkingDir,
    //   arg5 pGameID (CGameID*; low 24 bits are the AppId).
    let p_game_id = ctx.argument(5) as *mut CGameID;
    let cmd_line = ctx.argument(3) as *const i8;
    if p_game_id.is_null() {
        return;
    }

    let (app_id, has_onlinefix, suppress) = unsafe {
        let id = (*p_game_id).app_id(true);
        let onfix = c_str_contains(cmd_line, b"-onlinefix");
        let supp = onfix && c_str_contains(cmd_line, b"-realappid");
        (id, onfix, supp)
    };

    if has_onlinefix {
        ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.store(app_id, Ordering::Release);
        NETWORKING_SOCKETS_ACTIVE.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        SUPPRESS_APPID_FLIP.store(suppress, Ordering::Release);
        unsafe {
            (*p_game_id).set_app_id(K_ONLINE_FIX_APPID);
        }
        LOG_MISC_INFO!(
            "SpawnProcess: appid {} -> {}, realappid={}",
            app_id,
            K_ONLINE_FIX_APPID,
            suppress
        );
    } else {
        ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.store(0, Ordering::Release);
        SUPPRESS_APPID_FLIP.store(false, Ordering::Release);
    }
}

// ── Hooked functions ────────────────────────────────────────────────

hook_fn! {
    fn OptedInMask(p_this: *mut c_void, app_id: AppId_t) -> i64 {
        let mut app_id = app_id;
        let real = ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        if app_id == K_ONLINE_FIX_APPID && real != 0 {
            LOG_MISC_INFO!("OptedInMask: appid {} -> {}", app_id, real);
            app_id = real;
        }
        o_OptedInMask(p_this, app_id)
    }
}

hook_fn! {
    fn BuildSpawnEnvBlock(
        p_this: *mut c_void,
        p_cgame_id: *mut CGameID,
        a3: *mut c_void,
        env: *mut c_void,
        p_overlay_cgame_id: *mut CGameID,
        a6: *mut c_void,
        a7: i32,
        a8: *mut c_void,
        a9: *mut c_void,
        a10: u32,
        a11: i8,
    ) -> i64 {
        let real = ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        if real != 0 && !p_overlay_cgame_id.is_null() {
            let overlay_app = (*p_overlay_cgame_id).app_id(true);
            if overlay_app == K_ONLINE_FIX_APPID {
                LOG_MISC_INFO!(
                    "BuildSpawnEnvBlock: SetAppID in OverlayCGameID {} -> {}",
                    overlay_app,
                    real
                );
                (*p_overlay_cgame_id).set_app_id(real);
            }
        }
        o_BuildSpawnEnvBlock(
            p_this, p_cgame_id, a3, env,
            p_overlay_cgame_id, a6, a7,
            a8, a9, a10, a11,
        )
    }
}

// `GetOrAddAppData` is declared in the C++ header and defined in the
// .cpp, but its install line is commented out in `HookManager`-adjacent
// code and remains so here. The body would consult
// `LuaConfig::HasDepot` and `CAppData::IsUnresolvedAppInfo` and set
// `bSkipFlag`; since the hook never installs, porting it is deferred
// until a reason to enable it appears.

// ── Public API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub fn get_app_id_for_current_pipe_wrap() -> AppId_t {
    if !(capture_ready!(GetAppIDForCurrentPipe)) {
        LOG_MISC_WARN!(
            "GetAppIDForCurrentPipeWrap called before capture - returning 0"
        );
        return 0;
    }
    let engine = unsafe { CAPTURED_GET_APP_I_D_FOR_CURRENT_PIPE.load() };
    let app_id = unsafe { o_GetAppIDForCurrentPipe(engine) };
    if app_id == 0 {
        LOG_MISC_TRACE!("GetAppIDForCurrentPipeWrap: AppId=0(Not GamePipe)");
    } else {
        LOG_MISC_TRACE!("GetAppIDForCurrentPipeWrap: AppId={}", app_id);
    }
    app_id
}

pub fn resolve_app_id() -> AppId_t {
    let real = ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if real != 0 {
        return real;
    }
    get_app_id_for_current_pipe_wrap()
}

pub fn is_onlinefix_active() -> bool {
    ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 0
}

pub fn notify_networking_sockets_used() {
    if ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 0
        && !NETWORKING_SOCKETS_ACTIVE.load(Ordering::Acquire)
    {
        NETWORKING_SOCKETS_ACTIVE.store(true, Ordering::Release);
        LOG_MISC_INFO!(
            "NetworkingSockets active: GetAppID now reports 480 for cert match"
        );
    }
}

pub fn should_report_onlinefix_app_id() -> bool {
    // The flip exists so a P2P socket's appid matches the 480 session
    // cert, which some titles need. It is blunt though: from the moment
    // it trips, every GetAppID answer is the fake appid for the rest of
    // the process's life. Games that ask Steam for their own appid during
    // later startup then get 480 and misbehave. Both behaviours are
    // needed by different games, and the call itself gives no way to
    // tell them apart, so `-realappid` opts out per launch.
    if SUPPRESS_APPID_FLIP.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
        return false;
    }
    ONLINE_FIX_REAL_APPID.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 0
        && NETWORKING_SOCKETS_ACTIVE.load(Ordering::Acquire)
}

pub fn ensure_buffer_capacity(
    p_write: *mut CUtlBuffer,
    new_capacity: u32,
    update_put: bool,
) -> bool {
    if unsafe { O_C_UTL_BUFFER_ENSURE_CAPACITY.is_null() } {
        LOG_MISC_WARN!("EnsureBufferCapacity: oCUtlBufferEnsureCapacity not resolved");
        return false;
    }
    if !p_write.is_null() {
        let cap = unsafe { (*p_write).m_Memory.m_nAllocationCount };
        LOG_MISC_DEBUG!(
            "Before ensuring CUtlBuffer capacity: cap={} put={} get={}",
            cap,
            unsafe { (*p_write).m_Put },
            unsafe { (*p_write).m_Get },
        );
    }
    unsafe {
        o_CUtlBufferEnsureCapacity(p_write, new_capacity);
        if update_put && !p_write.is_null() {
            (*p_write).m_Put = new_capacity as i32;
        }
        if !p_write.is_null() {
            let cap = (*p_write).m_Memory.m_nAllocationCount;
            LOG_MISC_DEBUG!(
                "After ensuring CUtlBuffer capacity: cap={} put={} get={}",
                cap,
                (*p_write).m_Put,
                (*p_write).m_Get,
            );
        }
    }
    true
}

pub fn get_game_name_by_app_id(app_id: AppId_t) -> String {
    if let Some(cached) = GAME_NAME_CACHE.lock().get(&app_id).cloned() {
        return cached;
    }

    let mut name = String::new();
    if capture_ready!(GetAppDataFromAppInfo) {
        let mut buf = [0u8; 256];
        // "common/name" triggers auto-localization in the C++ helper:
        // prefix "common" (keyType=2) + key "name", then the helper tries
        // "name_localized/<current_lang>" before falling back to "name".
        // Returns strlen+1 on success, -1 on failure.
        let key = b"common/name\0";
        let p_this = unsafe { CAPTURED_GET_APP_DATA_FROM_APP_INFO.load() };
        let len = unsafe {
            o_GetAppDataFromAppInfo(
                p_this,
                app_id,
                key.as_ptr() as *const i8,
                buf.as_mut_ptr(),
                buf.len() as i32,
            )
        };
        if len > 1 {
            let n = (len - 1) as usize;
            if n <= buf.len() {
                name = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..n]).into_owned();
            }
        }
    }

    LOG_MISC_DEBUG!("GetGameNameByAppID({}): {}", app_id, name);
    GAME_NAME_CACHE.lock().insert(app_id, name.clone());
    name
}

pub fn install() -> bool {
    resolve_c!(CUtlBufferEnsureCapacity);

    arm_capture_c!(GetAppIDForCurrentPipe);
    arm_capture_c!(GetAppDataFromAppInfo);

    arm_int3_c!(SpawnProcess, true, on_spawn_process_hit, std::ptr::null_mut());

    let ok1 = install_hook_c!(BuildSpawnEnvBlock);
    let ok2 = install_hook_c!(OptedInMask);
    ok1 && ok2
}

pub fn uninstall() -> bool {
    let ok1 = uninstall_hook!(BuildSpawnEnvBlock);
    let ok2 = uninstall_hook!(OptedInMask);
    ok1 && ok2
}

===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\access_token.rs =====
//! `Hooks_NetPacket_AccessToken`. Outgoing
//! `CMsgClientPicsProductInfoRequest` (eMsg 8903).

use prost::Message;

use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientPicsProductInfoRequest;
use crate::utils::config::lua_config;

/// Patch `access_token` into each `apps[i]` entry whose appid is in
/// Lua's `addtoken` set. Returns `Some(new_body)` when at least one
/// patch was applied, `None` otherwise.
pub fn handle_send(body: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let req = CMsgClientPicsProductInfoRequest::decode(body).ok()?;
    LOG_PICS_DEBUG!(
        "CMsgClientPicsProductInfoRequest: {} apps, {} packages",
        req.apps.len(), req.packages.len(),
    );

    let mut needs_patch = false;
    for app in &req.apps {
        let appid = app.appid.unwrap_or(0);
        if lua_config::has_depot(appid, false)
            && lua_config::get_access_token(appid) != 0
        {
            needs_patch = true;
            LOG_PICS_DEBUG!(
                "CMsgClientPICSProductInfoRequest: found appid {} with access_token, need patching",
                appid,
            );
            break;
        }
    }
    if !needs_patch {
        LOG_PICS_TRACE!(
            "CMsgClientPICSProductInfoRequest: no apps need token injection, skip"
        );
        return None;
    }

    let mut req = req;
    let mut injected = 0;
    let mut no_token = 0;
    let mut not_addappid = 0;
    for app in req.apps.iter_mut() {
        let appid = app.appid.unwrap_or(0);
        if lua_config::has_depot(appid, false) {
            let token = lua_config::get_access_token(appid);
            if token != 0 {
                LOG_PICS_DEBUG!(
                    "CMsgClientPICSProductInfoRequest: inject appid={}: {} -> {}",
                    appid,
                    app.access_token.map(|t| t.to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| "absent".into()),
                    token,
                );
                app.access_token = Some(token);
                injected += 1;
            } else {
                LOG_PICS_WARN!(
                    "CMsgClientPICSProductInfoRequest: skip appid={}: in depot, no token configured",
                    appid,
                );
                no_token += 1;
            }
        } else {
            not_addappid += 1;
        }
    }
    LOG_PICS_DEBUG!(
        "CMsgClientPICSProductInfoRequest: injected={} no_token={} not_in_add_appid={} total={}",
        injected, no_token, not_addappid, req.apps.len(),
    );

    let encoded = req.encode_to_vec();
    if encoded.len() > super::state::K_MAX_BODY_SIZE {
        LOG_PICS_WARN!(
            "CMsgClientPICSProductInfoRequest: encoded size {} exceeds buffer",
            encoded.len(),
        );
        return None;
    }
    Some(encoded)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientPicsProductInfoRequest;

    fn encode(req: &CMsgClientPicsProductInfoRequest) -> Vec<u8> {
        req.encode_to_vec()
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_apps_needs_patch_returns_none() {
        let req = CMsgClientPicsProductInfoRequest {
            apps: vec![crate::steam::proto::c_msg_client_pics_product_info_request::AppInfo {
                appid: Some(0xDEAD_BEEF),
                access_token: None,
                only_public_obsolete: None,
            }],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let body = encode(&req);
        assert!(handle_send(&body).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn malformed_body_returns_none() {
        assert!(handle_send(&[0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF]).is_none());
    }
}


===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\cloud.rs =====
//! `Hooks_NetPacket_Cloud`. Steam Cloud save redirection via
//! CloudRedirect.
//!
//! Outgoing: `ServiceMethodCallFromClient` (eMsg 151) with a
//! `Cloud.*` target for an addappid-unlocked game.
//!
//! Incoming: a synthesized `ServiceMethodResponse` (eMsg 147) carrying
//! the answer produced by CloudRedirect, correlated by jobid.
//!
//! CloudRedirect answers the RPC locally (reading/writing the real save
//! bytes to the user's cloud provider). This module therefore suppresses
//! the outbound request — it must not reach Valve — and delivers the
//! response the same way RichPresence injects packets: by borrowing the
//! next inbound carrier packet for one call to the original.

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use prost::Message;

use crate::steam::net_packet as netpkt;
use crate::steam::proto::CMsgProtoBufHeader;
use crate::steam::structs::{CNetPacket, MsgHdr};
use crate::utils::cloud_redirect::host as cloud_redirect;

use super::packet::K_MSG_HDR_PROTO_FLAG;
use super::state::{K_MAX_BODY_SIZE, K_MAX_HDR_SIZE, K_MAX_PACKET_SIZE};

const K_EMSG_SERVICE_METHOD_RESPONSE: u32 = 147;
const K_MAX_QUEUE_LEN: usize = 64;

static G_LOCAL_STEAM_ID: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

static CLOUD_QUEUE: Lazy<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>> =
    Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));

// ── Minimal protobuf field reader ───────────────────────────────────
//
// Reads a single varint field from the body of a Cloud.* request
// without pulling the Cloud message definitions into the proto set.
// Mirrors CloudRedirect's `CloudRpcUtils::ExtractAppId`.

fn read_varint(d: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut out: u64 = 0;
    let mut shift = 0;
    while *pos < d.len() {
        let b = d[*pos];
        *pos += 1;
        out |= ((b & 0x7F) as u64) << shift;
        if b & 0x80 == 0 { return Some(out); }
        shift += 7;
        if shift >= 64 { return None; }
    }
    None
}

fn find_varint_field(d: &[u8], target: u32) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut pos = 0usize;
    while pos < d.len() {
        let tag = read_varint(d, &mut pos)?;
        let field = (tag >> 3) as u32;
        let wire = (tag & 7) as u32;
        if field == target && wire == 0 {
            return read_varint(d, &mut pos);
        }
        match wire {
            0 => { let _ = read_varint(d, &mut pos)?; }
            1 => pos = pos.checked_add(8)?,
            5 => pos = pos.checked_add(4)?,
            2 => {
                let len = read_varint(d, &mut pos)? as usize;
                pos = pos.checked_add(len)?;
            }
            _ => return None,
        }
        if pos > d.len() { return None; }
    }
    None
}

/// The appid lives in field 1 of every Cloud.* request except
/// `ClientCommitFileUpload`, where it is field 2.
fn extract_app_id(job_name: &str, body: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    let field = if job_name == "Cloud.ClientCommitFileUpload#1" { 2 } else { 1 };
    find_varint_field(body, field).map(|v| v as u32).unwrap_or(0)
}

// ── Send ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Returns `true` when CloudRedirect handled the request; the caller
/// must then suppress the outbound frame.
pub fn handle_send(job_name: &str, body: &[u8], hdr: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if !cloud_redirect::is_active() { return false; }

    let req_hdr = match CMsgProtoBufHeader::decode(hdr) {
        Ok(h) => h,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    if let Some(sid) = req_hdr.steamid.filter(|s| *s != 0) {
        G_LOCAL_STEAM_ID.store(sid, Ordering::Release);
    }

    let app_id = extract_app_id(job_name, body);
    if app_id == 0 || !cloud_redirect::is_app(app_id) { return false; }

    let account_id = (G_LOCAL_STEAM_ID.load(Ordering::Acquire) & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32;

    // CloudRedirect writes its response into a scratch buffer.
    let mut resp_buf = vec![0u8; K_MAX_BODY_SIZE];
    let (resp_len, eresult) = match cloud_redirect::handle_cloud_rpc(
        job_name, app_id, account_id, body, &mut resp_buf,
    ) {
        Some(pair) => pair,
        None => return false,
    };

    // Build the synthesized 147 response header.
    let mut resp_hdr = CMsgProtoBufHeader::default();
    if let Some(job_id) = req_hdr.jobid_source {
        resp_hdr.jobid_target = Some(job_id);
    }
    resp_hdr.eresult = Some(eresult);
    resp_hdr.target_job_name = Some(job_name.to_string());

    let hdr_bytes = resp_hdr.encode_to_vec();
    if hdr_bytes.len() > K_MAX_HDR_SIZE || resp_len > K_MAX_BODY_SIZE {
        LOG_NETPACKET_WARN!(
            "Cloud: {} response too large (hdr={}, body={}), passing through",
            job_name, hdr_bytes.len(), resp_len,
        );
        return false;
    }

    let total = std::mem::size_of::<MsgHdr>() + hdr_bytes.len() + resp_len;
    if total > K_MAX_PACKET_SIZE {
        LOG_NETPACKET_WARN!(
            "Cloud: {} response too large ({} bytes), passing through",
            job_name, total,
        );
        return false;
    }

    let mut pkt = vec![0u8; total];
    let raw = K_EMSG_SERVICE_METHOD_RESPONSE | K_MSG_HDR_PROTO_FLAG;
    pkt[0..4].copy_from_slice(&raw.to_le_bytes());
    pkt[4..8].copy_from_slice(&(hdr_bytes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    pkt[8..8 + hdr_bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(&hdr_bytes);
    if resp_len > 0 {
        pkt[8 + hdr_bytes.len()..].copy_from_slice(&resp_buf[..resp_len]);
    }

    {
        let mut q = CLOUD_QUEUE.lock();
        if q.len() < K_MAX_QUEUE_LEN {
            q.push_back(pkt);
        }
    }
    LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!(
        "Cloud: handled {} app={} -> queued {}-byte response (eresult={})",
        job_name, app_id, total, eresult,
    );
    true
}

// ── Drain ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub fn has_pending() -> bool {
    !CLOUD_QUEUE.lock().is_empty()
}

/// Deliver any queued cloud responses by borrowing the carrier packet
/// for one call to the original each. Same trick as
/// `RichPresence::try_inject`. Runs on the network thread from inside
/// the RecvPkt hook.
///
/// # Safety
/// Caller must be inside the `RecvPkt` hook with a live `p_carrier`.
pub unsafe fn drain<F>(p_this: *mut c_void, p_carrier: *mut CNetPacket, invoke_original: F)
where
    F: Fn(*mut c_void, *mut CNetPacket) -> *mut c_void,
{
    loop {
        let mut pkt = {
            let mut q = CLOUD_QUEUE.lock();
            match q.pop_front() {
                Some(p) => p,
                None => return,
            }
        };

        let orig_data = netpkt::read_data(p_carrier as *mut u8);
        let orig_size = netpkt::read_size(p_carrier as *mut u8);

        let len = pkt.len();
        netpkt::write_data(p_carrier as *mut u8, pkt.as_mut_ptr());
        netpkt::write_size(p_carrier as *mut u8, len as u32);

        let _ = invoke_original(p_this, p_carrier);

        netpkt::write_data(p_carrier as *mut u8, orig_data);
        netpkt::write_size(p_carrier as *mut u8, orig_size);

        LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!("Cloud: delivered {}-byte response", len);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn read_varint_basic() {
        let mut pos = 0;
        assert_eq!(read_varint(&[0x2A], &mut pos), Some(42));
    }

    #[test]
    fn read_varint_multibyte() {
        // 300 = 0xAC 0x02
        let mut pos = 0;
        assert_eq!(read_varint(&[0xAC, 0x02], &mut pos), Some(300));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_varint_field_finds_appid() {
        // field 1, wire 0 => tag = (1<<3)|0 = 0x08
        // value 730 = 0xDA 0x05 (varint)
        let body = [0x08, 0xDA, 0x05];
        assert_eq!(find_varint_field(&body, 1), Some(730));
    }

    #[test]
    fn extract_app_id_uses_field_2_for_commit() {
        // field 2, wire 0 => tag = (2<<3)|0 = 0x10
        let body = [0x10, 0x2A]; // value = 42
        assert_eq!(extract_app_id("Cloud.ClientCommitFileUpload#1", &body), 42);
        // For other jobs, field 1 is 0x08, so this body is empty of field 1.
        assert_eq!(extract_app_id("Cloud.GetFile#1", &body), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_queue_has_no_pending() {
        // Cannot cleanly assert on the shared queue if another test
        // populated it, but the call is safe to make.
        let _ = has_pending();
    }
}


===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\dispatch.rs =====
//! eMsg dispatch. Mirrors the C++ `SendJob` / `RecvJob` and
//! `SendServiceJob` / `RecvServiceJob` inside the anonymous namespace.

use prost::Message;

use crate::steam::net_packet as netpkt;
use crate::steam::proto::CMsgProtoBufHeader;
use crate::utils::cloud_redirect::host as cloud_redirect;
use crate::utils::support::fnv::fnv1a_hash;

use super::{
    access_token, cloud, family_sharing, legacy_key, licenses, manifest,
    manifest_probe, msg_name, onlinefix, ownershipticket,
    packet::{self, K_MSG_HDR_PROTO_FLAG},
    richpresence, userstats,
};

// ── Outcome of a dispatch ───────────────────────────────────────────

/// Result of dispatching an outgoing frame.
pub enum SendReplacement {
    /// Leave the packet untouched.
    None,
    /// Replace the body, keep the header.
    Body(Vec<u8>),
    /// Do not forward the frame; report success to the caller.
    Suppress,
}

/// Result of dispatching an incoming frame.
pub enum RecvReplacement {
    /// Leave the packet untouched.
    None,
    /// Replace the body, keep the header.
    Body(Vec<u8>),
    /// Replace the header, keep the body.
    Hdr(Vec<u8>),
    /// Replace both.
    Both { hdr: Vec<u8>, body: Vec<u8> },
}

// ── FNV-1a hashes of the service job names dispatched on 151/147 ────

const HASH_JOB_NOTIFY_RUNNING_APPS: u32 =
    fnv1a_hash("FamilyGroupsClient.NotifyRunningApps#1");
const HASH_JOB_GET_USER_STATS: u32 =
    fnv1a_hash("Player.GetUserStats#1");
const HASH_JOB_GET_MANIFEST_REQUEST_CODE: u32 =
    fnv1a_hash("ContentServerDirectory.GetManifestRequestCode#1");

// ── Service job dispatch (151 / 147) ────────────────────────────────

fn send_service_job(target: &str, body: &[u8], hdr: &[u8]) -> Option<SendReplacement> {
    LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!("Send target_job_name: {}", target);

    // Steam Cloud save redirection: hand every "Cloud.*" request to
    // CloudRedirect. If it answers, suppress the outbound frame (the
    // synthesized response is delivered from the RecvPkt hook).
    //
    // ExitSyncDone / ConflictResolution are notifications that must
    // reach Steam's internal cloud state machine untouched.
    //
    // Only swallow the request if we can actually deliver the answer.
    // Drain runs from the RecvPkt hook, which does nothing until the
    // packet layout is known - suppressing the send before then would
    // leave the job waiting forever on a reply that never comes.
    if target.starts_with("Cloud.") {
        if target == "Cloud.SignalAppExitSyncDone#1"
            || target == "Cloud.ClientConflictResolution#1"
        {
            return None;
        }
        if !netpkt::is_resolved() {
            return None;
        }
        if cloud::handle_send(target, body, hdr) {
            return Some(SendReplacement::Suppress);
        }
        return None;
    }

    match fnv1a_hash(target) {
        HASH_JOB_GET_USER_STATS => {
            userstats::handle_send_get_user_stats(body, hdr).map(SendReplacement::Body)
        }
        HASH_JOB_GET_MANIFEST_REQUEST_CODE => {
            manifest::handle_send(body, hdr);
            None
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn recv_service_job(target: &str, body: &[u8], hdr: &[u8]) -> RecvReplacement {
    LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!("Recv target_job_name: {}", target);

    match fnv1a_hash(target) {
        HASH_JOB_NOTIFY_RUNNING_APPS => family_sharing::clear_body(body),
        HASH_JOB_GET_USER_STATS => userstats::handle_recv_get_user_stats_response(hdr, body),
        HASH_JOB_GET_MANIFEST_REQUEST_CODE => {
            // Replies to our own originated requests are consumed here;
            // the normal handler would ignore them anyway, but this
            // keeps the two paths from having to reason about each
            // other.
            if manifest_probe::handle_recv(body, hdr) {
                return RecvReplacement::None;
            }
            manifest::handle_recv(body, hdr)
        }
        _ => RecvReplacement::None,
    }
}

// ── eMsg dispatch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub unsafe fn send_frame(frame: &[u8]) -> SendReplacement {
    let Some(p) = packet::unpack_raw(frame) else {
        return SendReplacement::None;
    };
    let st = super::state::state();
    st.need_replace_send = false;
    st.suppress_send = false;

    LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!(
        "Send eMsg {}({}) (cbBody={}, cbHdr={})",
        msg_name(p.e_msg), p.e_msg, p.body.len(), p.hdr.len(),
    );

    match p.e_msg {
        packet::K_EMSG_SERVICE_METHOD_CALL_FROM_CLIENT => {
            // Keep one real outbound 151 header as the template for
            // ManifestProbe-originated requests.
            manifest_probe::capture_context(
                std::ptr::null_mut(), std::ptr::null_mut(), Some(p.hdr),
            );
            if let Ok(hdr_msg) = CMsgProtoBufHeader::decode(p.hdr) {
                if let Some(target) = hdr_msg.target_job_name.as_deref() {
                    if let Some(rep) = send_service_job(target, p.body, p.hdr) {
                        return rep;
                    }
                }
            }
            SendReplacement::None
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_PICS_PRODUCT_INFO_REQUEST => {
            match access_token::handle_send(p.body) {
                Some(new_body) => SendReplacement::Body(new_body),
                None => SendReplacement::None,
            }
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_GAMES_PLAYED
        | packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_GAMES_PLAYED_WITH_DATA_BLOB => {
            richpresence::track_send_games_played(p.body, p.hdr);
            match onlinefix::handle_send(p.body, p.hdr) {
                Some(new_body) => SendReplacement::Body(new_body),
                None => SendReplacement::None,
            }
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_RICH_PRESENCE_UPLOAD => {
            richpresence::track_rp_send(p.body);
            SendReplacement::None
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_USER_STATS => {
            match userstats::handle_send_client_get_user_stats(p.body) {
                Some(new_body) => SendReplacement::Body(new_body),
                None => SendReplacement::None,
            }
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_STORE_USER_STATS2 => {
            let app_id = richpresence::playing_app_id();
            if app_id != 0 {
                cloud_redirect::notify_stats_stored(app_id);
            }
            SendReplacement::None
        }
        _ => SendReplacement::None,
    }
}

pub unsafe fn recv_frame(frame: &[u8]) -> RecvReplacement {
    let Some(p) = packet::unpack_raw(frame) else {
        return RecvReplacement::None;
    };
    let st = super::state::state();
    st.need_replace_body = false;
    st.need_replace_hdr = false;

    if p.e_msg == packet::K_EMSG_MULTI {
        LOG_NETPACKET_TRACE!("Received k_EMsgMulti, skipping dispatch");
        return RecvReplacement::None;
    }

    LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!(
        "Recv eMsg {}({}) (cbBody={}, cbHdr={})",
        msg_name(p.e_msg), p.e_msg, p.body.len(), p.hdr.len(),
    );

    match p.e_msg {
        packet::K_EMSG_SERVICE_METHOD_RESPONSE => {
            if let Ok(hdr_msg) = CMsgProtoBufHeader::decode(p.hdr) {
                if let Some(target) = hdr_msg.target_job_name.as_deref() {
                    return recv_service_job(target, p.body, p.hdr);
                }
            }
            RecvReplacement::None
        }
        // Disabled in the C++ with the note "migrated to IPC Layer
        // Hooks_IPC_ISteamUser::GetEncryptedAppTicketResponse". Ported
        // for reference in `super::eticket`; not called here.
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_USER_STATS_RESPONSE => {
            match userstats::handle_recv_client_get_user_stats_response(p.body) {
                Some(new_body) => RecvReplacement::Body(new_body),
                None => RecvReplacement::None,
            }
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_SHARED_LIBRARY_STOP_PLAYING => {
            family_sharing::clear_body(p.body)
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_PERSONA_STATE => {
            match richpresence::handle_recv(p.body, p.hdr) {
                Some(new_body) => RecvReplacement::Body(new_body),
                None => RecvReplacement::None,
            }
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_APP_OWNERSHIP_TICKET_RESPONSE => {
            match ownershipticket::handle_recv(p.body) {
                Some(new_body) => RecvReplacement::Body(new_body),
                None => RecvReplacement::None,
            }
        }
        packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_LICENSE_LIST => {
            licenses::handle_recv(p.body);
            RecvReplacement::None
        }
        _ => RecvReplacement::None,
    }
}

// Keep the flag constant visible.
#[allow(dead_code)]
const _: u32 = K_MSG_HDR_PROTO_FLAG;

    #[test]

    }

    }

    }
}


===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\eticket.rs =====
//! `Hooks_NetPacket_ETicket`. Incoming eMsg 5527
//! (`CMsgClientRequestEncryptedAppTicketResponse`).
//!
//! **Not wired.** The C++ has this dispatch case commented out with the
//! note "migrated to IPC Layer
//! `Hooks_IPC_ISteamUser::GetEncryptedAppTicketResponse`". The handler
//! is preserved here for reference so a future patch can re-enable it
//! by uncommenting one line in `dispatch.rs`; today it is not called
//! from anywhere.

use prost::Message;

use crate::steam::proto::{
    CMsgClientRequestEncryptedAppTicketResponse, EncryptedAppTicket,
};
use crate::utils::config::lua_config;
use crate::utils::tickets::app_ticket;

const K_ERESULT_OK: i32 = 1;

/// Serve a stored Encrypted App Ticket in place of the server's non-OK
/// response. Returns the new body when a replacement was made.
pub fn handle_recv(body: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut resp = CMsgClientRequestEncryptedAppTicketResponse::decode(body).ok()?;
    if resp.eresult.unwrap_or(2) == K_ERESULT_OK { return None; }
    let app_id = resp.app_id.unwrap_or(0);
    if !lua_config::has_depot(app_id, false) { return None; }

    let ticket = app_ticket::get_encrypted_ticket_from_credential_store(app_id);
    if ticket.is_empty() { return None; }

    let parsed = EncryptedAppTicket::decode(&*ticket).ok()?;
    resp.encrypted_app_ticket = Some(parsed);
    resp.eresult = Some(K_ERESULT_OK);

    let encoded = resp.encode_to_vec();
    if encoded.len() > super::state::K_MAX_BODY_SIZE {
        LOG_NETPACKET_WARN!(
            "ClientRequestEncryptedAppTicketResponse: modified message too large ({})",
            encoded.len(),
        );
        return None;
    }
    LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!(
        "ClientRequestEncryptedAppTicketResponse: served stored ticket for appid={} ({} bytes)",
        app_id, ticket.len(),
    );
    Some(encoded)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn malformed_body_returns_none() {
        assert!(handle_recv(&[0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF]).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn ok_response_is_passed_through() {
        // Build a minimal response with eresult = OK.
        use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientRequestEncryptedAppTicketResponse;
        let resp = CMsgClientRequestEncryptedAppTicketResponse {
            app_id: Some(730),
            eresult: Some(K_ERESULT_OK),
            encrypted_app_ticket: None,
        };
        let body = resp.encode_to_vec();
        assert!(handle_recv(&body).is_none());
    }
}

===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\legacy_key.rs =====
//! Legacy third-party CD key ("Updating product key").
//!
//! `k_EMsgClientGetLegacyGameKey` (730) is a non-proto STRUCT message,
//! so it never reaches the proto SendJob/RecvJob path (`unpack_raw`
//! bails on the missing proto flag). We catch the outbound request
//! straight off the send hook, answer it locally with a resolved key,
//! suppress the real send, and deliver the synthesized 785 response
//! from the RecvPkt hook — the same "answered locally" trick the Cloud
//! path uses.

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::ffi::c_void;

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use parking_lot::Mutex;

use crate::steam::net_packet as netpkt;
use crate::steam::structs::{CNetPacket, ExtendedMsgHdr, MsgClientGetLegacyGameKeyResponse};
use crate::steam::types::k_GIDNil;
use crate::utils::tickets::legacy_cd_key;

use super::state::K_MAX_PACKET_SIZE;

const K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_LEGACY_GAME_KEY: u32 =
    super::packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_LEGACY_GAME_KEY;
const K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_LEGACY_GAME_KEY_RESPONSE: u32 = 785;
const K_ERESULT_OK: i32 = 1;
const K_MAX_QUEUE_LEN: usize = 64;

static LEGACY_QUEUE: Lazy<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>> =
    Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));

/// Returns `true` when we answered the request locally; the caller must
/// then suppress the outbound frame.
pub fn handle_send(frame: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let hdr_size = std::mem::size_of::<ExtendedMsgHdr>();
    let body_size = std::mem::size_of::<MsgClientGetLegacyGameKeyResponse>();

    // Request body is a bare `u32 m_unAppId` at offset hdr_size.
    if frame.len() < hdr_size + 4 { return false; }

    // ExtendedMsgHdr field offsets (packed struct): m_ulSteamID is at
    // 24, m_JobIDSource at 15.
    let req_steamid = u64::from_le_bytes([
        frame[24], frame[25], frame[26], frame[27],
        frame[28], frame[29], frame[30], frame[31],
    ]);
    let req_job_source = u64::from_le_bytes([
        frame[15], frame[16], frame[17], frame[18],
        frame[19], frame[20], frame[21], frame[22],
    ]);

    let app_id = u32::from_le_bytes([
        frame[hdr_size], frame[hdr_size + 1],
        frame[hdr_size + 2], frame[hdr_size + 3],
    ]);
    let account_id = (req_steamid & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32;

    let Some(key) = legacy_cd_key::resolve(app_id, account_id) else {
        return false; // not a managed app — let Steam's real flow run
    };

    // Steam stores the legacy key as a NUL-terminated string; length
    // counts the terminator.
    let cch_key = (key.len() + 1) as u32;
    let total = hdr_size + body_size + cch_key as usize;
    if total > K_MAX_PACKET_SIZE {
        LOG_NETPACKET_WARN!(
            "LegacyKey: app={} response too large ({} bytes), passing through",
            app_id, total,
        );
        return false;
    }

    let mut pkt = vec![0u8; total];
    // Copy the whole request header, then override the three fields
    // that distinguish a response from a request.
    pkt[..hdr_size].copy_from_slice(&frame[..hdr_size]);
    // eMsg -> 785 (non-proto, flag stays clear)
    pkt[0..4].copy_from_slice(&K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_LEGACY_GAME_KEY_RESPONSE.to_le_bytes());
    // m_JobIDTarget = request's m_JobIDSource (offset 7..15)
    pkt[7..15].copy_from_slice(&req_job_source.to_le_bytes());
    // m_JobIDSource = k_GIDNil (offset 15..23)
    pkt[15..23].copy_from_slice(&k_GIDNil.to_le_bytes());

    // Response body: u32 m_unAppId, i32 m_eResult, u32 m_cchKey, then
    // the NUL-terminated key.
    pkt[hdr_size..hdr_size + 4].copy_from_slice(&app_id.to_le_bytes());
    pkt[hdr_size + 4..hdr_size + 8].copy_from_slice(&K_ERESULT_OK.to_le_bytes());
    pkt[hdr_size + 8..hdr_size + 12].copy_from_slice(&cch_key.to_le_bytes());
    let key_off = hdr_size + body_size;
    pkt[key_off..key_off + key.len()].copy_from_slice(key.as_bytes());
    // NUL terminator already zeroed by `vec![0u8; total]`.

    {
        let mut q = LEGACY_QUEUE.lock();
        if q.len() < K_MAX_QUEUE_LEN {
            q.push_back(pkt);
        }
    }
    LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!(
        "LegacyKey: app={} answered locally ({} bytes, key '{}')",
        app_id, total, key,
    );
    true
}

pub fn has_pending() -> bool {
    !LEGACY_QUEUE.lock().is_empty()
}

/// Deliver queued responses by borrowing the carrier packet for one
/// call to the original each. Same shape as `cloud::drain`.
///
/// # Safety
/// Caller must be inside the `RecvPkt` hook with a live `p_carrier`.
pub unsafe fn drain<F>(p_this: *mut c_void, p_carrier: *mut CNetPacket, invoke_original: F)
where
    F: Fn(*mut c_void, *mut CNetPacket) -> *mut c_void,
{
    loop {
        let mut pkt = {
            let mut q = LEGACY_QUEUE.lock();
            match q.pop_front() {
                Some(p) => p,
                None => return,
            }
        };

        let orig_data = netpkt::read_data(p_carrier as *mut u8);
        let orig_size = netpkt::read_size(p_carrier as *mut u8);

        let len = pkt.len();
        netpkt::write_data(p_carrier as *mut u8, pkt.as_mut_ptr());
        netpkt::write_size(p_carrier as *mut u8, len as u32);

        let _ = invoke_original(p_this, p_carrier);

        netpkt::write_data(p_carrier as *mut u8, orig_data);
        netpkt::write_size(p_carrier as *mut u8, orig_size);

        LOG_NETPACKET_DEBUG!("LegacyKey: delivered {}-byte response", len);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn short_frame_rejected() {
        // A frame shorter than ExtendedMsgHdr + u32 must be rejected.
        assert!(!handle_send(&[0u8; 8]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unmanaged_app_passes_through() {
        // Build a minimal ExtendedMsgHdr + appId frame. App id is 0,
        // which is not in the (empty) Lua config.
        let hdr_size = std::mem::size_of::<ExtendedMsgHdr>();
        let mut f = vec![0u8; hdr_size + 4];
        // eMsg (offset 0..4) = 730
        f[0..4].copy_from_slice(&730u32.to_le_bytes());
        // m_JobIDSource (offset 15..23) — arbitrary
        f[15..23].copy_from_slice(&0x1122334455667788u64.to_le_bytes());
        // m_ulSteamID (offset 24..32) — arbitrary
        f[24..32].copy_from_slice(&0x1100001000000042u64.to_le_bytes());
        // appId (offset hdr_size) = 730
        f[hdr_size..hdr_size + 4].copy_from_slice(&730u32.to_le_bytes());
        assert!(!handle_send(&f));
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_queue_has_no_pending() {
        let _ = has_pending();
    }
}

//! `Hooks_NetPacket_Licenses`. Incoming `CMsgClientLicenseList` (eMsg
//! 780). Read-only: the message is handed on untouched. Parses the
//! license list and hands it to `Hooks_Package::OnLicenseList`.

use prost::Message;

use crate::hook::package::{self, License};
use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientLicenseList;

pub fn handle_recv(body: &[u8]) {
    let msg = match CMsgClientLicenseList::decode(body) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(_) => {
            LOG_PACKAGE_WARN!("LicenseList: failed to parse CMsgClientLicenseList");
            return;
        }
    };

    let mut licenses = Vec::with_capacity(msg.licenses.len());
    for lic in &msg.licenses {
        let Some(package_id) = lic.package_id else { continue };
        licenses.push(License {
            package_id,
            access_token: lic.access_token.unwrap_or(0),
        });
    }

    LOG_PACKAGE_INFO!(
        "LicenseList: {} license(s), eresult={}",
        licenses.len(), msg.eresult.unwrap_or(0),
    );

    package::on_license_list(licenses);
    package::try_dump_owned_depots();
}

        msg.encode_to_vec()
    }

    #[test]
    fn malformed_body_does_not_panic() {
        handle_recv(&[0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_empty_list_is_ok() {
        let msg = CMsgClientLicenseList {
            eresult: Some(1),
            licenses: vec![],
        };
        handle_recv(&encode(&msg));
    }

                access_token: Some(0xCAFE_BABE),
                ..Default::default()
            }],
        };
        handle_recv(&encode(&msg));
    }
}


===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\manifest.rs =====
//! `Hooks_NetPacket_Manifest`. Outgoing and incoming
//! `ContentServerDirectory.GetManifestRequestCode#1`.
//!
//! On send, this reads the request, records the correlation for
//! passive capture, pre-seeds the manifest cache (for the exact gid
//! Steam is asking about), and launches a background HTTP fetch.
//!
//! On recv, this waits for the fetch (up to 12 s) and patches the
//! response in place. Passive capture of genuine Steam-issued codes
//! also runs here — this is what feeds `ManifestDonor`.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::mpsc;
use std::time::Duration;

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use prost::Message;

use crate::steam::proto::{
    CContentServerDirectoryGetManifestRequestCodeRequest as Req,
    CContentServerDirectoryGetManifestRequestCodeResponse as Resp,
    CMsgProtoBufHeader,
};
use crate::utils::config::{config, lua_config};
use crate::utils::steam_metadata::{manifest_cache, manifest_client, manifest_donor};

use super::dispatch::RecvReplacement;
use super::state::{K_MAX_BODY_SIZE, K_MAX_HDR_SIZE};

const K_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS: u64 = 12;
const K_MAX_SENT_TRACKED: usize = 4096;
const K_ERESULT_OK: i32 = 1;

struct SentReq {
    depot: u32,
    gid: u64,
}

struct State {
    /// jobid_source -> receiver that will yield the fetched code.
    code_futures: HashMap<u64, mpsc::Receiver<u64>>,
    /// Passive-capture map. Bounded so a reply that never arrives does
    /// not grow this without limit.
    sent_requests: HashMap<u64, SentReq>,
}

static MANIFEST_STATE: Lazy<Mutex<State>> = Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(State {
    code_futures: HashMap::new(),
    sent_requests: HashMap::new(),
}));

// ── Send ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Read the request, record the correlation, pre-seed the cache, and
/// launch the fetch. Does not modify the outgoing frame.
pub fn handle_send(body: &[u8], hdr: &[u8]) {
    let req = match Req::decode(body) {
        Ok(r) => r,
        Err(_) => {
            LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!("GetManifestRequestCode: failed to parse request");
            return;
        }
    };
    let Some(depot_id) = req.depot_id else { return; };
    let Some(manifest_gid) = req.manifest_id else { return; };
    let app_id = req.app_id.unwrap_or(0);

    let hdr_msg = CMsgProtoBufHeader::decode(hdr).ok();
    let job_id = hdr_msg.as_ref().and_then(|h| h.jobid_source);

    // Passive capture: remember every request so the recv handler can
    // harvest the real code Steam returns. Gated on [donate], where
    // captured codes are sent.
    if let Some(jid) = job_id {
        if config::get_donate_settings().enabled {
            let mut state = MANIFEST_STATE.lock();
            if state.sent_requests.len() < K_MAX_SENT_TRACKED {
                state.sent_requests.insert(jid, SentReq { depot: depot_id, gid: manifest_gid });
            }
        }
    }

    // Only Lua-declared depots get their code swapped.
    if !lua_config::has_depot(depot_id, false) { return; }

    // A depot can be both Lua-added and genuinely owned. There Steam is
    // about to receive a real, working code; replacing it with a
    // fetched one can only make things worse. `BuildDepotDependency`
    // records depot -> app; bridge through that.
    if let Some((seen_app, _)) = crate::hook::manifest::lookup_depot(depot_id) {
        if seen_app != 0 && lua_config::is_owned(seen_app) {
            LOG_MANIFEST_INFO!(
                "GetManifestRequestCode: depot={} belongs to owned app {}, \
                 leaving Steam's own code alone",
                depot_id, seen_app,
            );
            return;
        }
    }

    let Some(job_id) = job_id else {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!("GetManifestRequestCode: missing jobid_source in header");
        return;
    };

    LOG_MANIFEST_DEBUG!(
        "GetManifestRequestCode send: depot={} gid={} jobid={} app_id={}",
        depot_id, manifest_gid, job_id, app_id,
    );

    // Pre-seed the cache for the exact manifest Steam is asking about.
    // Detached; if the archive has it, Steam's own retry (~30 s) finds
    // the manifest on disk and skips the code path entirely. A miss
    // just falls through to the fetched-code attempt.
    //
    // Only a real user download bypasses the negative cache and
    // surfaces the "not ready" box. Scheduled/queued requests ride the
    // negative cache and stay silent.
    {
        let a = app_id;
        let d = depot_id;
        let g = manifest_gid;
        let active = crate::hook::steamui::active_download_count() > 0;
        let _ = crate::platform::thread::start_detached(move || {
            let (ok, not_archived) =
                manifest_cache::ensure_cached_ex(a, d, g, 0, active);
            if active && !ok && not_archived {
                crate::hook::manifest::report_missing_manifest(d, g);
            }
            0
        });
    }

    // Launch the fetch on a detached thread, hand its result back over
    // a channel.
    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
    {
        let mut state = MANIFEST_STATE.lock();
        state.code_futures.insert(job_id, rx);
    }
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let code = manifest_client::fetch_manifest_request_code(manifest_gid, app_id, depot_id)
            .unwrap_or(0);
        let _ = tx.send(code);
    });
}

// ── Recv ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub fn handle_recv(body: &[u8], hdr: &[u8]) -> RecvReplacement {
    let hdr_msg = match CMsgProtoBufHeader::decode(hdr) {
        Ok(h) => h,
        Err(_) => {
            LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!("GetManifestRequestCode recv: failed to decode header");
            return RecvReplacement::None;
        }
    };
    let Some(job_id) = hdr_msg.jobid_target else {
        return RecvReplacement::None;
    };

    // Passive capture: harvest the genuine code from this reply before
    // the injection path below can overwrite the body. Only real
    // successes for a request we tracked on send. The injected case
    // naturally filters out because Steam's own reply carries no valid
    // code.
    {
        let sent = MANIFEST_STATE.lock().sent_requests.remove(&job_id);
        if let Some(s) = sent {
            if hdr_msg.eresult.unwrap_or(0) == K_ERESULT_OK {
                if let Ok(resp) = Resp::decode(body) {
                    if let Some(code) = resp.manifest_request_code.filter(|c| *c != 0) {
                        LOG_MANIFEST_DEBUG!(
                            "GetManifestRequestCode recv: captured genuine code \
                             for depot={} gid={}",
                            s.depot, s.gid,
                        );
                        manifest_donor::submit_captured_code(s.depot, s.gid, code);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Injection path: only fires for Lua-declared, non-owned depots,
    // because handle_send only registered a receiver for those.
    let rx = {
        let mut state = MANIFEST_STATE.lock();
        state.code_futures.remove(&job_id)
    };
    let Some(rx) = rx else { return RecvReplacement::None; };

    let code = match rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(K_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS)) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => {
            LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
                "GetManifestRequestCode recv: HTTP timed out for jobid={}", job_id,
            );
            return RecvReplacement::None;
        }
    };
    if code == 0 {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
            "GetManifestRequestCode recv: HTTP returned 0 for jobid={}", job_id,
        );
        return RecvReplacement::None;
    }

    LOG_MANIFEST_DEBUG!(
        "GetManifestRequestCode recv: injecting code={} for jobid={}", code, job_id,
    );

    // Header: set eresult=OK.
    let mut new_hdr = hdr_msg;
    new_hdr.eresult = Some(K_ERESULT_OK);
    let new_hdr_bytes = new_hdr.encode_to_vec();
    if new_hdr_bytes.len() > K_MAX_HDR_SIZE {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
            "GetManifestRequestCode recv: modified header too large ({})",
            new_hdr_bytes.len(),
        );
        return RecvReplacement::None;
    }

    // Body: set manifest_request_code.
    let new_resp = Resp {
        manifest_request_code: Some(code),
    };
    let new_body = new_resp.encode_to_vec();
    if new_body.len() > K_MAX_BODY_SIZE {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
            "GetManifestRequestCode recv: modified body too large ({})",
            new_body.len(),
        );
        return RecvReplacement::None;
    }

    RecvReplacement::Both { hdr: new_hdr_bytes, body: new_body }
}

===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\manifest_probe.rs =====
//! `Hooks_NetPacket_ManifestProbe`. Originates
//! `ContentServerDirectory.GetManifestRequestCode#1` rather than
//! waiting for Steam to ask, and delivers the code that comes back.
//!
//! ## Origin vs response
//!
//! Everything else in this module reacts: it rewrites frames Steam is
//! already sending, or manufactures inbound ones. This is the only path
//! that initiates, which needs three things Steam normally supplies and
//! we have to borrow:
//!
//!   * the websocket object    - only visible inside the send hook
//!   * a valid header          - `steamid` / `session` must be right,
//!                               so a real outbound header is kept as a
//!                               template rather than built from parts
//!   * a jobid                 - taken from a high, distinctive range
//!                               so it can never collide with Steam's
//!                               own
//!
//! ## Correlation
//!
//! The reply is correlated by `jobid_target` == the `jobid_source` we
//! set. A per-jobid `mpsc::Sender<u64>` parked in the global map
//! carries the code to a [`request`] caller. The `std::future` the C++
//! returns from its `Request` becomes an `mpsc::Receiver<u64>` here,
//! since Rust has no standard future whose result can be waited on
//! with a timeout from synchronous code.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::sync::mpsc::{self, Sender};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use prost::Message;

use crate::steam::proto::{
    CContentServerDirectoryGetManifestRequestCodeRequest as Req,
    CContentServerDirectoryGetManifestRequestCodeResponse as Resp,
    CMsgProtoBufHeader,
};
use crate::steam::structs::MsgHdr;
use crate::steam::types::AppId_t;

use super::packet::K_MSG_HDR_PROTO_FLAG;
use super::state::{K_MAX_BODY_SIZE, K_MAX_HDR_SIZE};

/// The websocket send fn Steam uses for the connection. The signature
/// matches the `BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame` hook.
pub type SendFrameFn = unsafe extern "system" fn(
    *mut c_void, u32, *mut u8, u32,
) -> bool;

const K_BINARY_OPCODE: u32 = 0x02;
const K_EMSG_SERVICE_METHOD_CALL_FROM_CLIENT: u32 = 151;

/// Well clear of Steam's own job ids, which count up from small values.
const K_JOB_ID_BASE: u64 = 0x7E51_0000_0000_0000;

/// A disconnect between send and reply would otherwise leave a promise
/// nobody ever fulfils and a caller blocked on it forever. Swept on
/// each new request.
pub const K_PENDING_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

struct Pending {
    depot_id: u32,
    tx: Sender<u64>,
    sent_at: Instant,
}

struct ProbeState {
    /// Stored as `usize` so `ProbeState` is `Send` without an `unsafe
    /// impl`. `0` means null.
    p_websocket: usize,
    /// The trampoline address captured from the hook, stored as `usize`
    /// for the same reason. `0` means "not captured yet".
    send_frame: usize,
    hdr_template: Vec<u8>,
    next_job_id: u64,
    pending: HashMap<u64, Pending>,
}

static PROBE: Lazy<Mutex<ProbeState>> = Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(ProbeState {
    p_websocket: 0,
    send_frame: 0,
    hdr_template: Vec::new(),
    next_job_id: K_JOB_ID_BASE,
    pending: HashMap::new(),
}));

/// Capture the connection object, the trampoline address, and (first
/// time only) a real outbound header. Called from the send hook for
/// every binary frame, and from the 151 dispatch path with an actual
/// header. `None` means "leave the captured header alone"; the first
/// non-empty `hdr` wins.
pub fn capture_context(
    p_object: *mut c_void,
    send_fn: *mut c_void,
    hdr: Option<&[u8]>,
) {
    let mut s = PROBE.lock();
    if !p_object.is_null() {
        s.p_websocket = p_object as usize;
    }
    if !send_fn.is_null() {
        s.send_frame = send_fn as usize;
    }
    if s.hdr_template.is_empty() {
        if let Some(h) = hdr {
            if !h.is_empty() {
                s.hdr_template = h.to_vec();
            }
        }
    }
}

fn expire_stale(s: &mut ProbeState) {
    let now = Instant::now();
    let stale: Vec<u64> = s
        .pending
        .iter()
        .filter(|(_, p)| now.duration_since(p.sent_at) > K_PENDING_TIMEOUT)
        .map(|(k, _)| *k)
        .collect();
    for job_id in stale {
        if let Some(p) = s.pending.remove(&job_id) {
            LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
                "ManifestProbe: no reply for depot {} (jobid={}) after {}s",
                p.depot_id, job_id, K_PENDING_TIMEOUT.as_secs(),
            );
            let _ = p.tx.send(0);
        }
    }
}

/// Sends the request and hands back a receiver for the code. A receiver
/// that yields `0` means the request failed, was refused by Steam, or
/// timed out. Callers treat all three the same way.
pub fn request(app_id: AppId_t, depot_id: u32, manifest_gid: u64) -> mpsc::Receiver<u64> {
    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();

    // Every early exit sends 0 rather than dropping the sender, so a
    // caller waiting on the receiver is never left hanging on a request
    // that was never sent.
    let (hdr_template, ws, send, job_id) = {
        let mut s = PROBE.lock();
        expire_stale(&mut s);

        if s.p_websocket == 0 || s.send_frame == 0 || s.hdr_template.is_empty() {
            LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
                "ManifestProbe: no send context captured yet (websocket={}, \
                 sendFn={}, header={} bytes) - is Steam logged in?",
                s.p_websocket != 0,
                s.send_frame != 0,
                s.hdr_template.len(),
            );
            let _ = tx.send(0);
            return rx;
        }

        let job_id = s.next_job_id.wrapping_add(1);
        s.next_job_id = job_id;
        (s.hdr_template.clone(), s.p_websocket, s.send_frame, job_id)
    };

    // Modify the captured header template: set target_job_name, set
    // jobid_source, clear jobid_target.
    let mut hdr = match CMsgProtoBufHeader::decode(&*hdr_template) {
        Ok(h) => h,
        Err(_) => {
            LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!("ManifestProbe: header template failed to parse");
            let _ = tx.send(0);
            return rx;
        }
    };
    hdr.target_job_name = Some("ContentServerDirectory.GetManifestRequestCode#1".to_string());
    hdr.jobid_source = Some(job_id);
    hdr.jobid_target = None;

    let req = Req {
        app_id: Some(app_id),
        depot_id: Some(depot_id),
        manifest_id: Some(manifest_gid),
        ..Default::default()
    };

    let hdr_bytes = hdr.encode_to_vec();
    let body_bytes = req.encode_to_vec();
    if hdr_bytes.len() > K_MAX_HDR_SIZE || body_bytes.len() > K_MAX_BODY_SIZE {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
            "ManifestProbe: frame too large (hdr={}, body={})",
            hdr_bytes.len(), body_bytes.len(),
        );
        let _ = tx.send(0);
        return rx;
    }

    let frame_size = std::mem::size_of::<MsgHdr>() + hdr_bytes.len() + body_bytes.len();
    let mut frame = vec![0u8; frame_size];
    let raw_emsg = K_EMSG_SERVICE_METHOD_CALL_FROM_CLIENT | K_MSG_HDR_PROTO_FLAG;
    frame[0..4].copy_from_slice(&raw_emsg.to_le_bytes());
    frame[4..8].copy_from_slice(&(hdr_bytes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    frame[8..8 + hdr_bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(&hdr_bytes);
    frame[8 + hdr_bytes.len()..].copy_from_slice(&body_bytes);

    // Register the pending entry before sending: the reply can arrive on
    // another thread the instant the frame goes out, and it must find
    // the entry already there.
    {
        let mut s = PROBE.lock();
        s.pending.insert(job_id, Pending {
            depot_id,
            tx: tx.clone(),
            sent_at: Instant::now(),
        });
    }

    LOG_MANIFEST_INFO!(
        "ManifestProbe send: app={} depot={} gid={} jobid={} ({} bytes)",
        app_id, depot_id, manifest_gid, job_id, frame.len(),
    );

    let send_fn: SendFrameFn = unsafe { std::mem::transmute(send) };
    let ws_ptr = ws as *mut c_void;
    let sent = unsafe {
        send_fn(ws_ptr, K_BINARY_OPCODE, frame.as_mut_ptr(), frame.len() as u32)
    };
    if !sent {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!("ManifestProbe: send returned false for jobid={}", job_id);
        let mut s = PROBE.lock();
        if let Some(p) = s.pending.remove(&job_id) {
            let _ = p.tx.send(0);
        }
    }

    rx
}

/// Returns `true` when the reply belonged to us; the normal Manifest
/// handler should then skip it.
pub fn handle_recv(body: &[u8], hdr: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let hdr_msg = match CMsgProtoBufHeader::decode(hdr) {
        Ok(h) => h,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    let Some(job_id) = hdr_msg.jobid_target else { return false; };
    if job_id < K_JOB_ID_BASE { return false; }

    let (depot_id, tx) = {
        let mut s = PROBE.lock();
        match s.pending.remove(&job_id) {
            None => return false,
            Some(p) => (p.depot_id, p.tx),
        }
    };

    let code = Resp::decode(body)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|r| r.manifest_request_code)
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let eresult = hdr_msg.eresult.unwrap_or(0);

    if code != 0 {
        LOG_MANIFEST_INFO!(
            "ManifestProbe recv: depot={} -> code={} (eresult={})",
            depot_id, code, eresult,
        );
    } else {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
            "ManifestProbe recv: depot={} -> NO CODE (eresult={})",
            depot_id, eresult,
        );
    }
    let _ = tx.send(code);
    true
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn handle_recv_malformed_header_returns_false() {
        assert!(!handle_recv(&[], &[0xFF, 0xFF]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn handle_recv_header_without_jobid_target_returns_false() {
        let hdr = CMsgProtoBufHeader::default();
        let hdr_bytes = hdr.encode_to_vec();
        assert!(!handle_recv(&[], &hdr_bytes));
    }

    #[test]
    fn handle_recv_low_jobid_returns_false() {
        // A header with a jobid_target well below K_JOB_ID_BASE must not
        // match any pending entry.
        let mut hdr = CMsgProtoBufHeader::default();
        hdr.jobid_target = Some(0x1234);
        let hdr_bytes = hdr.encode_to_vec();
        assert!(!handle_recv(&[], &hdr_bytes));
    }

    #[test]
    fn job_id_base_is_high() {
        // Sanity: K_JOB_ID_BASE must be well outside the range Steam
        // uses for its own job ids.
        assert!(K_JOB_ID_BASE > 0x7E00_0000_0000_0000);
    }
}

//! `Hooks_NetPacket.cpp`. Hooks `BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame` (outgoing) and
//! `RecvPkt` (incoming) and dispatches every packet by `EMsg`.

use std::ffi::{c_void, CStr};

use crate::steam::net_packet as netpkt;
use crate::steam::structs::{CNetPacket, ExtendedMsgHdr, MsgHdr};
use crate::{hook_fn, install_hook_c, resolve_c, resolve_fn, resolve_ready, uninstall_hook};

pub mod state;
pub mod packet;
pub mod dispatch;

pub mod access_token;
pub mod family_sharing;
pub mod licenses;
pub mod onlinefix;
pub mod richpresence;
pub mod userstats;

pub mod eticket;
pub mod ownershipticket;
pub mod manifest_probe;

pub mod manifest;
pub mod cloud;
pub mod legacy_key;

pub use dispatch::{RecvReplacement, SendReplacement};

// ── Resolve ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

resolve_fn! {
    fn PchMsgNameFromEMsg(e_msg: u32) -> *const i8
}

/// Human-readable name for an `EMsg`, or `"?"` when the resolver has not
/// fired or the lookup fails. The returned pointer is to a static string
/// owned by steamclient, so the borrow is effectively `'static`.
pub fn msg_name(e_msg: u32) -> &'static str {
    if !resolve_ready!(PchMsgNameFromEMsg) { return "?"; }
    let p = unsafe { o_PchMsgNameFromEMsg(e_msg) };
    if p.is_null() { return "?"; }
    let s = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(p) };
    match s.to_str() {
        Ok(s) => unsafe { std::mem::transmute::<&str, &'static str>(s) },
        Err(_) => "?",
    }
}

// ── Top-level hooks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

hook_fn! {
    fn BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame(
        p_object: *mut c_void,
        op_code: u32,
        pub_data: *mut u8,
        cub_data: u32,
    ) -> bool {
        const K_BINARY: u32 = 0x02; // k_eWebSocketOpCode_Binary
        if op_code != K_BINARY {
            return o_BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame(p_object, op_code, pub_data, cub_data);
        }

        let size = cub_data as usize;
        if pub_data.is_null() || size < std::mem::size_of::<MsgHdr>() {
            return o_BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame(p_object, op_code, pub_data, cub_data);
        }

        // Capture the connection object and the trampoline address for
        // ManifestProbe. Called on every binary frame so a reconnect
        // updates the captured values.
        let send_fn = unsafe { O_B_BUILD_AND_ASYNC_SEND_FRAME.load() };
        manifest_probe::capture_context(p_object, send_fn, None);

        let frame: Vec<u8> = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(pub_data, size) }.to_vec();

        // Legacy CD-key request (EMsg 730) is a non-proto struct message
        // that `unpack_raw` skips. Intercept it here: if we can answer
        // locally, suppress the real send; the 785 response is delivered
        // from the RecvPkt hook. Deliberately gated on layout resolution
        // - the drain is inert until then, so a locally-answered request
        // before that would leave the caller waiting on a reply that
        // never arrives.
        if size >= std::mem::size_of::<ExtendedMsgHdr>() && netpkt::is_resolved() {
            let raw = u32::from_le_bytes([frame[0], frame[1], frame[2], frame[3]]);
            if raw & packet::K_MSG_HDR_PROTO_FLAG == 0
                && raw == packet::K_EMSG_CLIENT_GET_LEGACY_GAME_KEY
                && legacy_key::handle_send(&frame)
            {
                return true; // answered locally; report success so Steam treats it as sent
            }
        }

        let rep = unsafe { dispatch::send_frame(&frame) };

        match rep {
            SendReplacement::None => {
                o_BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame(p_object, op_code, pub_data, cub_data)
            }
            SendReplacement::Suppress => {
                // Report success so Steam treats the frame as sent, but
                // do not forward it.
                true
            }
            SendReplacement::Body(new_body) => {
                let orig_hdr_len = u32::from_le_bytes([
                    frame[4], frame[5], frame[6], frame[7],
                ]) as usize;
                let body_start = std::mem::size_of::<MsgHdr>() + orig_hdr_len;
                if body_start > frame.len() {
                    return o_BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame(p_object, op_code, pub_data, cub_data);
                }
                let new_size = body_start + new_body.len();
                let mut out = vec![0u8; new_size];
                out[..body_start].copy_from_slice(&frame[..body_start]);
                out[body_start..].copy_from_slice(&new_body);
                o_BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame(
                    p_object, op_code, out.as_mut_ptr(), new_size as u32,
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

hook_fn! {
    fn RecvPkt(p_this: *mut c_void, p_packet: *mut CNetPacket) -> *mut c_void {
        if p_packet.is_null() {
            return o_RecvPkt(p_this, p_packet);
        }

        let resolved = unsafe {
            netpkt::is_resolved() || packet::try_resolve_layout(p_packet)
        };
        if !resolved {
            return o_RecvPkt(p_this, p_packet);
        }

        // Delivery order matches the C++: resolve layout, TryInject,
        // drain Cloud, drain LegacyKey, then dispatch. Each of the three
        // swaps the carrier's data pointer for the duration of one call
        // to the original, then restores.
        if richpresence::is_inject_pending() {
            unsafe {
                richpresence::try_inject(p_this, p_packet, |t, p| o_RecvPkt(t, p));
            }
        }
        if cloud::has_pending() {
            unsafe {
                cloud::drain(p_this, p_packet, |t, p| o_RecvPkt(t, p));
            }
        }
        if legacy_key::has_pending() {
            unsafe {
                legacy_key::drain(p_this, p_packet, |t, p| o_RecvPkt(t, p));
            }
        }

        let data_ptr = unsafe { netpkt::read_data(p_packet as *mut u8) };
        let size = unsafe { netpkt::read_size(p_packet as *mut u8) } as usize;
        if data_ptr.is_null() || size < std::mem::size_of::<MsgHdr>() {
            return o_RecvPkt(p_this, p_packet);
        }
        let frame: Vec<u8> = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(data_ptr, size) }.to_vec();

        let rep = unsafe { dispatch::recv_frame(&frame) };

        match rep {
            RecvReplacement::None => o_RecvPkt(p_this, p_packet),
            RecvReplacement::Body(new_body) => {
                let _ = unsafe {
                    packet::replace_recv_packet(p_packet, &frame, None, Some(&new_body))
                };
                o_RecvPkt(p_this, p_packet)
            }
            RecvReplacement::Hdr(new_hdr) => {
                let _ = unsafe {
                    packet::replace_recv_packet(p_packet, &frame, Some(&new_hdr), None)
                };
                o_RecvPkt(p_this, p_packet)
            }
            RecvReplacement::Both { hdr, body } => {
                let _ = unsafe {
                    packet::replace_recv_packet(p_packet, &frame, Some(&hdr), Some(&body))
                };
                o_RecvPkt(p_this, p_packet)
            }
        }
    }
}

// ── Public API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub fn install() -> bool {
    resolve_c!(PchMsgNameFromEMsg);

    let ok1 = install_hook_c!(BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame);
    let ok2 = install_hook_c!(RecvPkt);
    ok1 && ok2
}

pub fn uninstall() -> bool {
    let ok1 = uninstall_hook!(BBuildAndAsyncSendFrame);
    let ok2 = uninstall_hook!(RecvPkt);
    ok1 && ok2
}

/// Ask Steam for a manifest request code, as this account. Blocks the
/// caller until the reply arrives or the pending-entry timeout fires.
pub fn request_manifest_code(app_id: u32, depot_id: u32, gid: u64) -> u64 {
    let rx = manifest_probe::request(app_id, depot_id, gid);
    rx.recv_timeout(manifest_probe::K_PENDING_TIMEOUT).unwrap_or(0)
}

/// Manual test convenience: resolve a depot via `LookupDepot` and probe.
/// Fire-and-forget; the reply handler logs the outcome. Detached so the
/// caller is not blocked on a network round-trip.
pub fn probe_manifest(depot_id: u32) -> bool {
    let Some((app_id, gid)) = crate::hook::manifest::lookup_depot(depot_id) else {
        LOG_MANIFEST_WARN!(
            "ManifestProbe: depot {} not seen yet - it only becomes known once its \
             app is installed or updated in this session",
            depot_id,
        );
        return false;
    };
    let _ = crate::platform::thread::start_detached(move || {
        let rx = manifest_probe::request(app_id, depot_id, gid);
        let _ = rx.recv_timeout(manifest_probe::K_PENDING_TIMEOUT);
        0
    });
    true
}

        assert_eq!(msg_name(0), "?");
    }
}


===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\onlinefix.rs =====
//! `Hooks_NetPacket_OnlineFix`. Outgoing `CMsgClientGamesPlayed` (eMsg
//! 742 / 5410). When a game launched with `-onlinefix` reports appid
//! 480, replace `game_extra_info` with the real game's localized name so
//! friends see the correct title.

use prost::Message;

use crate::dllmain::K_ONLINE_FIX_APPID;
use crate::hook::misc as hooks_misc;
use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientGamesPlayed;

pub fn handle_send(body: &[u8], _hdr: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut msg = match CMsgClientGamesPlayed::decode(body) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(_) => {
            LOG_ONLINEFIX_WARN!("OnlineFix: failed to parse CMsgClientGamesPlayed");
            return None;
        }
    };

    let mut patched = false;
    for game in msg.games_played.iter_mut() {
        let appid = (game.game_id.unwrap_or(0) & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32;
        if appid == K_ONLINE_FIX_APPID {
            let real_app_id = hooks_misc::resolve_app_id();
            if real_app_id != 0 && real_app_id != K_ONLINE_FIX_APPID {
                let name = hooks_misc::get_game_name_by_app_id(real_app_id);
                if !name.is_empty() {
                    game.game_extra_info = Some(name.clone());
                    patched = true;
                    LOG_ONLINEFIX_INFO!(
                        "OnlineFix: 480 -> name '{}' (real appid {})",
                        name, real_app_id,
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if !patched { return None; }
    let encoded = msg.encode_to_vec();
    if encoded.len() > super::state::K_MAX_BODY_SIZE {
        LOG_ONLINEFIX_WARN!("OnlineFix: encoded size {} exceeds buffer", encoded.len());
        return None;
    }
    Some(encoded)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientGamesPlayed;
    use crate::steam::proto::c_msg_client_games_played::GamePlayed;

    fn encode(msg: &CMsgClientGamesPlayed) -> Vec<u8> {
        msg.encode_to_vec()
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_480_game_id_not_patched() {
        let msg = CMsgClientGamesPlayed {
            games_played: vec![GamePlayed {
                game_id: Some(730),
                ..Default::default()
            }],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        assert!(handle_send(&encode(&msg), &[]).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn malformed_body_returns_none() {
        assert!(handle_send(&[0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF], &[]).is_none());
    }
}


===== FILE: src\hook\netpacket\ownershipticket.rs =====
//! `Hooks_NetPacket_OwnershipTicket`. Incoming eMsg 858
//! (`CMsgClientGetAppOwnershipTicketResponse`).
//!
//! Some Denuvo titles verify ownership via this network message instead
//! of the IPC `GetAppOwnershipTicketExtendedData` path, so the IPC
//! ownership spoof never engages and the real (non-owning) account
//! leaks through as error 88500012. This handler supplies a
//! credential-store or freshly-minted ticket when Steam returns a
//! non-OK response.

use prost::Message;

use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientGetAppOwnershipTicketResponse;
use crate::utils::config::lua_config;
use crate::utils::tickets::{app_ticket, eticket_client};

const K_ERESULT_OK: i32 = 1;

pub fn handle_recv(body: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut resp = CMsgClientGetAppOwnershipTicketResponse::decode(body).ok()?;

    // Steam already returned a valid ticket (account owns it) - leave it.
    if resp.eresult.unwrap_or(2) == K_ERESULT_OK { return None; }

    let app_id = resp.app_id.unwrap_or(0);
    if !lua_config::has_depot(app_id, false) { return None; }

    let orig_eresult = resp.eresult.unwrap_or(2);

    // Prefer the credential-store ticket when it is already valid: that
    // ensures GetAppOwnershipTicketExtendedData and the 858 response
    // hand Denuvo the identical bytes. Serving a different
    // (backend-minted) ticket here caused a cross-check mismatch even
    // when the SteamID was the same account. Only mint from the backend
    // when the credential store has no valid ticket.
    let stored = app_ticket::get_app_ownership_ticket_from_credential_store(app_id);
    let existing_steam_id = app_ticket::extract_steam_id_from_ticket_bytes(&stored);

    let ticket_bytes = if existing_steam_id != 0 {
        stored
    } else {
        match eticket_client::fetch_ownership_ticket(app_id, &[], 0) {
            Some(t) => t,
            None => {
                LOG_NETPACKET_WARN!(
                    "OwnershipTicketResponse[858]: appid={} eresult={} but no owner ticket available",
                    app_id, orig_eresult,
                );
                return None;
            }
        }
    };

    let ticket_len = ticket_bytes.len();
    resp.ticket = Some(ticket_bytes);
    resp.eresult = Some(K_ERESULT_OK);

    let encoded = resp.encode_to_vec();
    if encoded.len() > super::state::K_MAX_BODY_SIZE {
        LOG_NETPACKET_WARN!(
            "OwnershipTicketResponse[858]: modified message too large ({})",
            encoded.len(),
        );
        return None;
    }
    LOG_NETPACKET_INFO!(
        "OwnershipTicketResponse[858]: spoofed appid={} ticket_bytes={} (orig eresult={} -> OK)",
        app_id, ticket_len, orig_eresult,
    );
    Some(encoded)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn malformed_body_returns_none() {
        assert!(handle_recv(&[0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF]).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn ok_response_is_passed_through() {
        use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientGetAppOwnershipTicketResponse;
        let resp = CMsgClientGetAppOwnershipTicketResponse {
            eresult: Some(K_ERESULT_OK),
            app_id: Some(730),
            ticket: None,
        };
        let body = resp.encode_to_vec();
        assert!(handle_recv(&body).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_owned_app_is_passed_through() {
        // eresult != OK, but appid is not in the (empty) Lua config.
        use crate::steam::proto::CMsgClientGetAppOwnershipTicketResponse;
        let resp = CMsgClientGetAppOwnershipTicketResponse {
            eresult: Some(15), // AccessDenied
            app_id: Some(0xDEAD_BEEF),
            ticket: None,
        };
        let body = resp.encode_to_vec();
        assert!(handle_recv(&body).is_none());
    }
}
