===== FILE: src\main.rs =====
//! Standalone CLI entry point.
//!
//! Same library as the injected DLL, but runs as a normal process. Used
//! for developer tooling: parse Lua files, parse TOML configs, exercise
//! hashes, and drive the same `bst://` URI handler `rundll32` would.
//!
//! None of the subcommands require injection. They exercise the layers
//! that do not need a live Steam pipe. `init` and `parse-toml` are the
//! two that touch the config loader; both are the same code paths the
//! DLL uses, so a config that loads cleanly here loads cleanly there.

#![allow(non_snake_case)]

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use RustyTools::bridge;
use RustyTools::platform::hash;
use RustyTools::utils::config::{config, lua_config};
use RustyTools::utils::support::fnv1a_hash;
use RustyTools::utils::tokeer::bridge as tokeer_bridge;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let cmd = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");

    match cmd {
        ""                       => cmd_bare_init(),
        "version"                => cmd_version(),
        "init"                   => cmd_init(&args[1..]),
        "parse-lua"              => cmd_parse_lua(&args[1..]),
        "parse-toml"             => cmd_parse_toml(&args[1..]),
        "sha256"                 => cmd_sha256(&args[1..]),
        "fnv1a"                  => cmd_fnv1a(&args[1..]),
        "handle-uri"             => cmd_handle_uri(&args[1..]),
        "help" | "-h" | "--help" => { print_help(); ExitCode::SUCCESS }
        other => {
            eprintln!("ost-cli: unknown subcommand '{other}'");
            eprintln!();
            print_help();
            ExitCode::from(2)
        }
    }
}

fn cmd_bare_init() -> ExitCode {
    match RustyTools::init() {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("ost-cli: init failed: {e}");
            ExitCode::from(1)
        }
    }
}

fn cmd_version() -> ExitCode {
    println!("{}", RustyTools::VERSION);
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_init(rest: &[String]) -> ExitCode {
    let mut config_path: Option<&str> = None;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < rest.len() {
        match rest[i].as_str() {
            "--config" | "-c" => {
                i += 1;
                let Some(p) = rest.get(i) else {
                    eprintln!("ost-cli init: --config requires a path");
                    return ExitCode::from(2);
                };
                config_path = Some(p.as_str());
            }
            other => {
                eprintln!("ost-cli init: unexpected argument '{other}'");
                return ExitCode::from(2);
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }

    let path = config_path.unwrap_or("rustytools.toml");
    println!("Loading config: {path}");
    let result = config::load(path);
    print_config_summary(&result);
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_parse_lua(rest: &[String]) -> ExitCode {
    let Some(path) = rest.first() else {
        eprintln!("ost-cli parse-lua: missing <PATH>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let p = Path::new(path);
    if p.is_dir() {
        println!("Parsing Lua directory: {path}");
        lua_config::parse_directory(path);
    } else if p.is_file() {
        println!("Parsing Lua file: {path}");
        lua_config::parse_file(path);
    } else {
        eprintln!("ost-cli parse-lua: {path} is not a file or directory");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    print_lua_summary();
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_parse_toml(rest: &[String]) -> ExitCode {
    let Some(path) = rest.first() else {
        eprintln!("ost-cli parse-toml: missing <PATH>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    println!("Parsing TOML config: {path}");
    let result = config::load(path);
    print_config_summary(&result);
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_sha256(rest: &[String]) -> ExitCode {
    let Some(path) = rest.first() else {
        eprintln!("ost-cli sha256: missing <PATH>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let h = hash::sha256_of_file(Path::new(path));
    if h.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("ost-cli sha256: cannot read {path}");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    }
    println!("{h}");
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_fnv1a(rest: &[String]) -> ExitCode {
    let Some(s) = rest.first() else {
        eprintln!("ost-cli fnv1a: missing <STRING>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let h = fnv1a_hash(s);
    println!("0x{h:08X}  ({h})");
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_handle_uri(rest: &[String]) -> ExitCode {
    let Some(url) = rest.first() else {
        eprintln!("ost-cli handle-uri: missing <URL>");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    // Same entry point as the exported TokeerUri. On Windows, error
    // paths pop a modal MessageBox — the CLI does not suppress that.
    // On success the redemption completes normally.
    tokeer_bridge::handle_uri(url);
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn print_config_summary(result: &config::LoadResult) {
    println!("  applied:           {}", result.applied);
    println!("  lua_paths_changed: {}", result.lua_paths_changed);
    println!("  log.level:         {}", config::get_log_level().as_str());
    println!("  lua.paths:         {} entr(ies)", config::get_lua_paths().len());
    println!("  stats.enable_api:  {}", config::get_stats_enable_api());
    println!("  update.enabled:    {}", config::get_update_enabled());
    let t = config::get_manifest_timeouts();
    println!(
        "  manifest timeouts: resolve={} connect={} send={} recv={}",
        t.resolve, t.connect, t.send, t.recv
    );
    let c = config::get_cloud_settings();
    println!("  cloud.enabled:     {} (library='{}')", c.enabled, c.library);
    println!("  manifest provider: {}", bridge::manifest_active_provider_name());
}

fn print_lua_summary() {
    let depots = lua_config::get_all_depot_ids();
    let with_keys = depots
        .iter()
        .filter(|id| !lua_config::get_decryption_key(**id).is_empty())
        .count();
    let with_tokens = depots
        .iter()
        .filter(|id| lua_config::get_access_token(**id) != 0)
        .count();
    println!("  depot(s) registered:     {}", depots.len());
    println!("  depot(s) with AES key:   {with_keys}");
    println!("  appid(s) with token:     {with_tokens}");
    println!("  fetch_manifest_code:     {}", lua_config::has_manifest_code_func());
    println!("  fetch_manifest_code_ex:  {}", lua_config::has_manifest_code_func_ex());
    println!(
        "  eticket url configured:  {}",
        !lua_config::get_eticket_url().is_empty()
    );
}

fn print_help() {
    println!(
        "\
ost-cli - rusty_tools CLI

USAGE:
    ost-cli <SUBCOMMAND>

SUBCOMMANDS:
    (none)                Initialize the runtime and exit cleanly.
    version               Print the library version.
    init [--config PATH]  Load a TOML config file (default:
                          rustytools.toml) and print the resulting
                          settings.
    parse-lua PATH        Parse a Lua file or directory and print the
                          resulting depot / token / override state.
    parse-toml PATH       Parse a TOML config file and print the settings
                          the loader would apply.
    sha256 PATH           Print the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of a file.
    fnv1a STRING          Print the FNV-1a 32-bit hash of a string (the
                          pattern-loader key format).
    handle-uri URL        Parse and dispatch a bst:// URL exactly as the
                          rundll32 TokeerUri entry point would. On
                          Windows, error paths pop a modal MessageBox.
    help, -h, --help      Print this help.
"
    );
}


===== FILE: src\pipe\denuvo_auth.rs =====
//! Per-process Denuvo detection + authorization state. Source:
//! `Pipe/Features/DenuvoAuth/DenuvoAuth.cpp`.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use parking_lot::Mutex;

use crate::pipe::pipe_types::{make_pipe_key, PipeContext, PipeKey, ProcessKey};
use crate::pipe::protection_scan;
use crate::platform::steam_credential_store;
use crate::steam::enums::{EAccountType, EUniverse};
use crate::steam::structs::{CPipeClient, CSteamID};
use crate::steam::types::AppId_t;
use crate::utils::config::lua_config;
use crate::utils::tickets::app_ticket;

const K_END_DENUVO_VERIFICATION_HANDSHAKE: u32 = 2;

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Stage {
    None,
    Authorizing,
    EndAuthorization,
}

fn stage_str(s: Stage) -> &'static str {
    match s {
        Stage::None => "None",
        Stage::Authorizing => "Authorizing",
        Stage::EndAuthorization => "EndAuthorization",
    }
}

fn parse_universe(name: &str) -> Option<EUniverse> {
    if name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Public") { return Some(EUniverse::Public); }
    if name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Beta") { return Some(EUniverse::Beta); }
    if name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Internal") { return Some(EUniverse::Internal); }
    if name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Dev") { return Some(EUniverse::Dev); }
    None
}

fn get_current_steam_id_for_denuvo_auth() -> Option<u64> {
    let (account_id, universe_name) = match steam_credential_store::get_active_user() {
        Ok(pair) => pair,
        Err(status) => {
            LOG_PIPE_WARN!(
                "DenuvoAuth: active Steam user unavailable ({})", status.as_str(),
            );
            return None;
        }
    };
    let universe = match parse_universe(&universe_name) {
        Some(u) => u,
        None => {
            LOG_PIPE_WARN!("DenuvoAuth: active Steam user has unsupported universe");
            return None;
        }
    };
    let mut id = CSteamID::default();
    id.set(account_id, universe, EAccountType::Individual);
    Some(id.convert_to_u64())
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct ProcessAuth {
    scanned: bool,
    denuvo: bool,
    stage: Stage,
    pid: u32,
    handshake_count: u32,
    authorization_pipe: Option<PipeKey>,
    authorized_app_id: AppId_t,
}

impl ProcessAuth {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self { stage: Stage::None, ..Default::default() }
    }

    fn debug_string(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "denuvo={} stage={} handshakeCount={} auth_appid={} pid={}",
            self.denuvo,
            stage_str(self.stage),
            self.handshake_count,
            self.authorized_app_id,
            self.pid,
        )
    }

    fn on_handshake(&mut self, ctx: &PipeContext, pipe_key: PipeKey) {
        self.handshake_count += 1;

        if !self.denuvo {
            self.stage = Stage::None;
            return;
        }

        if self.authorization_pipe.is_none() {
            self.authorization_pipe = Some(pipe_key);
            self.authorized_app_id = ctx.app_id;
            self.pid = ctx.process.pid;
            self.stage = Stage::Authorizing;
            LOG_PIPE_INFO!("DenuvoAuth: authorization pipe selected {}", self.debug_string());
        }

        if self.stage == Stage::Authorizing
            && self.handshake_count >= K_END_DENUVO_VERIFICATION_HANDSHAKE
        {
            self.stage = Stage::EndAuthorization;
            LOG_PIPE_INFO!("DenuvoAuth: authorization window ended {}", self.debug_string());
            if lua_config::is_owned(self.authorized_app_id) {
                self.write_steam_id_on_end_authorization();
            }
        }
    }

    fn can_use_authorized_identity(&self, key: PipeKey) -> bool {
        self.denuvo
            && self.stage == Stage::Authorizing
            && self.authorization_pipe == Some(key)
    }

    fn write_steam_id_on_end_authorization(&self) {
        if self.authorized_app_id == 0 {
            LOG_PIPE_WARN!(
                "DenuvoAuth: end authorization skipped SteamID persist without auth app",
            );
            return;
        }
        let Some(steam_id) = get_current_steam_id_for_denuvo_auth() else { return; };
        if steam_id == 0 { return; }

        if app_ticket::write_steam_id(self.authorized_app_id, steam_id) {
            LOG_PIPE_INFO!(
                "DenuvoAuth: persisted end-authorization SteamID auth_appid={} steamid={}",
                self.authorized_app_id, steam_id,
            );
        } else {
            LOG_PIPE_WARN!(
                "DenuvoAuth: failed to persist end-authorization SteamID auth_appid={} steamid={}",
                self.authorized_app_id, steam_id,
            );
        }
    }
}

impl Default for Stage {
    fn default() -> Self { Stage::None }
}

static G_PROCESS_AUTH: Lazy<Mutex<HashMap<ProcessKey, ProcessAuth>>> =
    Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));

static G_PIPE_PROCESS: Lazy<Mutex<HashMap<PipeKey, ProcessKey>>> =
    Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));

fn find_auth_for_pipe(pipe_key: PipeKey) -> Option<ProcessAuth> {
    let process_key = {
        let pipes = G_PIPE_PROCESS.lock();
        *pipes.get(&pipe_key)?
    };
    let auths = G_PROCESS_AUTH.lock();
    auths.get(&process_key).map(|_| ())?;
    // Return a "clone" of the interesting bits. We cannot borrow the
    // HashMap across locks, so recompute the query here. The clone cost
    // is tiny (a small struct with a bool / Option / u32 / u32 / u32).
    let a = auths.get(&process_key).unwrap();
    Some(ProcessAuth {
        scanned: a.scanned,
        denuvo: a.denuvo,
        stage: a.stage,
        pid: a.pid,
        handshake_count: a.handshake_count,
        authorization_pipe: a.authorization_pipe,
        authorized_app_id: a.authorized_app_id,
    })
}

fn ensure_scanned(auth: &mut ProcessAuth, process: &ProcessKey, app_id: AppId_t) {
    if auth.scanned {
        LOG_PIPE_TRACE!(
            "DenuvoAuth: reusing cached protection result {} denuvo={}",
            process.debug_string(), auth.denuvo,
        );
        return;
    }
    auth.scanned = true;
    if lua_config::is_forced_denuvo(app_id) {
        auth.denuvo = true;
        LOG_PIPE_INFO!(
            "DenuvoAuth: forcedenuvo appid={} - skipping ProtectionScan", app_id,
        );
    } else {
        auth.denuvo = protection_scan::scan_protection(process.pid).denuvo_detected;
    }
    if !auth.denuvo {
        auth.stage = Stage::None;
    }
}

/// Entry point from `PipeManager::OnHandshake`.
///
/// # Safety
/// `ctx.pipe`, if non-null, must point at a live `CPipeClient`.
pub unsafe fn apply(ctx: &PipeContext) {
    if !ctx.game_process || !ctx.tracked_app { return; }

    let pipe_key = make_pipe_key(ctx.pipe);
    if !pipe_key.is_valid() { return; }

    let mut auths = G_PROCESS_AUTH.lock();
    let auth = auths.entry(ctx.process).or_insert_with(ProcessAuth::new);
    G_PIPE_PROCESS.lock().insert(pipe_key, ctx.process);

    ensure_scanned(auth, &ctx.process, ctx.app_id);
    auth.on_handshake(ctx, pipe_key);
}

/// True only while the pipe is the selected authorization pipe and
/// Denuvo has not reached the end-authorization handshake.
pub fn is_authorized_pipe(pipe: *const CPipeClient) -> bool {
    if pipe.is_null() {
        LOG_PIPE_TRACE!("DenuvoAuth: pipe not in authorization window: null pipe");
        return false;
    }
    let pipe_key = unsafe { make_pipe_key(pipe) };
    let Some(auth) = find_auth_for_pipe(pipe_key) else {
        LOG_PIPE_TRACE!(
            "DenuvoAuth: pipe not tracked by DenuvoAuth {}", pipe_key.debug_string(),
        );
        return false;
    };
    if !auth.can_use_authorized_identity(pipe_key) {
        LOG_PIPE_TRACE!(
            "DenuvoAuth: pipe not in authorization window {} {}",
            pipe_key.debug_string(), auth.debug_string(),
        );
        return false;
    }
    LOG_PIPE_INFO!(
        "DenuvoAuth: pipe in authorization window {} {}",
        pipe_key.debug_string(), auth.debug_string(),
    );
    true
}

===== FILE: src\pipe\injection.rs =====
//! Per-pipe DLL injection. Source:
//! `Pipe/Features/Injection/Injection.cpp`.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use parking_lot::Mutex;

use crate::pipe::pipe_types::{PipeContext, ProcessKey};
use crate::platform::process;
use crate::platform::remote_process::{self, InjectStatus};
use crate::utils::config::config::{self, InjectDll};

/// Keyed on `(process, path)` so each DLL injects at most once per
/// process while several `[[inject]]` entries can still target the
/// same game.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
struct InjectedKey {
    process: ProcessKey,
    path: String,
}

static G_INJECTED: Lazy<Mutex<HashSet<InjectedKey>>> =
    Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(HashSet::new()));

fn claim_injection(key: &InjectedKey) -> bool {
    G_INJECTED.lock().insert(key.clone())
}

fn matches(dll: &InjectDll, ctx: &PipeContext, cmd_line: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    if !dll.all_games && !ctx.tracked_app { return false; }
    if !dll.when_appids.is_empty() && !dll.when_appids.contains(&ctx.app_id) {
        return false;
    }
    if !dll.when_cmdline.is_empty() {
        match cmd_line {
            Some(c) if c.contains(&dll.when_cmdline) => {}
            _ => return false,
        }
    }
    true
}

pub fn apply(ctx: &PipeContext) {
    let dlls = config::get_inject_dlls();
    if dlls.is_empty() { return; }
    if !ctx.game_process { return; }

    // Read the command line lazily: only if an injection entry uses it.
    let mut cmd_line: Option<String> = None;
    let mut cmd_line_resolved = false;

    for dll in &dlls {
        let cmd = if dll.when_cmdline.is_empty() {
            cmd_line.as_deref()
        } else {
            if !cmd_line_resolved {
                cmd_line = process::get_process_command_line(ctx.process.pid);
                cmd_line_resolved = true;
            }
            cmd_line.as_deref()
        };

        if !matches(dll, ctx, cmd) { continue; }
        if !claim_injection(&InjectedKey {
            process: ctx.process,
            path: dll.path.clone(),
        }) {
            continue;
        }

        let path = PathBuf::from(&dll.path);
        let status = remote_process::inject_library(ctx.process.pid, &path);
        if status == InjectStatus::Ok {
            LOG_INJECT_INFO!(
                "injected pid={} appid={} dll=\"{}\"",
                ctx.process.pid, ctx.app_id,
                path.file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("?"),
            );
        } else {
            LOG_INJECT_WARN!(
                "inject failed pid={} appid={} status={} dll=\"{}\"",
                ctx.process.pid, ctx.app_id, status.as_str(),
                path.file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("?"),
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn mk_dll(all_games: bool, when_appids: &[u32], when_cmdline: &str) -> InjectDll {
        InjectDll {
            path: String::new(),
            when_cmdline: when_cmdline.to_string(),
            when_appids: when_appids.iter().copied().collect(),
            all_games,
        }
    }

    fn mk_ctx(tracked: bool, app_id: u32) -> PipeContext {
        PipeContext {
            pipe: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            process: ProcessKey { pid: 1, creation_time: 1 },
            app_id,
            game_process: true,
            tracked_app: tracked,
            owned: false,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn matches_requires_tracked_or_all_games() {
        let ctx = mk_ctx(false, 100);
        assert!(!matches(&mk_dll(false, &[], ""), &ctx, None));
        assert!(matches(&mk_dll(true, &[], ""), &ctx, None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn matches_requires_appid_when_appids_given() {
        let ctx = mk_ctx(true, 100);
        assert!(matches(&mk_dll(true, &[100], ""), &ctx, None));
        assert!(!matches(&mk_dll(true, &[200], ""), &ctx, None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn matches_requires_substring_in_cmdline() {
        let ctx = mk_ctx(true, 100);
        assert!(matches(&mk_dll(true, &[], "launch"), &ctx, Some("game.exe launch")));
        assert!(!matches(&mk_dll(true, &[], "launch"), &ctx, Some("game.exe")));
        assert!(!matches(&mk_dll(true, &[], "launch"), &ctx, None));
    }
}

===== FILE: src\pipe\pipe_manager.rs =====
//! `Pipe/PipeManager.cpp`. `OnHandshake` resolves the caller once,
//! caches the process snapshot, then lets each Pipe feature react.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::time::Duration;

use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
use parking_lot::Mutex;

use crate::hook::misc as hooks_misc;
use crate::pipe::denuvo_auth;
use crate::pipe::injection;
use crate::pipe::pipe_types::{make_pipe_key, PipeContext, PipeKey, ProcessKey};
use crate::pipe::process_inspector::{self, ProcessSnapshot};
use crate::steam::structs::CPipeClient;
use crate::steam::types::AppId_t;
use crate::utils::config::lua_config;

/// steamclient doesn't always finish binding a brand-new pipe to its
/// appid by the literal handshake instant. Observed empirically:
/// `GetAppIDForCurrentPipe` returns invalid at handshake time, then the
/// correct appid ~20 ms later once the game's first real IPC call
/// lands. `OnHandshake` only runs once per pipe, so a wrong
/// `trackedApp=false` on that single call permanently mis-tracks the
/// process. Retry briefly instead of accepting the first sample.
const K_APPID_RESOLVE_RETRIES: i32 = 10;
const K_APPID_RESOLVE_RETRY_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_millis(20);

static G_PROCESSES: Lazy<Mutex<HashMap<ProcessKey, ProcessSnapshot>>> =
    Lazy::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));

fn make_process_key(snapshot: &ProcessSnapshot) -> ProcessKey {
    ProcessKey { pid: snapshot.pid, creation_time: snapshot.creation_time }
}

fn try_reuse_cached_process(pid: u32) -> Option<ProcessSnapshot> {
    let current = process_inspector::get_process_creation_time(pid)?;
    let key = ProcessKey { pid, creation_time: current };
    let g = G_PROCESSES.lock();
    g.get(&key).cloned()
}

fn resolve_process(pid: u32) -> ProcessSnapshot {
    if let Some(cached) = try_reuse_cached_process(pid) { return cached; }

    // First sighting: inspect once and cache so sibling pipes reuse it.
    // A dead process yields creation_time=0, so skip caching that junk
    // key.
    let snapshot = process_inspector::inspect_process(pid);
    let key = make_process_key(&snapshot);
    if key.is_valid() {
        G_PROCESSES.lock().insert(key, snapshot.clone());
    }
    snapshot
}

/// Env-based appid first (cheap, and a missing env var will never
/// appear no matter how long we wait, so it's only tried once). Falls
/// back to the pipe's own appid, retrying briefly since that binding
/// can lag the handshake by a few ms. Returns 0 if every attempt comes
/// up empty and the process-name config lookup also fails.
fn resolve_app_id_with_retry(
    snapshot: &ProcessSnapshot,
    out_from_pipe: &mut bool,
) -> AppId_t {
    *out_from_pipe = false;

    let env_app_id = snapshot.resolve_app_id();
    if env_app_id != 0 { return env_app_id; }

    for attempt in 0..K_APPID_RESOLVE_RETRIES {
        let pipe_app_id = hooks_misc::resolve_app_id();
        if pipe_app_id != 0 {
            *out_from_pipe = true;
            if attempt > 0 {
                LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
                    "PipeManager: pipe appid resolved on retry attempt={} appid={}",
                    attempt, pipe_app_id,
                );
            }
            return pipe_app_id;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(K_APPID_RESOLVE_RETRY_DELAY);
    }

    // Neither env var nor IPC pipe binding resolved an appid — the
    // game launched without SteamAppId and never called
    // IClientUtils::GetAppID in the retry window. Fall back to an
    // explicit process-name mapping from `addprocess()` in LuaConfig.
    if !snapshot.image_name.is_empty() {
        let config_app_id = lua_config::get_app_id_for_process(&snapshot.image_name);
        if config_app_id != 0 {
            LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
                "PipeManager: process-name config appid image={} appid={}",
                snapshot.image_name, config_app_id,
            );
            return config_app_id;
        }
    }

    0
}

/// # Safety
/// `pipe`, if non-null, must point at a live `CPipeClient`.
pub unsafe fn on_handshake(pipe: *mut CPipeClient) {
    if pipe.is_null() {
        LOG_PIPE_INFO!("PipeManager: ignore null pipe handshake");
        return;
    }

    let pipe_key = make_pipe_key(pipe);
    if pipe_key.pid == 0 {
        LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
            "PipeManager: ignore handshake with invalid pipe key {}",
            pipe_key.debug_string(),
        );
        return;
    }

    let snapshot = resolve_process(pipe_key.pid);
    let process_key = make_process_key(&snapshot);
    if !process_key.is_valid() {
        LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
            "PipeManager: ignore handshake with invalid process key {} snapshot={}",
            process_key.debug_string(), snapshot.debug_string(),
        );
        return;
    }

    // Env-based appid first; fall back to the pipe's appid (with a
    // short retry) for games that launch WITHOUT exporting SteamAppId
    // (a launcher / child process). Without this, those games never
    // get tracked and DenuvoAuth never runs.
    let mut app_id_from_pipe = false;
    let app_id = resolve_app_id_with_retry(&snapshot, &mut app_id_from_pipe);
    let tracked_app = app_id != 0 && lua_config::has_depot(app_id, false);

    // `likely_game_process` is env-derived (needs SteamAppId exported),
    // so it's false for env-less games. A pipe that resolves to a
    // configured depot is a tracked game regardless, and
    // `DenuvoAuth::Apply` requires `gameProcess && trackedApp` — so
    // treat a tracked depot as a game process even without the env.
    let game_process = snapshot.likely_game_process || tracked_app;

    let ctx = PipeContext {
        pipe,
        process: process_key,
        app_id,
        game_process,
        tracked_app,
        owned: tracked_app && lua_config::is_owned(app_id),
    };

    LOG_PIPE_INFO!(
        "PipeManager: handshake {} process={} appid={} appIdFromPipe={} gameProcess={} trackedApp={} snapshot={}",
        pipe_key.debug_string(), process_key.debug_string(), app_id,
        app_id_from_pipe, game_process, tracked_app, snapshot.debug_string(),
    );

    // Feature side effects run without holding the registry lock.
    denuvo_auth::apply(&ctx);
    injection::apply(&ctx);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]

        // Should not panic and should not create any state.
        unsafe { on_handshake(std::ptr::null_mut()) };
    }

        let snap = ProcessSnapshot { pid: 5, creation_time: 10, ..Default::default() };
        assert_eq!(make_process_key(&snap), ProcessKey { pid: 5, creation_time: 10 });
    }
}


===== FILE: src\pipe\pipe_types.rs =====
//! Shared identities passed between Pipe features. Source:
//! `Pipe/PipeTypes.h`.

use crate::steam::structs::CPipeClient;
use crate::steam::types::{AppId_t, HSteamPipe, PID_t};

/// PID plus creation time. Lets caches survive PID reuse safely.
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ProcessKey {
    pub pid: PID_t,
    pub creation_time: u64,
}

impl ProcessKey {
    pub fn is_valid(&self) -> bool {
        self.pid != 0 && self.creation_time != 0
    }

    pub fn debug_string(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "pid={} creation={} filetime={}",
            self.pid,
            crate::platform::process::format_creation_time(self.creation_time),
            self.creation_time,
        )
    }
}

/// A process may open several Steam IPC pipes.
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct PipeKey {
    pub pid: PID_t,
    pub pipe: HSteamPipe,
}

impl PipeKey {
    pub fn is_valid(&self) -> bool {
        self.pid != 0 && self.pipe != 0
    }

    pub fn debug_string(&self) -> String {
        format!("pid={} pipe=0x{:08X}", self.pid, self.pipe as u32)
    }
}

/// # Safety
/// `pipe`, if non-null, must point at a live `CPipeClient`.
pub unsafe fn make_pipe_key(pipe: *const CPipeClient) -> PipeKey {
    if pipe.is_null() {
        return PipeKey { pid: 0, pipe: 0 };
    }
    PipeKey {
        pid: (*pipe).m_clientPID,
        pipe: (*pipe).m_hSteamPipe,
    }
}

pub struct PipeContext {
    pub pipe: *mut CPipeClient,
    pub process: ProcessKey,
    pub app_id: AppId_t,
    pub game_process: bool,
    pub tracked_app: bool,
    pub owned: bool,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn process_key_valid_requires_both_fields() {
        assert!(!ProcessKey { pid: 0, creation_time: 1 }.is_valid());
        assert!(!ProcessKey { pid: 1, creation_time: 0 }.is_valid());
        assert!(ProcessKey { pid: 1, creation_time: 1 }.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn pipe_key_valid_requires_both_fields() {
        assert!(!PipeKey { pid: 0, pipe: 1 }.is_valid());
        assert!(!PipeKey { pid: 1, pipe: 0 }.is_valid());
        assert!(PipeKey { pid: 1, pipe: 1 }.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn make_pipe_key_null_is_invalid() {
        let k = unsafe { make_pipe_key(std::ptr::null()) };
        assert_eq!(k.pid, 0);
        assert_eq!(k.pipe, 0);
        assert!(!k.is_valid());
    }
}


===== FILE: src\pipe\process_inspector.rs =====
//! Process snapshot + Steam environment query. Source:
//! `Pipe/ProcessInspector.cpp`.

use crate::platform::numbers;
use crate::platform::process;
use crate::platform::stopwatch::Stopwatch;
use crate::steam::types::AppId_t;

pub const K_STEAM_PROCESS_NAMES: [&str; 6] = [
    "steam.exe",
    "steamwebhelper.exe",
    "steamservice.exe",
    "steamerrorreporter.exe",
    "gameoverlayui.exe",
    "gameoverlayui64.exe",
];

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ProcessEnvironment {
    pub steam_overlay_game_id_app_id: Option<AppId_t>,
    pub steam_game_id_app_id: Option<AppId_t>,
    pub steam_app_id: Option<AppId_t>,
}

impl ProcessEnvironment {
    pub fn resolve_app_id(&self) -> AppId_t {
        if let Some(id) = self.steam_overlay_game_id_app_id { return id; }
        if let Some(id) = self.steam_game_id_app_id { return id; }
        self.steam_app_id.unwrap_or(0)
    }

    pub fn has_steam_app_environment(&self) -> bool {
        self.steam_app_id.is_some()
            || self.steam_game_id_app_id.is_some()
            || self.steam_overlay_game_id_app_id.is_some()
    }

    pub fn debug_string(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "SteamAppId={} SteamGameId={} SteamOverlayGameId={} resolvedAppId={}",
            self.steam_app_id.unwrap_or(0),
            self.steam_game_id_app_id.unwrap_or(0),
            self.steam_overlay_game_id_app_id.unwrap_or(0),
            self.resolve_app_id(),
        )
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ProcessSnapshot {
    pub pid: u32,
    pub creation_time: u64,
    pub image_path: String,
    pub image_name: String,
    pub steam_client_process: bool,
    pub likely_game_process: bool,
    pub environment: ProcessEnvironment,
}

impl ProcessSnapshot {
    pub fn resolve_app_id(&self) -> AppId_t {
        self.environment.resolve_app_id()
    }

    pub fn debug_string(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "pid={} creation={} image={} steamClientProcess={} likelyGameProcess={} env=[{}]",
            self.pid,
            format!(
                "{} filetime={}",
                process::format_creation_time(self.creation_time),
                self.creation_time,
            ),
            if self.image_name.is_empty() { "-" } else { &self.image_name },
            self.steam_client_process,
            self.likely_game_process,
            self.environment.debug_string(),
        )
    }
}

fn base_name_from_path(path: &str) -> String {
    match path.rfind(|c| c == '\\' || c == '/') {
        Some(i) => path[i + 1..].to_string(),
        None => path.to_string(),
    }
}

fn app_id_from_game_id_string(value: &str) -> Option<AppId_t> {
    let parsed = numbers::parse_u64(value)?;
    let app_id = (parsed & 0x00FF_FFFF) as u32;
    if app_id == 0 { None } else { Some(app_id) }
}

fn app_id_from_appid_string(value: &str) -> Option<AppId_t> {
    let parsed = numbers::parse_u32(value)?;
    if parsed == 0 { None } else { Some(parsed) }
}

fn wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> { s.encode_utf16().collect() }

pub fn get_process_creation_time(pid: u32) -> Option<u64> {
    process::get_creation_time(pid)
}

pub fn is_steam_process_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    let lower = name.to_ascii_lowercase();
    K_STEAM_PROCESS_NAMES.iter().any(|n| *n == lower)
}

pub fn read_steam_environment(pid: u32) -> ProcessEnvironment {
    let mut env = ProcessEnvironment::default();
    if let Some(v) = process::get_environment_variable_value(pid, &wide("SteamAppId")) {
        env.steam_app_id = app_id_from_appid_string(&v);
    }
    if let Some(v) = process::get_environment_variable_value(pid, &wide("SteamGameId")) {
        env.steam_game_id_app_id = app_id_from_game_id_string(&v);
    }
    if let Some(v) = process::get_environment_variable_value(pid, &wide("SteamOverlayGameId")) {
        env.steam_overlay_game_id_app_id = app_id_from_game_id_string(&v);
    }
    LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!("ProcessInspector: pid={} steam env {}", pid, env.debug_string());
    env
}

pub fn inspect_process(pid: u32) -> ProcessSnapshot {
    let timer = Stopwatch::new();
    let mut snapshot = ProcessSnapshot {
        pid,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    snapshot.creation_time = get_process_creation_time(pid).unwrap_or(0);

    if let Some(p) = process::get_image_path(pid) {
        snapshot.image_path = p;
        snapshot.image_name = base_name_from_path(&snapshot.image_path);
    }
    snapshot.steam_client_process = is_steam_process_name(&snapshot.image_name);
    snapshot.environment = read_steam_environment(pid);
    snapshot.likely_game_process =
        !snapshot.steam_client_process && snapshot.environment.has_steam_app_environment();

    LOG_PIPE_INFO!(
        "ProcessInspector: inspected {} elapsed_ms={:.3}",
        snapshot.debug_string(),
        timer.elapsed_ms(),
    );
    snapshot
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn base_name_variants() {
        assert_eq!(base_name_from_path("C:\\a\\b\\c.exe"), "c.exe");
        assert_eq!(base_name_from_path("c.exe"), "c.exe");
        assert_eq!(base_name_from_path("C:/a/b/c.exe"), "c.exe");
    }

    #[test]
    fn app_id_from_game_id_masks_24_bits() {
        // Mask keeps 24 bits. 730 = 0x2DA, well within range.
        assert_eq!(app_id_from_game_id_string("730"), Some(730));
        // 0x1100001000000042 -> masked to 0x42. Use the literal here
        // rather than a decimal transcription: the equivalence between
        // the two representations is exactly what a hand-typed decimal
        // gets wrong.
        let big: u64 = 0x1100_0010_0000_0042;
        assert_eq!(app_id_from_game_id_string(&big.to_string()), Some(0x42));
        // Zero masked -> None
        assert_eq!(app_id_from_game_id_string("0"), None);
        // Non-numeric
        assert_eq!(app_id_from_game_id_string("xyz"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn app_id_from_appid_rejects_zero() {
        assert_eq!(app_id_from_appid_string("730"), Some(730));
        assert_eq!(app_id_from_appid_string("0"), None);
        assert_eq!(app_id_from_appid_string("xyz"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn steam_process_name_case_insensitive() {
        assert!(is_steam_process_name("steam.exe"));
        assert!(is_steam_process_name("STEAM.EXE"));
        assert!(is_steam_process_name("SteamWebHelper.exe"));
        assert!(!is_steam_process_name("notsteam.exe"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn environment_resolve_prefers_overlay_then_game_then_app() {
        let mut env = ProcessEnvironment::default();
        assert_eq!(env.resolve_app_id(), 0);
        assert!(!env.has_steam_app_environment());

        env.steam_app_id = Some(100);
        assert_eq!(env.resolve_app_id(), 100);

        env.steam_game_id_app_id = Some(200);
        assert_eq!(env.resolve_app_id(), 200);

        env.steam_overlay_game_id_app_id = Some(300);
        assert_eq!(env.resolve_app_id(), 300);

        assert!(env.has_steam_app_environment());
    }
}

//! Denuvo-specific module scanner. Source:
//! `Pipe/Features/DenuvoAuth/ProtectionScan.cpp`.
//!
//! ProcessInspector stays generic; this file owns only the current
//! "is this process protected" policy.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use crate::platform::byte_search;
use crate::platform::pe::Image;
use crate::platform::process;
use crate::platform::stopwatch::Stopwatch;
use crate::steam::types::AppId_t;

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DetectionMethod {
    None,
    LegacySectionString,
    OepPattern,
    ProtectedBlobSection,
}

pub fn to_string(method: DetectionMethod) -> &'static str {
    match method {
        DetectionMethod::None => "None",
        DetectionMethod::LegacySectionString => "LegacySectionString",
        DetectionMethod::OepPattern => "OepPattern",
        DetectionMethod::ProtectedBlobSection => "ProtectedBlobSection",
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ProtectionScanReport {
    pub denuvo_detected: bool,
    pub method: Option<DetectionMethod>,
    pub module_path: String,
    pub section_name: String,
    pub pid: u32,
    pub module_size: u32,
    pub entry_point_rva: u32,
    pub match_rva: u32,
    pub match_raw_offset: usize,
    pub scanned_modules: usize,
    pub elapsed_ms: f64,
}

impl ProtectionScanReport {
    pub fn debug_string(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "[pid={}] denuvoDetected={} method={} module={} section={} moduleSize={} entryPointRva=0x{:X} matchRva=0x{:X} matchRaw=0x{:X} scannedModules={} elapsedMs={:.3}",
            self.pid,
            self.denuvo_detected,
            to_string(self.method.unwrap_or(DetectionMethod::None)),
            if self.module_path.is_empty() { "-" } else { &self.module_path },
            if self.section_name.is_empty() { "-" } else { &self.section_name },
            self.module_size,
            self.entry_point_rva,
            self.match_rva,
            self.match_raw_offset,
            self.scanned_modules,
            self.elapsed_ms,
        )
    }
}

// ── Constants ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const K_LEGACY_DENUVO_SECTIONS: [&str; 5] =
    [".arch", ".srdata", ".xpdata", ".xdata", ".xtls"];

const K_LEGACY_DENUVO_STRING: [u8; 6] = *b"DENUVO";

/// `48 B9` = mov rcx, imm64, immediately followed by "DENUVO\0\0".
const K_DENUVO_OEP_PATTERN: [u8; 10] =
    [0x48, 0xB9, 0x44, 0x4F, 0x44, 0x45, 0x4E, 0x55, 0x56, 0x4F];

const K_MIN_PACKED_MODULE_BYTES: u32 = 80 * 1024 * 1024;
const K_LEGACY_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
const K_OEP_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;

const K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_MIN_BYTES: u32 = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
const K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_MIN_ENTROPY: f64 = 6.0;
const K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_HIGH_CONFIDENCE_ENTROPY: f64 = 7.0;
const K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_ENTROPY_SAMPLE_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;

const K_STEAM_RUNTIME_MODULE_NAMES: [&str; 10] = [
    "steamclient.dll",
    "steamclient64.dll",
    "steam_api.dll",
    "steam_api64.dll",
    "tier0_s.dll",
    "tier0_s64.dll",
    "vstdlib_s.dll",
    "vstdlib_s64.dll",
    "gameoverlayrenderer.dll",
    "gameoverlayrenderer64.dll",
];

// ── Internal types ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ModuleCandidate {
    path: String,
    native_path: PathBuf,
    size: u32,
    executable: bool,
    in_game_tree: bool,
    order: usize,
}

impl ModuleCandidate {
    fn debug_string(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "path={} size={} executable={} inGameTree={} order={}",
            self.path, self.size, self.executable, self.in_game_tree, self.order,
        )
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
struct DetectionMatch {
    method: Option<DetectionMethod>,
    section_name: String,
    entry_point_rva: u32,
    match_rva: u32,
    match_raw_offset: usize,
}

// ── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn section_entropy(bytes: &[u8]) -> f64 {
    if bytes.is_empty() { return 0.0; }
    let mut counts = [0u64; 256];
    for &b in bytes {
        counts[b as usize] += 1;
    }
    let n = bytes.len() as f64;
    let mut e = 0.0f64;
    for &c in counts.iter() {
        if c > 0 {
            let p = c as f64 / n;
            e -= p * p.log2();
        }
    }
    e
}

fn bytes_to_mib(bytes: u64) -> f64 {
    bytes as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0)
}

fn ends_with_insensitive(value: &str, suffix: &str) -> bool {
    if value.len() < suffix.len() { return false; }
    value.as_bytes()[value.len() - suffix.len()..]
        .eq_ignore_ascii_case(suffix.as_bytes())
}

fn base_name_from_path(path: &str) -> String {
    match path.rfind(|c| c == '\\' || c == '/') {
        Some(i) => path[i + 1..].to_string(),
        None => path.to_string(),
    }
}

fn directory_from_path(path: &str) -> String {
    match path.rfind(|c| c == '\\' || c == '/') {
        Some(i) => path[..=i].to_string(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

fn normalize_directory_prefix(path: &str) -> String {
    let mut s = path.to_ascii_lowercase().replace('/', "\\");
    if !s.is_empty() && !s.ends_with('\\') { s.push('\\'); }
    s
}

fn path_starts_with_insensitive(path: &str, prefix: &str) -> bool {
    if prefix.is_empty() { return false; }
    let p = path.to_ascii_lowercase().replace('/', "\\");
    p.starts_with(prefix)
}

fn is_steam_runtime_module_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    let lower = name.to_ascii_lowercase();
    K_STEAM_RUNTIME_MODULE_NAMES.iter().any(|n| *n == lower)
}

fn find_legacy_denuvo_section(image: &Image) -> Option<&crate::platform::pe::Section> {
    for name in K_LEGACY_DENUVO_SECTIONS {
        for s in image.sections() {
            if s.name == name { return Some(s); }
        }
    }
    None
}

// ── Detection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn try_legacy_section_string(
    module: &ModuleCandidate,
    image: &Image,
    section: &crate::platform::pe::Section,
) -> Option<DetectionMatch> {
    let match_raw = byte_search::find_in_file(
        &module.native_path,
        &K_LEGACY_DENUVO_STRING,
        K_LEGACY_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES,
    )?;
    let mut m = DetectionMatch::default();
    m.method = Some(DetectionMethod::LegacySectionString);
    m.section_name = section.name.clone();
    m.entry_point_rva = image.entry_point_rva();
    m.match_raw_offset = match_raw as usize;
    m.match_rva = image.raw_offset_to_rva(m.match_raw_offset).unwrap_or(0);
    Some(m)
}

fn try_oep_pattern(module: &ModuleCandidate, image: &Image) -> Option<DetectionMatch> {
    let oep = image.entry_point_rva();
    if oep == 0 { return None; }
    let section = image.section_containing_rva(oep)?;
    if section.raw_size == 0 { return None; }
    let match_raw = byte_search::find_in_file_range(
        &module.native_path,
        section.raw_offset as u64,
        section.raw_size as u64,
        &K_DENUVO_OEP_PATTERN,
        K_OEP_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES,
    )?;
    let local_match = (match_raw - section.raw_offset as u64) as u32;
    let mut m = DetectionMatch::default();
    m.method = Some(DetectionMethod::OepPattern);
    m.section_name = section.name.clone();
    m.entry_point_rva = oep;
    m.match_raw_offset = match_raw as usize;
    m.match_rva = section.virtual_address.wrapping_add(local_match);
    Some(m)
}

fn try_protected_blob_section(
    module: &ModuleCandidate,
    image: &Image,
) -> Option<DetectionMatch> {
    for section in image.sections() {
        if !(section.is_executable() && section.is_writable()) { continue; }
        if section.raw_size < K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_MIN_BYTES { continue; }

        let sample_size =
            (section.raw_size as usize).min(K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_ENTROPY_SAMPLE_BYTES);
        let sample = image.read_raw_bytes(section.raw_offset as usize, sample_size);
        if sample.is_empty() { continue; }

        let entropy = section_entropy(sample.as_slice());
        if entropy < K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_MIN_ENTROPY { continue; }

        let mut m = DetectionMatch::default();
        m.method = Some(DetectionMethod::ProtectedBlobSection);
        m.section_name = section.name.clone();
        m.entry_point_rva = image.entry_point_rva();
        m.match_raw_offset = section.raw_offset as usize;
        m.match_rva = section.virtual_address;

        let confidence = if entropy >= K_PROTECTOR_BLOB_HIGH_CONFIDENCE_ENTROPY {
            "high(encrypted)"
        } else { "elevated" };
        LOG_PIPE_INFO!(
            "DenuvoAuth: protector blob section path={} section={} raw_size={} ({:.2} MB) entropy={:.3} flags=RWX confidence={}",
            module.path, section.name, section.raw_size,
            bytes_to_mib(section.raw_size as u64), entropy, confidence,
        );
        return Some(m);
    }
    None
}

fn detect_module(module: &ModuleCandidate, image: &Image) -> Option<DetectionMatch> {
    if let Some(m) = try_oep_pattern(module, image) { return Some(m); }
    if let Some(section) = find_legacy_denuvo_section(image) {
        if let Some(m) = try_legacy_section_string(module, image, section) { return Some(m); }
    }
    try_protected_blob_section(module, image)
}

// ── Module enumeration ──────────────────────────────────────────────

fn enumerate_modules(pid: u32) -> Vec<ModuleCandidate> {
    let timer = Stopwatch::new();
    let mut modules: Vec<ModuleCandidate> = Vec::new();
    let mut order = 0usize;

    for m in process::enumerate_modules(pid) {
        if m.path.is_empty() { continue; }
        let executable = ends_with_insensitive(&m.path, ".exe");
        let dll = ends_with_insensitive(&m.path, ".dll");
        if !executable && !dll { continue; }
        if m.size < K_MIN_PACKED_MODULE_BYTES { continue; }
        if !executable && process::is_system_module_path(&m.path) { continue; }
        if !executable && is_steam_runtime_module_name(&base_name_from_path(&m.path)) {
            continue;
        }
        modules.push(ModuleCandidate {
            path: m.path,
            native_path: m.native_path,
            size: m.size,
            executable,
            in_game_tree: false,
            order,
        });
        order += 1;
    }

    // The first executable module in the list defines the game tree.
    let mut game_directory = String::new();
    for m in &modules {
        if m.executable {
            game_directory = normalize_directory_prefix(&directory_from_path(&m.path));
            break;
        }
    }
    for m in modules.iter_mut() {
        m.in_game_tree = !m.executable
            && path_starts_with_insensitive(&m.path, &game_directory);
    }

    // Sort: .exe first, then in-game-tree DLLs, then by size descending,
    // ties broken by discovery order.
    modules.sort_by(|a, b| {
        if a.executable != b.executable {
            return b.executable.cmp(&a.executable);
        }
        if !a.executable && a.in_game_tree != b.in_game_tree {
            return b.in_game_tree.cmp(&a.in_game_tree);
        }
        if !a.executable && a.size != b.size {
            return b.size.cmp(&a.size);
        }
        a.order.cmp(&b.order)
    });

    LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
        "DenuvoAuth: pid={} enumerated {} candidate module(s) elapsed_ms={:.3}",
        pid, modules.len(), timer.elapsed_ms(),
    );
    modules
}

// ── Entry point ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub fn scan_protection(pid: u32) -> ProtectionScanReport {
    let mut report = ProtectionScanReport::default();
    if pid == 0 { return report; }

    let total_timer = Stopwatch::new();
    let modules = enumerate_modules(pid);
    LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
        "DenuvoAuth: pid={} scanning {} candidate module(s)", pid, modules.len(),
    );

    for module in &modules {
        report.scanned_modules += 1;
        LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
            "DenuvoAuth: module candidate {}: {}",
            report.scanned_modules, module.debug_string(),
        );

        let image = Image::new(&module.native_path);
        if !image.is_valid() {
            continue;
        }

        let Some(m) = detect_module(module, &image) else { continue; };

        report.pid = pid;
        report.denuvo_detected = true;
        report.method = m.method;
        report.module_path = module.path.clone();
        report.section_name = m.section_name;
        report.module_size = module.size;
        report.entry_point_rva = m.entry_point_rva;
        report.match_rva = m.match_rva;
        report.match_raw_offset = m.match_raw_offset;
        report.elapsed_ms = total_timer.elapsed_ms();

        LOG_PIPE_INFO!(
            "DenuvoAuth: success to detect Denuvo in module {}", report.debug_string(),
        );
        return report;
    }

    report.elapsed_ms = total_timer.elapsed_ms();
    LOG_PIPE_DEBUG!(
        "DenuvoAuth: pid={} no Denuvo match scanned={} elapsed_ms={:.3}",
        pid, report.scanned_modules, report.elapsed_ms,
    );
    report
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {

        assert_eq!(section_entropy(&[]), 0.0);
    }

        let bytes = vec![0xAA; 1024];
        assert_eq!(section_entropy(&bytes), 0.0);
    }

    fn entropy_of_all_distinct_is_near_eight() {
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = (0..=255u8).collect();
        let e = section_entropy(&bytes);
        assert!((e - 8.0).abs() < 0.001, "entropy was {}", e);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ends_with_insensitive_case_folding() {
        assert!(ends_with_insensitive("Kernel32.DLL", ".dll"));
        assert!(ends_with_insensitive("Kernel32.dll", ".DLL"));
        assert!(!ends_with_insensitive("Kernel32.dll", ".exe"));
        assert!(!ends_with_insensitive("x.dll", ".verylong"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_directory_prefix_appends_backslash() {
        assert_eq!(normalize_directory_prefix("C:\\Steam"), "c:\\steam\\");
        assert_eq!(normalize_directory_prefix("C:/Steam/"), "c:\\steam\\");
        assert_eq!(normalize_directory_prefix(""), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_starts_with_insensitive_case_and_sep() {
        assert!(path_starts_with_insensitive("C:\\Steam\\x.dll", "c:\\steam\\"));
        assert!(path_starts_with_insensitive("C:/Steam/x.dll", "c:\\steam\\"));
        assert!(!path_starts_with_insensitive("C:\\Other\\x.dll", "c:\\steam\\"));
        assert!(!path_starts_with_insensitive("x", ""));
    }

    #[test]
    fn base_name_variants() {
        assert_eq!(base_name_from_path("C:\\a\\b.dll"), "b.dll");
        assert_eq!(base_name_from_path("b.dll"), "b.dll");
    }

    #[test]
    fn to_string_covers_all_variants() {
        assert_eq!(to_string(DetectionMethod::None), "None");
        assert_eq!(to_string(DetectionMethod::OepPattern), "OepPattern");
        assert_eq!(to_string(DetectionMethod::ProtectedBlobSection), "ProtectedBlobSection");
        assert_eq!(to_string(DetectionMethod::LegacySectionString), "LegacySectionString");
    }

    #[test]
    fn scan_zero_pid_returns_empty() {
        let r = scan_protection(0);
        assert!(!r.denuvo_detected);
        assert_eq!(r.scanned_modules, 0);
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\byte_search.rs =====
//! Byte-pattern scanning. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/ByteSearch.cpp`
//!
//! * [`find`] - BMH scan over an in-memory buffer.
//! * [`find_in_file`] - whole-file scan via [`find_in_file_range`].
//! * [`find_in_file_range`] - scan a sub-range of a file with a
//!   sliding window, re-reading `pattern.len() - 1` overlapping bytes
//!   between chunks so a match that straddles a boundary is still
//!   found.
//!
//! ## Simplification vs C++
//!
//! The C++ uses overlapped (async) reads with double buffering so the
//! scan of chunk i overlaps the read of chunk i+1. This port uses
//! synchronous positioned reads. The observable behaviour is
//! identical - same results, same overlap logic - but the port does
//! not exploit disk/CPU concurrency. If throughput becomes a
//! bottleneck (e.g. while scanning a ~100 MB module in ProtectionScan),
//! swap the read loop for `windows-sys` `ReadFile` with `OVERLAPPED`;
//! the public API will not change.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{ErrorKind, Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
use std::path::Path;

pub const DEFAULT_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;

/// BMH pattern scanner. Matches the C++ `FixedPatternScanner` exactly.
struct FixedPatternScanner {
    pattern: Vec<u8>,
    skip: [usize; 256],
}

impl FixedPatternScanner {
    fn new(pattern: &[u8]) -> Self {
        let ps = pattern.len();
        // C++ fills with pattern size (or 1 for empty), then overwrites
        // all positions except the last.
        let fill = if ps == 0 { 1 } else { ps };
        let mut skip = [fill; 256];
        if ps > 1 {
            for i in 0..(ps - 1) {
                skip[pattern[i] as usize] = ps - 1 - i;
            }
        }
        Self { pattern: pattern.to_vec(), skip }
    }

    fn find(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
        let ps = self.pattern.len();
        if ps == 0 || bytes.len() < ps {
            return None;
        }
        let mut offset = 0usize;
        while offset <= bytes.len() - ps {
            let tail = bytes[offset + ps - 1];
            if tail == self.pattern[ps - 1] {
                let mut i = ps - 1;
                while i > 0 && bytes[offset + i - 1] == self.pattern[i - 1] {
                    i -= 1;
                }
                if i == 0 {
                    return Some(offset);
                }
            }
            offset += self.skip[tail as usize];
        }
        None
    }
}

/// Find `needle` in `haystack`. Returns the byte offset of the first
/// match, or `None`.
pub fn find(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    FixedPatternScanner::new(needle).find(haystack)
}

/// Read the full buffer, looping on short reads. Stops early on EOF;
/// returns the number of bytes actually read.
fn read_fully(file: &mut File, buf: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
    let mut total = 0usize;
    while total < buf.len() {
        match file.read(&mut buf[total..]) {
            Ok(0) => break,
            Ok(n) => total += n,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        }
    }
    Ok(total)
}

/// Scan an entire file for `needle`. Returns the absolute file offset
/// of the first match.
pub fn find_in_file(path: &Path, needle: &[u8], chunk_bytes: usize) -> Option<u64> {
    // A whole-file scan is a range scan over [0, EOF). The range variant
    // clamps `size` to the real file size, so u64::MAX means "to EOF".
    find_in_file_range(path, 0, u64::MAX, needle, chunk_bytes)
}

/// Scan a sub-range of a file for `needle`.
///
/// `offset` and `size` describe a half-open `[offset, offset+size)`
/// window. If `offset + size` exceeds the file length, the window is
/// clamped to EOF. Returns the absolute file offset of the first match
/// in the window.
pub fn find_in_file_range(
    path: &Path,
    offset: u64,
    size: u64,
    needle: &[u8],
    chunk_bytes: usize,
) -> Option<u64> {
    let scanner = FixedPatternScanner::new(needle);
    let ps = scanner.pattern.len();
    if ps == 0 || size == 0 {
        return None;
    }

    let mut file = File::open(path).ok()?;
    let file_size = file.metadata().ok()?.len();
    if file_size == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    if offset >= file_size {
        return None;
    }

    let range_end = offset + size.min(file_size - offset);
    let chunk = chunk_bytes.max(ps);
    // Consecutive chunks overlap by (ps - 1) bytes so a match that
    // straddles a chunk boundary is fully contained at the head of the
    // next chunk.
    let stride = (chunk - (ps - 1)) as u64;

    let mut buffer = vec![0u8; chunk];
    let mut cur_start = offset;

    while cur_start < range_end {
        let remaining = range_end - cur_start;
        let to_read = chunk.min(remaining as usize);

        if file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(cur_start)).is_err() {
            return None;
        }
        let n = read_fully(&mut file, &mut buffer[..to_read]).ok()?;
        if n == 0 {
            break;
        }

        if let Some(local) = scanner.find(&buffer[..n]) {
            return Some(cur_start + local as u64);
        }

        let next_start = cur_start + stride;
        if next_start >= range_end || next_start <= cur_start {
            break;
        }
        cur_start = next_start;
    }

    None
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Write;

    // ─── in-memory BMH ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    #[test]
    fn find_empty_needle_none() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"abc", b""), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_needle_longer_than_haystack() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"ab", b"abc"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_exact_match() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"abc", b"abc"), Some(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_at_start() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"abcdef", b"abc"), Some(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_at_end() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"abcdef", b"def"), Some(3));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_in_middle() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"abcdefgh", b"de"), Some(3));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_returns_first_match() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"abcabcabc", b"abc"), Some(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_no_match() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"hello world", b"xyz"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_single_byte() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"\x00\x01\x02", b"\x01"), Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_binary_pattern() {
        let haystack = [0u8, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
        let needle = [3u8, 4];
        assert_eq!(find(&haystack, &needle), Some(3));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_pattern_that_almost_matches() {
        // BMH skip table must not miss a match after a partial overlap.
        assert_eq!(find(b"abcabxabcaby", b"abcaby"), Some(6));
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_overlapping_candidates() {
        assert_eq!(find(b"aaab", b"aab"), Some(1));
    }

    // ─── file scanning ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    fn write_temp(name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::path::PathBuf {
        let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(name);
        let mut f = File::create(&p).unwrap();
        f.write_all(bytes).unwrap();
        p
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_finds_at_start() {
        let p = write_temp("ost_bs_start.bin", b"MATCH_and_rest_of_bytes");
        let r = find_in_file(&p, b"MATCH", 1024);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
        assert_eq!(r, Some(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_finds_in_middle() {
        let p = write_temp("ost_bs_mid.bin", b"xxxxxHELLOxxxxx");
        let r = find_in_file(&p, b"HELLO", 1024);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
        assert_eq!(r, Some(5));
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_matches_across_chunk_boundary() {
        // 16-byte chunk, 6-byte pattern. Place the pattern so it
        // straddles the boundary between chunk 0 and chunk 1.
        let mut data = vec![b'a'; 13];
        data.extend_from_slice(b"NEEDLE");
        data.extend_from_slice(&[b'b'; 32]);
        let p = write_temp("ost_bs_boundary.bin", &data);
        // chunk = 16, ps = 6, stride = 16 - 5 = 11. So chunk 0 = [0,16),
        // chunk 1 = [11, 27), etc. The match at offset 13 straddles.
        let r = find_in_file_range(&p, 0, data.len() as u64, b"NEEDLE", 16);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
        assert_eq!(r, Some(13));
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_respects_range_start() {
        let p = write_temp("ost_bs_range.bin", b"HELLO_WORLD_HELLO");
        // Only search [10, 20) - should find the second HELLO at 12.
        let r = find_in_file_range(&p, 10, 10, b"HELLO", 1024);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
        assert_eq!(r, Some(12));
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_range_clamps_to_eof() {
        let p = write_temp("ost_bs_clamp.bin", b"abcdef");
        // Ask for 1000 bytes from offset 3; file is only 6 bytes.
        let r = find_in_file_range(&p, 3, 1000, b"def", 1024);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
        assert_eq!(r, Some(3));
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_no_match_returns_none() {
        let p = write_temp("ost_bs_miss.bin", b"abcdefghij");
        let r = find_in_file(&p, b"xyz", 4);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
        assert_eq!(r, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_offset_past_eof_returns_none() {
        let p = write_temp("ost_bs_past.bin", b"abc");
        let r = find_in_file_range(&p, 100, 10, b"a", 4);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
        assert_eq!(r, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_scan_missing_file_returns_none() {
        let r = find_in_file(Path::new("definitely-not-a-real-file-xyz"), b"a", 4);
        assert_eq!(r, None);
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\detour.rs =====
//! Detour transaction API. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Detour.cpp`
//!
//! Real implementation backed by Microsoft Detours via the FFI
//! declarations in `crate::platform::windows::detours_ffi`.
//!
//! The four public functions preserve the C++ API shape exactly. State
//! is per-thread: a transaction lives only on the thread that opened
//! it, matching Detours' own contract. `HookMacros.h` runs the
//! begin / attach / commit sequence from a single thread, so this is
//! never crossed in practice.
//!
//! ## Thread enrolment
//!
//! Detours requires the calling thread to be enrolled via
//! `DetourUpdateThread` before the first attach. On x64,
//! `DetourTransactionCommit` suspends and updates every other thread
//! automatically, so we enrol lazily: the first `attach` or `detach`
//! inside a transaction calls `DetourUpdateThread(GetCurrentThread())`
//! once. On x86 this would be insufficient - every thread would need
//! enrolling individually. This crate targets x64.

use std::cell::Cell;
use std::ffi::c_void;

#[cfg(windows)]
use super::windows::detours_ffi as ffi;

thread_local! {
    /// `true` when a transaction is open on the calling thread.
    static IN_TRANSACTION: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
    /// `true` once the calling thread has been enrolled in the current
    /// transaction. Reset by `commit_transaction`.
    static THREAD_ENROLLED: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
}

/// Begin a detour transaction on the calling thread.
///
/// Idempotent: calling this while a transaction is already open returns
/// `true` without re-entering Detours.
pub fn begin_transaction() -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        if IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()) {
            return true;
        }
        let status = unsafe { ffi::DetourTransactionBegin() };
        if status != ffi::NO_ERROR {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("DetourTransactionBegin failed (status={})", status);
            return false;
        }
        IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.set(true));
        THREAD_ENROLLED.with(|c| c.set(false));
        true
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("detour::begin_transaction: unsupported on this target");
        false
    }
}

/// Commit a detour transaction.
///
/// Every `attach` / `detach` registered since [`begin_transaction`]
/// applies atomically. Returns `false` if no transaction is open on
/// this thread, or if Detours refuses the commit.
pub fn commit_transaction() -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        if !IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()) {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("detour::commit_transaction called with no transaction open");
            return false;
        }
        let status = unsafe { ffi::DetourTransactionCommit() };
        IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.set(false));
        THREAD_ENROLLED.with(|c| c.set(false));
        if status != ffi::NO_ERROR {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("DetourTransactionCommit failed (status={})", status);
            return false;
        }
        true
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("detour::commit_transaction: unsupported on this target");
        false
    }
}

/// Abort a detour transaction, undoing any pending attaches.
///
/// Not part of the C++ public API, but present here for tests and for
/// the hook layer to use when an attach fails mid-sequence: the C++
/// `HookMacros.h` sets `_ost_detour_transaction_ok_ = false` and
/// expects the surrounding code to unwind, which maps cleanly onto an
/// explicit abort.
pub fn abort_transaction() -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        if !IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()) {
            return false;
        }
        let status = unsafe { ffi::DetourTransactionAbort() };
        IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.set(false));
        THREAD_ENROLLED.with(|c| c.set(false));
        status == ffi::NO_ERROR
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        false
    }
}

/// Install a detour.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// * `target` must point to a writable `*mut c_void` slot owned by the
///   caller. Detours writes the trampoline address into it.
/// * `detour` must be a valid code address with a signature compatible
///   with the target.
/// * A transaction must be open on the calling thread.
/// * Every successful `attach` must be paired with a matching `detach`
///   before the surrounding code unloads the module that owns `detour`.
pub unsafe fn attach(target: *mut *mut c_void, detour: *mut c_void) -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        if target.is_null() || detour.is_null() {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("detour::attach called with null target/detour");
            return false;
        }
        if !IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()) {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("detour::attach called outside a transaction");
            return false;
        }
        if !enrol_current_thread() {
            return false;
        }
        let status = ffi::DetourAttach(target, detour);
        if status != ffi::NO_ERROR {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("DetourAttach failed (status={}, target={:p})", status, target);
            return false;
        }
        true
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        let _ = (target, detour);
        false
    }
}

/// Remove a detour installed by [`attach`].
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `target` and `detour` must be the exact pair passed to [`attach`].
/// A transaction must be open on the calling thread.
pub unsafe fn detach(target: *mut *mut c_void, detour: *mut c_void) -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        if target.is_null() || detour.is_null() {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("detour::detach called with null target/detour");
            return false;
        }
        if !IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()) {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("detour::detach called outside a transaction");
            return false;
        }
        if !enrol_current_thread() {
            return false;
        }
        let status = ffi::DetourDetach(target, detour);
        if status != ffi::NO_ERROR {
            LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("DetourDetach failed (status={}, target={:p})", status, target);
            return false;
        }
        true
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        let _ = (target, detour);
        false
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn enrol_current_thread() -> bool {
    if THREAD_ENROLLED.with(|c| c.get()) {
        return true;
    }
    let h = crate::platform::thread::current_native_thread_handle();
    let status = unsafe { ffi::DetourUpdateThread(h) };
    if status != ffi::NO_ERROR {
        LOG_PLATFORM_WARN!("DetourUpdateThread failed (status={})", status);
        return false;
    }
    THREAD_ENROLLED.with(|c| c.set(true));
    true
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    // Detours transactions are per-thread. The Rust test harness runs
    // each test on its own thread, so the thread-local state is clean
    // at entry. A serial mutex guards the tests that touch Detours
    // itself, because some Detours calls assume process-wide state.
    static SERIAL: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());

    fn reset_thread_state() {
        IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.set(false));
        THREAD_ENROLLED.with(|c| c.set(false));
    }

    #[test]
    fn commit_without_begin_fails() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        assert!(!commit_transaction());
    }

    #[test]
    fn abort_without_begin_fails() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        assert!(!abort_transaction());
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn begin_commit_roundtrip() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        assert!(begin_transaction());
        assert!(IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()));
        assert!(commit_transaction());
        assert!(!IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()));
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn begin_is_idempotent() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        assert!(begin_transaction());
        assert!(begin_transaction());
        assert!(commit_transaction());
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn abort_clears_state() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        assert!(begin_transaction());
        assert!(abort_transaction());
        assert!(!IN_TRANSACTION.with(|c| c.get()));
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn commit_after_commit_fails() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        assert!(begin_transaction());
        assert!(commit_transaction());
        // No transaction is open now.
        assert!(!commit_transaction());
    }

    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    #[test]
    fn non_windows_begin_fails() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        assert!(!begin_transaction());
    }

    #[test]
    fn attach_with_null_target_returns_false() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        let ok = unsafe { attach(std::ptr::null_mut(), 0x1234 as *mut c_void) };
        assert!(!ok);
    }

    #[test]
    fn attach_with_null_detour_returns_false() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        let mut target: *mut c_void = 0x1000 as *mut c_void;
        let ok = unsafe { attach(&mut target, std::ptr::null_mut()) };
        assert!(!ok);
    }

    #[test]
    fn attach_outside_transaction_returns_false() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        let mut target: *mut c_void = 0x1000 as *mut c_void;
        let ok = unsafe { attach(&mut target, 0x2000 as *mut c_void) };
        assert!(!ok);
    }

    #[test]
    fn detach_outside_transaction_returns_false() {
        let _g = SERIAL.lock().unwrap();
        reset_thread_state();
        let mut target: *mut c_void = 0x1000 as *mut c_void;
        let ok = unsafe { detach(&mut target, 0x2000 as *mut c_void) };
        assert!(!ok);
    }
}
