//! Modal message boxes. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Dialog.cpp`
//!
//! Uses `MessageBoxA` with `MB_TOPMOST`, matching the C++ (Steam's
//! overlay can cover a non-topmost box).

/// Modal warning box (OK, warning icon).
pub fn show_warning(title: &str, message: &str) {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    message_box(title, message, MB_OK | MB_ICONWARNING);
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        let _ = (title, message);
    }
}

/// Modal information box (OK, info icon). Blocks until dismissed.
pub fn show_info(title: &str, message: &str) {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    message_box(title, message, MB_OK | MB_ICONINFORMATION);
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        let _ = (title, message);
    }
}

/// Modal Yes/No confirmation. Returns true when the user chose Yes.
pub fn show_confirm(title: &str, message: &str) -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let r = message_box(title, message, MB_YESNO | MB_ICONINFORMATION);
        r == IDYES
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        let _ = (title, message);
        false
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{
    MessageBoxA, IDYES, MB_ICONINFORMATION, MB_ICONWARNING, MB_OK, MB_TOPMOST, MB_YESNO,
};

#[cfg(windows)]
fn message_box(title: &str, message: &str, flags: u32) -> i32 {
    use std::ffi::CString;
    let t = CString::new(title).unwrap_or_default();
    let m = CString::new(message).unwrap_or_default();
    unsafe {
        MessageBoxA(
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            m.as_ptr() as *const u8,
            t.as_ptr() as *const u8,
            flags | MB_TOPMOST,
        )
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    // We do not pop modal dialogs in tests - they would hang the test
    // runner. These tests only verify the functions are callable.

    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    #[test]
    fn stubs_are_callable() {
        show_warning("t", "m");
        show_info("t", "m");
        assert!(!show_confirm("t", "m"));
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\directory_watch.rs =====
//! Directory change notifications. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/DirectoryWatch.cpp`
//!
//! `Watch` is an opaque handle wrapping:
//!   * a directory handle opened with `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`
//!   * an event for the overlapped read
//!   * a `Vec<u8>` for `FILE_NOTIFY_INFORMATION` records
//!   * a pending-read flag
//!
//! `wait_any` blocks on the event handles via `WaitForMultipleObjects`.

use std::path::PathBuf;

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ChangeAction {
    Added,
    Removed,
    Modified,
    RenamedOldName,
    RenamedNewName,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Change {
    pub relative_path: String,
    pub action: ChangeAction,
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WaitStatus { Signaled, Timeout, Failed }

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct WaitResult {
    pub status: WaitStatus,
    pub index: usize,
}

// ─── Watch handle ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct Watch {
    directory: Option<PathBuf>,
    imp: imp::WatchImpl,
}

impl Watch {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { directory: None, imp: imp::WatchImpl::new() }
    }

    pub fn open(&mut self, directory: &str, buffer_size: u32) -> bool {
        self.directory = Some(PathBuf::from(directory));
        self.imp.open(directory, buffer_size)
    }

    pub fn issue_read(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.imp.issue_read()
    }

    pub fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<Change> {
        self.imp.drain()
    }

    pub fn cancel(&mut self) {
        self.imp.cancel();
        self.directory = None;
    }

    pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool { self.imp.is_open() }
    pub fn directory(&self) -> &str {
        self.directory.as_ref().and_then(|p| p.to_str()).unwrap_or("")
    }

    pub(super) fn native_event(&self) -> imp::NativeEvent { self.imp.native_event() }
}

impl Default for Watch {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }
}

// ─── Windows implementation ─────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use std::ffi::c_void;
    use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{
        CloseHandle, GetLastError, HANDLE, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, WAIT_OBJECT_0, WAIT_TIMEOUT,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::Storage::FileSystem::{
        CreateFileW, ReadDirectoryChangesW, FILE_ACTION_ADDED, FILE_ACTION_MODIFIED,
        FILE_ACTION_REMOVED, FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_NEW_NAME, FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_OLD_NAME,
        FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS, FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY, FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME,
        FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_WRITE, FILE_NOTIFY_INFORMATION, FILE_SHARE_DELETE, FILE_SHARE_READ,
        FILE_SHARE_WRITE, OPEN_EXISTING,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::IO::{CancelIoEx, GetOverlappedResult, OVERLAPPED};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{CreateEventW, ResetEvent, WaitForMultipleObjects};

    pub(super) type NativeEvent = HANDLE;

    fn to_wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        std::ffi::OsStr::new(s).encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    fn from_wide(units: &[u16]) -> String {
        String::from_utf16_lossy(units)
    }

    fn from_windows_action(a: u32) -> ChangeAction {
        match a {
            x if x == FILE_ACTION_ADDED => ChangeAction::Added,
            x if x == FILE_ACTION_REMOVED => ChangeAction::Removed,
            x if x == FILE_ACTION_MODIFIED => ChangeAction::Modified,
            x if x == FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_OLD_NAME => ChangeAction::RenamedOldName,
            x if x == FILE_ACTION_RENAMED_NEW_NAME => ChangeAction::RenamedNewName,
            _ => ChangeAction::Modified,
        }
    }

    pub(super) struct WatchImpl {
        dir: HANDLE,
        event: HANDLE,
        overlapped: OVERLAPPED,
        buffer: Vec<u8>,
        read_pending: bool,
    }

    unsafe impl Send for WatchImpl {}

    impl WatchImpl {
        pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
            Self {
                dir: std::ptr::null_mut(),
                event: std::ptr::null_mut(),
                overlapped: unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() },
                buffer: Vec::new(),
                read_pending: false,
            }
        }

        pub(super) fn open(&mut self, directory: &str, buffer_size: u32) -> bool {
            self.close();

            let event = unsafe { CreateEventW(std::ptr::null(), 1, 0, std::ptr::null()) };
            if event.is_null() {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "DirectoryWatch: CreateEvent failed for '{}' (error={})",
                    directory,
                    unsafe { GetLastError() }
                );
                return false;
            }
            self.event = event;

            let native = to_wide(directory);
            let dir = unsafe {
                CreateFileW(
                    native.as_ptr(),
                    FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY,
                    FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE,
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    OPEN_EXISTING,
                    FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED,
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                )
            };
            if dir == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "DirectoryWatch: CreateFile failed for '{}' (error={})",
                    directory,
                    unsafe { GetLastError() }
                );
                self.close();
                return false;
            }
            self.dir = dir;

            self.buffer = vec![0u8; buffer_size as usize];
            self.overlapped = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            self.overlapped.hEvent = event;
            true
        }

        pub(super) fn issue_read(&mut self) -> bool {
            if !self.is_open() { return false; }
            if self.read_pending { return true; }

            let event = self.event;
            self.overlapped = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            self.overlapped.hEvent = event;

            let mut dummy: u32 = 0;
            let ok = unsafe {
                ReadDirectoryChangesW(
                    self.dir,
                    self.buffer.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
                    self.buffer.len() as u32,
                    0,
                    FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME | FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_WRITE,
                    &mut dummy,
                    &mut self.overlapped,
                    None,
                )
            };
            if ok == 0 {
                let err = unsafe { GetLastError() };
                // ERROR_IO_PENDING (997) means the async op is queued
                // successfully; anything else is a real failure.
                const ERROR_IO_PENDING: u32 = 997;
                if err != ERROR_IO_PENDING {
                    crate::ostp_warn!("DirectoryWatch: ReadDirectoryChangesW failed (error={})", err);
                    self.read_pending = false;
                    return false;
                }
            }
            self.read_pending = true;
            true
        }

        pub(super) fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<Change> {
            let mut changes = Vec::new();
            if !self.is_open() || !self.read_pending { return changes; }

            let mut bytes_returned: u32 = 0;
            let ok = unsafe {
                GetOverlappedResult(self.dir, &self.overlapped, &mut bytes_returned, 0)
            };
            if ok == 0 || bytes_returned == 0 {
                self.read_pending = false;
                return changes;
            }
            self.read_pending = false;

            // Walk the FILE_NOTIFY_INFORMATION chain.
            let mut offset = 0usize;
            let base = self.buffer.as_ptr();
            loop {
                if offset + std::mem::size_of::<FILE_NOTIFY_INFORMATION>() > self.buffer.len() {
                    break;
                }
                let info = unsafe { &*(base.add(offset) as *const FILE_NOTIFY_INFORMATION) };
                let chars = (info.FileNameLength / 2) as usize;
                let name_slice = unsafe {
                    std::slice::from_raw_parts(info.FileName.as_ptr() as *const u16, chars)
                };
                let relative_path = from_wide(name_slice);
                if !relative_path.is_empty() {
                    changes.push(Change {
                        relative_path,
                        action: from_windows_action(info.Action),
                    });
                }
                if info.NextEntryOffset == 0 { break; }
                offset += info.NextEntryOffset as usize;
            }
            changes
        }

        pub(super) fn cancel(&mut self) {
            self.close();
        }

        pub(super) fn is_open(&self) -> bool {
            !self.dir.is_null() && !self.event.is_null()
        }

        pub(super) fn native_event(&self) -> HANDLE { self.event }

        fn close(&mut self) {
            if !self.dir.is_null() {
                unsafe { CancelIoEx(self.dir, std::ptr::null()); }
            }
            if !self.dir.is_null() && self.dir != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE {
                unsafe { CloseHandle(self.dir); }
            }
            if !self.event.is_null() {
                unsafe { CloseHandle(self.event); }
            }
            self.dir = std::ptr::null_mut();
            self.event = std::ptr::null_mut();
            self.overlapped = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            self.buffer.clear();
            self.read_pending = false;
        }
    }

    impl Drop for WatchImpl {
        fn drop(&mut self) { self.close(); }
    }

    pub(super) fn wait_any(watches: &mut [&mut Watch], timeout_ms: u32) -> WaitResult {
        let mut events: Vec<HANDLE> = Vec::with_capacity(watches.len());
        let mut indexes: Vec<usize> = Vec::with_capacity(watches.len());
        for (i, w) in watches.iter().enumerate() {
            if !w.is_open() { continue; }
            events.push(w.native_event());
            indexes.push(i);
        }
        if events.is_empty() {
            return WaitResult { status: WaitStatus::Failed, index: 0 };
        }

        let n = events.len() as u32;
        let result = unsafe {
            WaitForMultipleObjects(n, events.as_ptr(), 0, timeout_ms)
        };
        if result == WAIT_TIMEOUT {
            return WaitResult { status: WaitStatus::Timeout, index: 0 };
        }
        if result >= WAIT_OBJECT_0 && result < WAIT_OBJECT_0 + n {
            let idx = (result - WAIT_OBJECT_0) as usize;
            return WaitResult { status: WaitStatus::Signaled, index: indexes[idx] };
        }
        crate::ostp_warn!("DirectoryWatch: WaitForMultipleObjects failed (result={})", result);
        let _ = ResetEvent; // silence unused
        WaitResult { status: WaitStatus::Failed, index: 0 }
    }
}

    pub(super) type NativeEvent = *mut c_void;

    pub(super) struct WatchImpl;
    impl WatchImpl {
        pub(super) fn new() -> Self { Self }
        pub(super) fn open(&mut self, _d: &str, _b: u32) -> bool { false }
        pub(super) fn issue_read(&mut self) -> bool { false }

        pub(super) fn native_event(&self) -> NativeEvent { std::ptr::null_mut() }
    }

        WaitResult { status: WaitStatus::Failed, index: 0 }
    }
}

pub fn wait_any(watches: &mut [&mut Watch], timeout_ms: u32) -> WaitResult {
    imp::wait_any(watches, timeout_ms)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn new_watch_is_not_open() {
        let w = Watch::new();
        assert!(!w.is_open());
        assert_eq!(w.directory(), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancel_clears_state() {
        let mut w = Watch::new();
        let _ = w.open("C:\\temp", 4096);
        w.cancel();
        assert!(!w.is_open());
        assert_eq!(w.directory(), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn drain_empty_when_not_opened() {
        let mut w = Watch::new();
        assert!(w.drain().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn change_action_equality() {
        assert_eq!(ChangeAction::Added, ChangeAction::Added);
        assert_ne!(ChangeAction::Added, ChangeAction::Removed);
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn open_existing_directory_succeeds() {
        let sysdir = crate::platform::dynamic_library::get_system_directory_path();
        if sysdir.is_empty() { return; }
        let mut w = Watch::new();
        assert!(w.open(&sysdir, 4096));
        assert!(w.is_open());
        w.cancel();
        assert!(!w.is_open());
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn issue_read_then_cancel() {
        let sysdir = crate::platform::dynamic_library::get_system_directory_path();
        if sysdir.is_empty() { return; }
        let mut w = Watch::new();
        assert!(w.open(&sysdir, 4096));
        assert!(w.issue_read());
        w.cancel();
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\dynamic_library.rs =====
//! Dynamic library loading. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/DynamicLibrary.cpp`
//!
//! Real Win32 implementation via `windows-sys`.
//!
//! ## Argument-order divergence in Win32
//!
//! `GetCurrentDirectoryW` and `GetSystemDirectoryW` take the same two
//! arguments in the opposite order:
//!   GetCurrentDirectoryW(capacity, buffer)
//!   GetSystemDirectoryW(buffer, capacity)
//!
//! The C++ header hides this with two thunks. We do the same here with
//! `get_current_directory_w_thunk` and `get_system_directory_w_thunk`.

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

#[repr(transparent)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ModuleHandle(pub *mut c_void);

impl ModuleHandle {
    pub const fn null() -> Self { Self(std::ptr::null_mut()) }
    pub fn is_null(&self) -> bool { self.0.is_null() }
}

// SAFETY: an `HMODULE` is a process-global loader handle. Windows
// documentation permits it to be passed between threads; the loader
// serialises map/unmap operations internally, and the value itself
// carries no thread affinity. The default `!Send` / `!Sync` come only
// from the raw pointer field. CloudRedirect's host registry stores a
// `ModuleHandle` in a `Mutex<...>` static, which requires this.
unsafe impl Send for ModuleHandle {}
unsafe impl Sync for ModuleHandle {}

impl Default for ModuleHandle {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::null() }
}

// ─── Windows implementation ──────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::MAX_PATH;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Environment::GetCurrentDirectoryW;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::{
        GetModuleFileNameW, GetModuleHandleW, GetProcAddress, LoadLibraryW,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::SystemInformation::GetSystemDirectoryW;

    const MAX_WIN32_PATH_BUFFER: u32 = 32768;

    fn path_to_wide_null(p: &Path) -> Vec<u16> {
        p.as_os_str().encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    fn str_to_wide_null(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    fn wide_to_string(buf: &[u16]) -> String {
        String::from_utf16_lossy(buf)
    }

    pub(super) fn load(path: &Path) -> ModuleHandle {
        let wide = path_to_wide_null(path);
        let h = unsafe { LoadLibraryW(wide.as_ptr()) };
        if h.is_null() {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "LoadLibraryW('{}') failed (error={})",
                path.display(),
                get_last_error_code()
            );
        }
        ModuleHandle(h as *mut c_void)
    }

    pub(super) fn get_loaded(module_name: &str) -> ModuleHandle {
        let wide = str_to_wide_null(module_name);
        let h = unsafe { GetModuleHandleW(wide.as_ptr()) };
        ModuleHandle(h as *mut c_void)
    }

    pub(super) unsafe fn get_symbol(module: ModuleHandle, symbol_name: &str) -> *mut c_void {
        if module.0.is_null() { return std::ptr::null_mut(); }
        let name = std::ffi::CString::new(symbol_name).unwrap_or_default();
        let f = GetProcAddress(module.0 as _, name.as_ptr() as *const u8);
        match f {
            Some(f) => f as *mut c_void,
            None => {
                crate::ostp_debug!(
                    "GetProcAddress('{}') failed (error={})",
                    symbol_name,
                    get_last_error_code()
                );
                std::ptr::null_mut()
            }
        }
    }

    pub(super) unsafe fn get_symbol_ordinal(module: ModuleHandle, ordinal: u16) -> *mut c_void {
        if module.0.is_null() { return std::ptr::null_mut(); }
        let ord_ptr = ordinal as usize as *const u8;
        let f = GetProcAddress(module.0 as _, ord_ptr);
        match f {
            Some(f) => f as *mut c_void,
            None => {
                crate::ostp_debug!(
                    "GetProcAddress(ordinal={}) failed (error={})",
                    ordinal,
                    get_last_error_code()
                );
                std::ptr::null_mut()
            }
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn get_last_error_code() -> u32 {
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::GetLastError() }
    }

    fn module_file_path(module: *mut c_void, operation: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let mut capacity: u32 = MAX_PATH;
        while capacity <= MAX_WIN32_PATH_BUFFER {
            let mut buf = vec![0u16; capacity as usize];
            unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::SetLastError(0); }
            let len = unsafe { GetModuleFileNameW(module as _, buf.as_mut_ptr(), capacity) };
            if len == 0 {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "{}: GetModuleFileNameW failed (error={})",
                    operation,
                    get_last_error_code()
                );
                return PathBuf::new();
            }
            if len < capacity {
                return PathBuf::from(wide_to_string(&buf[..len as usize]));
            }
            capacity = capacity.saturating_mul(2);
        }
        crate::ostp_warn!(
            "{}: GetModuleFileNameW path exceeds {} wchars",
            operation,
            MAX_WIN32_PATH_BUFFER
        );
        PathBuf::new()
    }

    // ── Directory thunks ─────────────────────────────────────────
    // Normalise both APIs to the (capacity, buffer) shape so a single
    // loop handles them. Matches the C++ thunk pattern.

    unsafe extern "system" fn get_current_directory_w_thunk(
        capacity: u32,
        buffer: *mut u16,
    ) -> u32 {
        GetCurrentDirectoryW(capacity, buffer)
    }

    unsafe extern "system" fn get_system_directory_w_thunk(
        capacity: u32,
        buffer: *mut u16,
    ) -> u32 {
        // Note the reversed order - GetSystemDirectoryW takes (buffer, capacity).
        GetSystemDirectoryW(buffer, capacity)
    }

    fn directory_from_query(
        query: unsafe extern "system" fn(u32, *mut u16) -> u32,
        operation: &str,
    ) -> String {
        let mut capacity: u32 = MAX_PATH;
        while capacity <= MAX_WIN32_PATH_BUFFER {
            let mut buf = vec![0u16; capacity as usize];
            let len = unsafe { query(capacity, buf.as_mut_ptr()) };
            if len == 0 {
                crate::ostp_warn!("{} failed (error={})", operation, get_last_error_code());
                return String::new();
            }
            if len < capacity {
                return wide_to_string(&buf[..len as usize]);
            }
            capacity = if len > capacity { len } else { capacity.saturating_mul(2) };
        }
        crate::ostp_warn!(
            "{} path exceeds {} wchars",
            operation,
            MAX_WIN32_PATH_BUFFER
        );
        String::new()
    }

    pub(super) fn get_current_directory_path() -> String {
        directory_from_query(get_current_directory_w_thunk, "GetCurrentDirectoryW")
    }

    pub(super) fn get_system_directory_path() -> String {
        directory_from_query(get_system_directory_w_thunk, "GetSystemDirectoryW")
    }

    pub(super) fn get_module_directory(module: ModuleHandle) -> PathBuf {
        module_file_path(module.0, "GetModuleDirectory")
            .parent()
            .map(|p| p.to_path_buf())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    pub(super) fn get_main_executable_path() -> PathBuf {
        module_file_path(std::ptr::null_mut(), "GetMainExecutablePath")
    }
}

    pub(super) fn get_loaded(_module_name: &str) -> ModuleHandle { ModuleHandle::null() }
    pub(super) unsafe fn get_symbol(_m: ModuleHandle, _s: &str) -> *mut c_void { std::ptr::null_mut() }
    pub(super) unsafe fn get_symbol_ordinal(_m: ModuleHandle, _o: u16) -> *mut c_void { std::ptr::null_mut() }
    pub(super) fn get_last_error_code() -> u32 { 0 }
    pub(super) fn get_current_directory_path() -> String { String::new() }

===== FILE: src\platform\encoding.rs =====
//! Wide <-> UTF-8 conversions. Source: `OSTPlatform/Encoding.cpp`
//!
//! The C++ version calls `WideCharToMultiByte` / `MultiByteToWideChar`
//! with `CP_UTF8` and default flags. In that mode, invalid input is
//! substituted with U+FFFD rather than rejected. Rust's
//! `String::from_utf16_lossy` and `str::encode_utf16` behave identically
//! without the FFI hop, so no `windows` crate binding is needed here.
//!
//! The C++ returns an empty string on failure. Its failure modes are
//! API-level (null pointers, oversized length) rather than content-based;
//! only the length guard survives the port. All other inputs succeed.

use crate::ostp_debug;
use crate::platform::logging::Level;

/// A UTF-16 wide string. On Windows `wchar_t` is 16 bits, one `u16`
/// per code unit.
pub type Wide = [u16];

/// Maximum length, matching the C++ guard against `int` overflow in the
/// Win32 length parameter. `WideCharToMultiByte` takes an `int` count,
/// so inputs above `INT_MAX` would be truncated silently.
const MAX_LEN: usize = i32::MAX as usize;

/// Convert a UTF-16 slice to a UTF-8 `String`.
///
/// Unpaired surrogates become U+FFFD, matching `WideCharToMultiByte` with
/// `CP_UTF8` and no `WC_ERR_INVALID_CHARS` flag.
pub fn wide_to_utf8(value: &[u16]) -> String {
    if value.is_empty() {
        return String::new();
    }
    if value.len() > MAX_LEN {
        ostp_debug!("wide_to_utf8: input too large ({} code units)", value.len());
        return String::new();
    }
    String::from_utf16_lossy(value)
}

/// Convert a UTF-8 `&str` to a UTF-16 `Vec<u16>`.
///
/// Rust `&str` is always valid UTF-8, so this never fails on content.
pub fn utf8_to_wide(value: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
    if value.is_empty() {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    if value.len() > MAX_LEN {
        ostp_debug!("utf8_to_wide: input too large ({} bytes)", value.len());
        return Vec::new();
    }
    value.encode_utf16().collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn empty_roundtrip() {
        assert_eq!(wide_to_utf8(&[]), "");
        assert_eq!(utf8_to_wide(""), Vec::<u16>::new());
    }

    #[test]
    fn ascii_roundtrip() {
        let s = "hello world";
        let w = utf8_to_wide(s);
        assert_eq!(w.len(), s.len()); // ASCII: 1 byte = 1 code unit
        assert_eq!(wide_to_utf8(&w), s);
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_ascii_roundtrip() {
        // 'é' = 1 BMP unit, '日' = 1 BMP unit, '🦀' = 1 surrogate pair
        let s = "caf\u{00E9} \u{2014} \u{65E5}\u{672C}\u{8A9E} \u{2014} \u{1F980}";
        let w = utf8_to_wide(s);
        assert_eq!(wide_to_utf8(&w), s);
        // c a f é (4) + ' — ' (3) + 日本語 (3) + ' — ' (3) + 🦀 (2) = 15
        assert_eq!(w.len(), 15);
    }

    #[test]
    fn lone_high_surrogate_becomes_replacement() {
        // Unpaired D800. C++ substitutes U+FFFD.
        let wide = [0xD800u16, 0x0041, 0x0042];
        let utf8 = wide_to_utf8(&wide);
        assert!(utf8.starts_with('\u{FFFD}'));
        assert!(utf8.ends_with("AB"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn lone_low_surrogate_becomes_replacement() {
        let wide = [0xDC00u16, 0x0041];
        let utf8 = wide_to_utf8(&wide);
        assert!(utf8.starts_with('\u{FFFD}'));
    }

    #[test]
    fn valid_surrogate_pair_preserved() {
        let wide = [0xD83Du16, 0xDE00u16]; // U+1F600
        assert_eq!(wide_to_utf8(&wide), "\u{1F600}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_utf16_input_gives_empty_string() {
        assert_eq!(wide_to_utf8(&[]), "");
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\hash.rs =====
//! SHA-256. Source: `OSTPlatform/include/Hash.h`
//!
//! The C++ uses BCrypt. Rust's `sha2` crate produces byte-identical
//! digests, and the implementation is portable. The chunked read loop
//! matches the C++ exactly (64 KiB per read).

use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Read;
use std::path::Path;

/// Lower-case hex SHA-256 of a file, or `""` on failure.
pub fn sha256_of_file(path: &Path) -> String {
    let mut file = match File::open(path) {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(_) => return String::new(),
    };
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    let mut buf = [0u8; 65536];
    loop {
        match file.read(&mut buf) {
            Ok(0) => break,
            Ok(n) => hasher.update(&buf[..n]),
            Err(_) => return String::new(),
        }
    }
    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
}

/// Lower-case hex SHA-256 of a buffer.
pub fn sha256_of_buffer(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(data);
    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn buffer_empty_matches_known_value() {
        // SHA-256 of the empty string.
        assert_eq!(
            sha256_of_buffer(b""),
            "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn buffer_abc_matches_known_value() {
        assert_eq!(
            sha256_of_buffer(b"abc"),
            "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn buffer_long_input() {
        // 1 MiB of 0x00. Known SHA-256 value.
        let data = vec![0u8; 1024 * 1024];
        assert_eq!(
            sha256_of_buffer(&data),
            "30e14955ebf1352266dc2ff8067e68104607e750abb9d3b36582b8af909fcb58"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_missing_returns_empty() {
        assert_eq!(sha256_of_file(Path::new("does-not-exist-xyz")), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_of_abc() {
        let tmp = std::env::temp_dir().join("ost_hash_test_abc.bin");
        std::fs::write(&tmp, b"abc").unwrap();
        let h = sha256_of_file(&tmp);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
        assert_eq!(h, "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad");
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\http.rs =====
//! WinHTTP wrapper. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Http.cpp`

use std::ffi::c_void;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Result {
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
    pub status: u32,
    pub ok: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Request<'a> {
    pub method: &'a str,
    pub url: &'a str,
    pub body: Option<&'a [u8]>,
    pub headers: Option<&'a str>,
    pub timeout_resolve_ms: u32,
    pub timeout_connect_ms: u32,
    pub timeout_send_ms: u32,
    pub timeout_recv_ms: u32,
    pub max_body_bytes: u32,
}

impl<'a> Request<'a> {
    pub fn new(method: &'a str, url: &'a str) -> Self {
        Self {
            method,
            url,
            body: None,
            headers: None,
            timeout_resolve_ms: 5000,
            timeout_connect_ms: 5000,
            timeout_send_ms: 10000,
            timeout_recv_ms: 10000,
            max_body_bytes: 256 * 1024,
        }
    }
}

// ─── Windows implementation ─────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use std::ffi::OsStr;
    use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinHttp::{
        WinHttpAddRequestHeaders, WinHttpCloseHandle, WinHttpConnect, WinHttpOpen,
        WinHttpOpenRequest, WinHttpQueryDataAvailable, WinHttpQueryHeaders, WinHttpReadData,
        WinHttpReceiveResponse, WinHttpSendRequest, WinHttpSetOption, WinHttpSetTimeouts,
        WINHTTP_ACCESS_TYPE_DEFAULT_PROXY, WINHTTP_FLAG_SECURE, WINHTTP_QUERY_FLAG_NUMBER,
        WINHTTP_QUERY_STATUS_CODE,
    };

    // All of these are NULL-pointer constants in the Win32 SDK that
    // windows-sys does not re-export as named items.
    const WINHTTP_NO_PROXY_NAME: *const u16 = std::ptr::null();
    const WINHTTP_NO_PROXY_BYPASS: *const u16 = std::ptr::null();
    const WINHTTP_NO_REFERER: *const u16 = std::ptr::null();
    const WINHTTP_NO_ADDITIONAL_HEADERS: *const u16 = std::ptr::null();
    const WINHTTP_DEFAULT_ACCEPT_TYPES: *const *const u16 = std::ptr::null();
    const WINHTTP_HEADER_NAME_BY_INDEX: *const u16 = std::ptr::null();
    const WINHTTP_NO_HEADER_INDEX: *mut u32 = std::ptr::null_mut();

    const INTERNET_DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT: u16 = 80;
    const INTERNET_DEFAULT_HTTPS_PORT: u16 = 443;

    const WINHTTP_OPTION_DECOMPRESSION: u32 = 118;
    const WINHTTP_DECOMPRESSION_FLAG_GZIP: u32 = 0x00000001;
    const WINHTTP_DECOMPRESSION_FLAG_DEFLATE: u32 = 0x00000002;

    fn to_wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        OsStr::new(s).encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    struct ParsedUrl {
        host: Vec<u16>,
        path: Vec<u16>,
        port: u16,
        tls: bool,
        valid: bool,
    }

    fn parse_url(raw: &str) -> ParsedUrl {
        let mut out = ParsedUrl { host: Vec::new(), path: Vec::new(), port: 0, tls: false, valid: false };
        let (tls, rest) = if let Some(r) = raw.strip_prefix("https://") {
            (true, r)
        } else if let Some(r) = raw.strip_prefix("http://") {
            (false, r)
        } else {
            return out;
        };
        out.tls = tls;
        out.port = if tls { INTERNET_DEFAULT_HTTPS_PORT } else { INTERNET_DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT };

        let slash = rest.find('/').unwrap_or(rest.len());
        let host_part = &rest[..slash];
        let path_part = if slash < rest.len() { &rest[slash..] } else { "/" };
        out.path = to_wide(path_part);

        if let Some(colon) = host_part.find(':') {
            out.host = to_wide(&host_part[..colon]);
            if let Ok(p) = host_part[colon + 1..].parse::<u16>() {
                if p != 0 { out.port = p; }
            }
        } else {
            out.host = to_wide(host_part);
        }

        out.valid = !out.host.is_empty();
        out
    }

    pub(super) fn execute(req: &Request<'_>) -> Result {
        let mut r = Result { body: Vec::new(), status: 0, ok: false };

        let pu = parse_url(req.url);
        if !pu.valid {
            crate::ostp_warn!("Invalid URL: {}", req.url);
            return r;
        }

        unsafe {
            let h_session = WinHttpOpen(
                to_wide("OpenSteamTool/1.0").as_ptr(),
                WINHTTP_ACCESS_TYPE_DEFAULT_PROXY,
                WINHTTP_NO_PROXY_NAME,
                WINHTTP_NO_PROXY_BYPASS,
                0,
            );
            if h_session.is_null() {
                crate::ostp_warn!("{} - WinHttpOpen failed", req.url);
                return r;
            }

            WinHttpSetTimeouts(
                h_session,
                req.timeout_resolve_ms as i32,
                req.timeout_connect_ms as i32,
                req.timeout_send_ms as i32,
                req.timeout_recv_ms as i32,
            );

            {
                let mut flag: u32 =
                    WINHTTP_DECOMPRESSION_FLAG_GZIP | WINHTTP_DECOMPRESSION_FLAG_DEFLATE;
                let _ = WinHttpSetOption(
                    h_session,
                    WINHTTP_OPTION_DECOMPRESSION,
                    &mut flag as *mut _ as *mut c_void,
                    std::mem::size_of::<u32>() as u32,
                );
            }

            let h_connect = WinHttpConnect(h_session, pu.host.as_ptr(), pu.port, 0);
            if h_connect.is_null() {
                crate::ostp_warn!("{} - WinHttpConnect failed", req.url);
                WinHttpCloseHandle(h_session);
                return r;
            }

            let flags = if pu.tls { WINHTTP_FLAG_SECURE } else { 0 };
            let method_wide = to_wide(req.method);
            let h_request = WinHttpOpenRequest(
                h_connect,
                method_wide.as_ptr(),
                pu.path.as_ptr(),
                std::ptr::null(),
                WINHTTP_NO_REFERER,
                WINHTTP_DEFAULT_ACCEPT_TYPES,
                flags,
            );
            if h_request.is_null() {
                crate::ostp_warn!("{} - WinHttpOpenRequest failed", req.url);
                WinHttpCloseHandle(h_connect);
                WinHttpCloseHandle(h_session);
                return r;
            }

            if let Some(hdr) = req.headers {
                if !hdr.is_empty() {
                    let hdr_wide: Vec<u16> = OsStr::new(hdr).encode_wide().collect();
                    let _ = WinHttpAddRequestHeaders(
                        h_request,
                        hdr_wide.as_ptr(),
                        hdr_wide.len() as u32,
                        0x2000_0000 | 0x1000_0000,
                    );
                }
            }

            let body_ptr = req.body.map(|b| b.as_ptr()).unwrap_or(std::ptr::null());
            let body_len = req.body.map(|b| b.len()).unwrap_or(0) as u32;

            let send_ok = WinHttpSendRequest(
                h_request,
                WINHTTP_NO_ADDITIONAL_HEADERS,
                0,
                body_ptr as *const c_void,
                body_len,
                body_len,
                0,
            );
            if send_ok == 0 {
                crate::ostp_warn!("{} - WinHttpSendRequest failed", req.url);
            } else if WinHttpReceiveResponse(h_request, std::ptr::null_mut()) == 0 {
                crate::ostp_warn!("{} - WinHttpReceiveResponse failed", req.url);
            } else {
                let mut status: u32 = 0;
                let mut sz = std::mem::size_of::<u32>() as u32;
                let _ = WinHttpQueryHeaders(
                    h_request,
                    WINHTTP_QUERY_STATUS_CODE | WINHTTP_QUERY_FLAG_NUMBER,
                    WINHTTP_HEADER_NAME_BY_INDEX,
                    &mut status as *mut u32 as *mut c_void,
                    &mut sz,
                    WINHTTP_NO_HEADER_INDEX,
                );
                r.status = status;

                loop {
                    let mut avail: u32 = 0;
                    if WinHttpQueryDataAvailable(h_request, &mut avail) == 0 { break; }
                    if avail == 0 { break; }

                    let off = r.body.len();
                    r.body.resize(off + avail as usize, 0);
                    let mut read: u32 = 0;
                    if WinHttpReadData(
                        h_request,
                        r.body[off..].as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
                        avail,
                        &mut read,
                    ) == 0
                    {
                        r.body.truncate(off);
                        break;
                    }
                    r.body.truncate(off + read as usize);
                    if r.body.len() >= req.max_body_bytes as usize { break; }
                }
                r.ok = true;
            }

            WinHttpCloseHandle(h_request);
            WinHttpCloseHandle(h_connect);
            WinHttpCloseHandle(h_session);
        }

        r
    }
}

===== FILE: src\platform\logging.rs =====
//! Logging facade. Source: `OSTPlatform/Log.cpp` + `include/Log.h`
//!
//! The C++ facade is a plain function-pointer sink installed by the host,
//! stored in a `std::atomic<Sink>` with acquire/release ordering. We use an
//! `Arc<dyn Fn>` behind an `RwLock` - reads are cheap, writes are once at
//! init, and the callback can be a closure rather than a bare fn pointer.
//!
//! Six convenience macros mirror the C++ `OSTP_LOG_TRACE`..`OSTP_LOG_ERROR`
//! family. The `ostp_log!` macro captures `file!()` / `line!()` at the call
//! site and formats the message eagerly.

use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock};

#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Level {
    Trace = 0,
    Debug = 1,
    Info  = 2,
    Warn  = 3,
    Error = 4,
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Source {
    pub file: &'static str,
    pub line: u32,
    pub function: &'static str,
}

pub type Sink = Arc<dyn Fn(Level, &Source, &str) + Send + Sync + 'static>;

static G_SINK: RwLock<Option<Sink>> = RwLock::new(None);

pub fn set_sink(sink: Sink) {
    *G_SINK.write().expect("log sink lock poisoned") = Some(sink);
}

pub fn clear_sink() {
    *G_SINK.write().expect("log sink lock poisoned") = None;
}

pub fn dispatch(level: Level, src: &Source, msg: &str) {
    // Clone the Arc out of the lock so the callback runs without holding it.
    let sink = G_SINK
        .read()
        .expect("log sink lock poisoned")
        .as_ref()
        .cloned();
    if let Some(sink) = sink {
        sink(level, src, msg);
    }
}

/// Generic dispatch macro. Captures source location; formats eagerly.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ostp_log {
    ($level:expr, $($arg:tt)*) => {
        $crate::platform::logging::dispatch(
            $level,
            &$crate::platform::logging::Source {
                file:     file!(),
                line:     line!(),
                function: "",
            },
            &format!($($arg)*),
        )
    };
}

#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ostp_trace {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { $crate::ostp_log!($crate::platform::logging::Level::Trace, $($arg)*) };
}

#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ostp_debug {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { $crate::ostp_log!($crate::platform::logging::Level::Debug, $($arg)*) };
}

#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ostp_info {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { $crate::ostp_log!($crate::platform::logging::Level::Info, $($arg)*) };
}

#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ostp_warn {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { $crate::ostp_log!($crate::platform::logging::Level::Warn, $($arg)*) };
}

#[macro_export]
macro_rules! ostp_error {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { $crate::ostp_log!($crate::platform::logging::Level::Error, $($arg)*) };
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    // Sink is a process-global. Serialise the tests that mutate it.
    static TEST_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());

    #[test]
    fn dispatch_without_sink_is_noop() {
        let _g = TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap();
        clear_sink();
        // Must not panic, must not do anything.
        dispatch(
            Level::Info,
            &Source { file: "x.rs", line: 1, function: "f" },
            "hello",
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sink_receives_messages() {
        let _g = TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap();
        clear_sink();

        let captured: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(Level, &'static str, String)>>> =
            Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let cap = captured.clone();

        set_sink(Arc::new(move |lvl, src, msg| {
            cap.lock().unwrap().push((lvl, src.file, msg.to_string()));
        }));

        dispatch(
            Level::Warn,
            &Source { file: "a.rs", line: 42, function: "f" },
            "warning text",
        );

        let log = captured.lock().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(log.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(log[0].0, Level::Warn);
        assert_eq!(log[0].1, "a.rs");
        assert_eq!(log[0].2, "warning text");

        clear_sink();
    }

    #[test]
    fn macro_fills_source_location() {
        let _g = TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap();
        clear_sink();

        let captured: Arc<Mutex<Option<(Level, &'static str, u32, String)>>> =
            Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
        let cap = captured.clone();

        set_sink(Arc::new(move |lvl, src, msg| {
            *cap.lock().unwrap() = Some((lvl, src.file, src.line, msg.to_string()));
        }));

        ostp_info!("value = {}", 42);

        let got = captured.lock().unwrap();
        let (lvl, file, _line, msg) = got.as_ref().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(*lvl, Level::Info);
        assert!(file.ends_with("logging.rs"));
        assert_eq!(msg, "value = 42");

        clear_sink();
    }

    #[test]
    fn clears_and_reinstalls() {
        let _g = TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap();
        clear_sink();

        let count: Arc<Mutex<u32>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(0));
        let c1 = count.clone();
        set_sink(Arc::new(move |_, _, _| { *c1.lock().unwrap() += 1; }));

        dispatch(Level::Info, &Source { file: "f", line: 1, function: "g" }, "a");
        assert_eq!(*count.lock().unwrap(), 1);

        clear_sink();
        dispatch(Level::Info, &Source { file: "f", line: 2, function: "g" }, "b");
        assert_eq!(*count.lock().unwrap(), 1); // unchanged

        let c2 = count.clone();
        set_sink(Arc::new(move |_, _, _| { *c2.lock().unwrap() += 10; }));
        dispatch(Level::Info, &Source { file: "f", line: 3, function: "g" }, "c");
        assert_eq!(*count.lock().unwrap(), 11);

        clear_sink();
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\memory.rs =====
//! In-process memory probing. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Memory.cpp`
//!
//! Three functions:
//!
//! * `get_module_image`  - base address and size of a loaded module.
//! * `write_executable_byte` - patch one byte in executable memory with
//!   the VirtualProtect dance and instruction-cache flush.
//! * `is_readable` - probe whether a byte range is committed and readable.
//!   Used before dereferencing a pointer of unknown provenance.
//!
//! The C++ `IsReadable` walks every region the range spans, because a
//! single VirtualQuery only describes the region containing the start
//! address. We do the same here.

use super::dynamic_library::ModuleHandle;
use std::ffi::c_void;

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ModuleImage {
    pub base: *mut u8,
    pub size: usize,
}

// ─── Windows implementation ─────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::FlushInstructionCache;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        VirtualProtect, VirtualQuery, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ,
        PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY, PAGE_GUARD, PAGE_NOCACHE, PAGE_READONLY,
        PAGE_READWRITE, PAGE_WRITECOMBINE, PAGE_WRITECOPY,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::ProcessStatus::{GetModuleInformation, MODULEINFO};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcess;

    pub(super) fn get_module_image(module: ModuleHandle) -> Option<ModuleImage> {
        if module.0.is_null() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut info: MODULEINFO = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let ok = unsafe {
            GetModuleInformation(
                GetCurrentProcess(),
                module.0,
                &mut info,
                std::mem::size_of::<MODULEINFO>() as u32,
            )
        };
        if ok == 0 {
            crate::ostp_debug!(
                "GetModuleInformation(module={:p}) failed (error={})",
                module.0,
                super::super::dynamic_library::get_last_error_code()
            );
            return None;
        }
        Some(ModuleImage {
            base: info.lpBaseOfDll as *mut u8,
            size: info.SizeOfImage as usize,
        })
    }

    pub(super) fn write_executable_byte(target: *mut c_void, value: u8) -> bool {
        if target.is_null() {
            crate::ostp_warn!("write_executable_byte: target is null");
            return false;
        }

        let mut old_protect: u32 = 0;
        let ok = unsafe { VirtualProtect(target, 1, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &mut old_protect) };
        if ok == 0 {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "write_executable_byte({:p}) VirtualProtect(RWX) failed (error={})",
                target,
                super::super::dynamic_library::get_last_error_code()
            );
            return false;
        }

        unsafe { *(target as *mut u8) = value };

        let mut ignored: u32 = 0;
        let ok2 = unsafe { VirtualProtect(target, 1, old_protect, &mut ignored) };
        if ok2 == 0 {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "write_executable_byte({:p}) VirtualProtect(restore=0x{:X}) failed (error={})",
                target,
                old_protect,
                super::super::dynamic_library::get_last_error_code()
            );
            return false;
        }

        let ok3 = unsafe { FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), target, 1) };
        if ok3 == 0 {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "write_executable_byte({:p}) FlushInstructionCache failed (error={})",
                target,
                super::super::dynamic_library::get_last_error_code()
            );
            return false;
        }

        true
    }

    /// Protections that permit a read. Bare `PAGE_EXECUTE` (execute-only)
    /// and `PAGE_NOACCESS` are deliberately excluded.
    fn is_readable_protect(protect: u32) -> bool {
        // Strip the modifier bits - they combine with the base protection.
        let base = protect & !(PAGE_GUARD | PAGE_NOCACHE | PAGE_WRITECOMBINE);
        matches!(
            base,
            PAGE_READONLY
                | PAGE_READWRITE
                | PAGE_WRITECOPY
                | PAGE_EXECUTE_READ
                | PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE
                | PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY
        )
    }

    pub(super) fn is_readable(addr: *const c_void, bytes: usize) -> bool {
        if addr.is_null() || bytes == 0 {
            return false;
        }

        let start = addr as usize;
        if start > usize::MAX - bytes {
            return false; // wraps
        }
        let end = start + bytes;

        let mut cursor = start;
        while cursor < end {
            let mut mbi: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            let n = unsafe {
                VirtualQuery(
                    cursor as *const c_void,
                    &mut mbi,
                    std::mem::size_of::<MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION>(),
                )
            };
            if n != std::mem::size_of::<MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION>() {
                return false;
            }

            if mbi.State != MEM_COMMIT
                || (mbi.Protect & PAGE_GUARD) != 0
                || !is_readable_protect(mbi.Protect)
            {
                return false;
            }

            let region_end = mbi.BaseAddress as usize + mbi.RegionSize;
            if region_end <= cursor {
                return false; // no forward progress
            }
            cursor = region_end;
        }
        true
    }
}

===== FILE: src\platform\numbers.rs =====
//! Strict integer parsers. Source: `OSTPlatform/Numbers.cpp`
//!
//! Every parser is strict in the sense of C++ `std::from_chars`:
//!  * the entire input must be consumed,
//!  * no leading or trailing whitespace,
//!  * no leading `+` (rejected for both signed and unsigned by `from_chars`),
//!  * `-` is accepted only for signed types,
//!  * overflow is a failure, not a clamp,
//!  * for hex, an optional `0x` / `0X` prefix is stripped first.
//!
//! Rust's `from_str_radix` matches most of these rules natively. The one
//! delta is the leading `+`: Rust accepts it for signed types, the C++
//! `from_chars` does not. Both base-10 and base-16 helpers reject it
//! explicitly.

use super::encoding::wide_to_utf8;

// ─── TextSlice ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// A byte-range descriptor, mirroring the C++ `TextSlice { offset; count }`.
/// `count == usize::MAX` means "to the end of the string" (the C++
/// `std::string_view::npos` sentinel).
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TextSlice {
    pub offset: usize,
    pub count: usize,
}

impl TextSlice {
    /// Whole string.
    pub const FULL: TextSlice = TextSlice { offset: 0, count: usize::MAX };
    /// Explicit range.
    pub const fn new(offset: usize, count: usize) -> Self {
        Self { offset, count }
    }
}

fn apply_slice<'a>(value: &'a str, slice: TextSlice) -> Option<&'a str> {
    if slice.offset > value.len() {
        return None;
    }
    // `count == usize::MAX` saturates and then gets capped below.
    let end = slice.offset.saturating_add(slice.count).min(value.len());
    value.get(slice.offset..end)
}

fn strip_hex_prefix(value: &str) -> &str {
    let b = value.as_bytes();
    if b.len() >= 2 && b[0] == b'0' && (b[1] == b'x' || b[1] == b'X') {
        return &value[2..];
    }
    value
}

// ─── Base helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

macro_rules! define_base10 {
    ($name:ident, $t:ty) => {
        fn $name(value: &str) -> Option<$t> {
            if value.is_empty() || value.starts_with('+') {
                return None;
            }
            <$t>::from_str_radix(value, 10).ok()
        }
    };
}

define_base10!(base10_u64, u64);
define_base10!(base10_u32, u32);
define_base10!(base10_i64, i64);
define_base10!(base10_i32, i32);

macro_rules! define_base16 {
    ($name:ident, $t:ty) => {
        fn $name(value: &str) -> Option<$t> {
            let s = strip_hex_prefix(value);
            if s.is_empty() || s.starts_with('+') {
                return None;
            }
            <$t>::from_str_radix(s, 16).ok()
        }
    };
}

define_base16!(base16_u64, u64);
define_base16!(base16_u32, u32);
define_base16!(base16_u8,  u8);

// ─── Public API ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// One family per type: plain, sliced, and wide (UTF-16) variants.
// The wide variants convert via `wide_to_utf8` and delegate, matching
// the C++ overload set exactly.

macro_rules! define_family {
    ($parse:ident, $parse_slice:ident, $parse_wide:ident, $t:ty, $base:ident) => {
        pub fn $parse(value: &str) -> Option<$t> {
            $base(value)
        }
        pub fn $parse_slice(value: &str, slice: TextSlice) -> Option<$t> {
            $parse(apply_slice(value, slice)?)
        }
        pub fn $parse_wide(value: &[u16]) -> Option<$t> {
            $parse(&wide_to_utf8(value))
        }
    };
}

define_family!(parse_u64,     parse_u64_slice,     parse_u64_wide,     u64, base10_u64);
define_family!(parse_u32,     parse_u32_slice,     parse_u32_wide,     u32, base10_u32);
define_family!(parse_i64,     parse_i64_slice,     parse_i64_wide,     i64, base10_i64);
define_family!(parse_i32,     parse_i32_slice,     parse_i32_wide,     i32, base10_i32);

define_family!(parse_hex_u64, parse_hex_u64_slice, parse_hex_u64_wide, u64, base16_u64);
define_family!(parse_hex_u32, parse_hex_u32_slice, parse_hex_u32_wide, u32, base16_u32);
define_family!(parse_hex_u8,  parse_hex_u8_slice,  parse_hex_u8_wide,  u8,  base16_u8);

// ─── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn slice_full_and_offsets() {
        assert_eq!(apply_slice("abc", TextSlice::FULL), Some("abc"));
        assert_eq!(apply_slice("abcdef", TextSlice::new(2, 3)), Some("cde"));
        assert_eq!(apply_slice("abcdef", TextSlice::new(4, 100)), Some("ef"));
        assert_eq!(apply_slice("abc", TextSlice::new(10, 1)), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_u64_basic() {
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("0"), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("123"), Some(123));
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("18446744073709551615"), Some(u64::MAX));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_u64_rejects() {
        assert_eq!(parse_u64(""), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("+1"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("-1"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64(" 1"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("1 "), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("0x10"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("18446744073709551616"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("1.5"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64("abc"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_u32_bounds() {
        assert_eq!(parse_u32("4294967295"), Some(u32::MAX));
        assert_eq!(parse_u32("4294967296"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_i64_basic() {
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("0"), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("-1"), Some(-1));
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("-0"), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("9223372036854775807"), Some(i64::MAX));
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("-9223372036854775808"), Some(i64::MIN));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_i64_rejects() {
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("+1"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_i64(" 1"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("9223372036854775808"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_i64("-9223372036854775809"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_i32_bounds() {
        assert_eq!(parse_i32("-5"), Some(-5));
        assert_eq!(parse_i32("2147483647"), Some(i32::MAX));
        assert_eq!(parse_i32("-2147483648"), Some(i32::MIN));
        assert_eq!(parse_i32("2147483648"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_hex_u64_basic() {
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("0"), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("10"), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("0x10"), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("0X10"), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("ff"), Some(255));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("FF"), Some(255));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("deadbeef"), Some(0xDEAD_BEEF));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_hex_u64_rejects() {
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64(""), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("0x"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("+1"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("-1"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("0xgg"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u64("0x 1"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_hex_u32_overflow() {
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u32("ffffffff"), Some(u32::MAX));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u32("100000000"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_hex_u8_bounds() {
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u8("00"), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u8("ff"), Some(255));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u8("0xFF"), Some(255));
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u8("100"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn slice_variants() {
        assert_eq!(parse_u64_slice("12abc34", TextSlice::new(0, 2)), Some(12));
        assert_eq!(parse_u64_slice("12abc34", TextSlice::new(5, 2)), Some(34));
        assert_eq!(parse_u64_slice("12abc34", TextSlice::new(10, 2)), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_u64_slice("12abc34", TextSlice::new(2, 3)), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn wide_variants() {
        let w: Vec<u16> = "123".encode_utf16().collect();
        assert_eq!(parse_u64_wide(&w), Some(123));

        let w: Vec<u16> = "ff".encode_utf16().collect();
        assert_eq!(parse_hex_u8_wide(&w), Some(255));

        let w: Vec<u16> = "abc".encode_utf16().collect();
        assert_eq!(parse_u64_wide(&w), None);

        let w: Vec<u16> = "-5".encode_utf16().collect();
        assert_eq!(parse_i32_wide(&w), Some(-5));
    }
}

//! PE parsing. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/PE.cpp`
//!
//! We define our own `IMAGE_*` structs rather than using
//! `windows-sys`'s, because the Win32 headers place them in several
//! different feature-gated modules (`SystemServices`, `Diagnostics::Debug`)
//! and the paths differ across crate versions. The PE format is a
//! documented, stable ABI; declaring the layouts locally is the honest
//! translation and removes a class of feature-gate errors.

// ─── Safe helpers for reading unaligned POD from a byte slice ──────

/// Read a `T` from `bytes[offset..]`. Returns `None` if the slice is
/// too short. `T: Copy` with no references inside; the source bytes
/// come from a heap buffer that may not be aligned for `T`, so this
/// uses `read_unaligned`.
unsafe fn pod_at<T: Copy>(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<T> {
    if offset > bytes.len() || std::mem::size_of::<T>() > bytes.len() - offset {
        return None;
    }
    let p = bytes.as_ptr().add(offset) as *const T;
    Some(std::ptr::read_unaligned(p))
}

// ─── ByteBuffer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Owning byte buffer. `Vec<u8>` is zero-filled at allocation; the C++
/// uses `make_unique_for_overwrite` for uninitialized storage. The
/// difference is a `memset` at allocation; the read path immediately
/// overwrites every byte.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ByteBuffer {
    data: Vec<u8>,
}

impl ByteBuffer {
    pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }
    pub fn with_size(size: usize) -> Self { Self { data: vec![0u8; size] } }
    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.data }
    pub fn as_mut_slice(&mut self) -> &mut [u8] { &mut self.data }
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.data.len() }
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { self.data.is_empty() }
    pub fn resize(&mut self, size: usize) { self.data.resize(size, 0); }
}

impl AsRef<[u8]> for ByteBuffer {
    fn as_ref(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.data }
}

// ─── Section / Export ───────────────────────────────────────────────

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Section {
    pub name: String,
    pub virtual_address: u32,
    pub virtual_size: u32,
    pub raw_offset: u32,
    pub raw_size: u32,
    pub characteristics: u32,
}

impl Section {
    pub fn contains_rva(&self, rva: u32) -> bool {
        let size = self.virtual_size.max(self.raw_size);
        let end = self.virtual_address.wrapping_add(size);
        end >= self.virtual_address && rva >= self.virtual_address && rva < end
    }
    pub fn is_executable(&self) -> bool { (self.characteristics & IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE) != 0 }
    pub fn is_writable(&self) -> bool { (self.characteristics & IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE) != 0 }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Export {
    pub rva: u32,
    pub forwarder: String,
}

impl Export {
    pub fn is_forwarder(&self) -> bool { !self.forwarder.is_empty() }
}

// ─── Image ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct Image {
    path: PathBuf,
    header_bytes: ByteBuffer,
    sections: Vec<Section>,
    file_size: u64,
    entry_point_rva: u32,
    export_directory_rva: u32,
    export_directory_size: u32,
    valid: bool,
}

impl Image {
    pub fn new(path: &Path) -> Self {
        let mut img = Self {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            header_bytes: ByteBuffer::new(),
            sections: Vec::new(),
            file_size: 0,
            entry_point_rva: 0,
            export_directory_rva: 0,
            export_directory_size: 0,
            valid: false,
        };
        img.parse_header();
        img
    }

    fn parse_header(&mut self) {
        let file = match std::fs::File::open(&self.path) {
            Ok(f) => f,
            Err(_) => return,
        };
        self.file_size = file.metadata().map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0);
        if self.file_size == 0 { return; }

        // Read at most HEADER_READ_BYTES.
        use std::io::Read;
        let read_len = (self.file_size as usize).min(HEADER_READ_BYTES);
        self.header_bytes.resize(read_len);
        let mut f = file;
        if f.read_exact(self.header_bytes.as_mut_slice()).is_err() {
            return;
        }

        let bytes = self.header_bytes.as_slice();

        // DOS header
        let dos: ImageDosHeader = match unsafe { pod_at(bytes, 0) } {
            Some(d) => d,
            None => return,
        };
        if dos.e_magic != IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE || dos.e_lfanew < 0 { return; }

        let nt_offset = dos.e_lfanew as usize;
        let sig: u32 = match unsafe { pod_at(bytes, nt_offset) } {
            Some(s) => s,
            None => return,
        };
        if sig != IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE { return; }

        let fh_off = nt_offset + 4;
        let fh: ImageFileHeader = match unsafe { pod_at(bytes, fh_off) } {
            Some(f) => f,
            None => return,
        };
        if fh.number_of_sections == 0 { return; }

        let opt_off = fh_off + std::mem::size_of::<ImageFileHeader>();
        let magic: u16 = match unsafe { pod_at(bytes, opt_off) } {
            Some(m) => m,
            None => return,
        };

        let export_dir: ImageDataDirectory;
        if magic == IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC {
            let opt: ImageOptionalHeader64 = match unsafe { pod_at(bytes, opt_off) } {
                Some(o) => o,
                None => return,
            };
            self.entry_point_rva = opt.address_of_entry_point;
            export_dir = opt.data_directory[IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_EXPORT];
        } else if magic == IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR32_MAGIC {
            let opt: ImageOptionalHeader32 = match unsafe { pod_at(bytes, opt_off) } {
                Some(o) => o,
                None => return,
            };
            self.entry_point_rva = opt.address_of_entry_point;
            export_dir = opt.data_directory[IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_EXPORT];
        } else {
            return;
        }

        let sec_off = opt_off + fh.size_of_optional_header as usize;
        let sec_end = sec_off + (fh.number_of_sections as usize) * std::mem::size_of::<ImageSectionHeader>();
        if sec_end > bytes.len() { return; }

        self.sections.reserve(fh.number_of_sections as usize);
        for i in 0..fh.number_of_sections as usize {
            let off = sec_off + i * std::mem::size_of::<ImageSectionHeader>();
            let sh: ImageSectionHeader = match unsafe { pod_at(bytes, off) } {
                Some(s) => s,
                None => return,
            };
            // Section name is a fixed 8-byte array with optional NUL padding.
            let name_end = sh.name.iter().position(|&b| b == 0).unwrap_or(8);
            let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(&sh.name[..name_end]).into_owned();

            self.sections.push(Section {
                name,
                virtual_address: sh.virtual_address,
                virtual_size: sh.virtual_size,
                raw_offset: sh.pointer_to_raw_data,
                raw_size: sh.size_of_raw_data,
                characteristics: sh.characteristics,
            });
        }

        self.export_directory_rva = export_dir.virtual_address;
        self.export_directory_size = export_dir.size;
        self.valid = true;
    }

    pub fn is_valid(&self) -> bool { self.valid }
    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path { &self.path }
    pub fn file_size(&self) -> u64 { self.file_size }
    pub fn entry_point_rva(&self) -> u32 { self.entry_point_rva }
    pub fn sections(&self) -> &[Section] { &self.sections }

    pub fn has_section(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.sections.iter().any(|s| s.name == name)
    }

    pub fn section_containing_rva(&self, rva: u32) -> Option<&Section> {
        self.sections.iter().find(|s| s.contains_rva(rva))
    }

    pub fn rva_to_offset(&self, rva: u32) -> Option<usize> {
        let s = self.section_containing_rva(rva)?;
        let delta = rva.wrapping_sub(s.virtual_address);
        if delta >= s.raw_size { return None; }
        let off = s.raw_offset as usize + delta as usize;
        if (off as u64) < self.file_size { Some(off) } else { None }
    }

    pub fn raw_offset_to_rva(&self, raw_offset: usize) -> Option<u32> {
        for s in &self.sections {
            let start = s.raw_offset as usize;
            let end = start.checked_add(s.raw_size as usize)?;
            if raw_offset < start || raw_offset >= end { continue; }
            let delta = (raw_offset - start) as u32;
            return s.virtual_address.checked_add(delta);
        }
        None
    }

    /// Read raw bytes from the file. Returns an empty buffer on failure.
    pub fn read_raw_bytes(&self, offset: usize, size: usize) -> ByteBuffer {
        use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
        let mut out = ByteBuffer::with_size(size);
        let mut f = match std::fs::File::open(&self.path) { Ok(f) => f, Err(_) => return ByteBuffer::new() };
        if f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset as u64)).is_err() { return ByteBuffer::new(); }
        let mut done = 0usize;
        while done < size {
            match f.read(&mut out.as_mut_slice()[done..]) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(n) => done += n,
                Err(_) => return ByteBuffer::new(),
            }
        }
        out.resize(done);
        out
    }

    pub fn read_all_bytes(&self) -> ByteBuffer {
        use std::io::Read;
        let mut out = ByteBuffer::new();
        let mut f = match std::fs::File::open(&self.path) { Ok(f) => f, Err(_) => return out };
        let _ = f.read_to_end(&mut out.data);
        out
    }

    pub fn find_export(&self, symbol_name: &str) -> Option<Export> {
        if !self.valid || self.export_directory_rva == 0 || self.export_directory_size == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let export_sec = self.section_containing_rva(self.export_directory_rva)?;
        let export_bytes = self.read_raw_bytes(export_sec.raw_offset as usize, export_sec.raw_size as usize);
        if export_bytes.is_empty() { return None; }
        let view = export_bytes.as_slice();

        // Helper: view offset within the export section for a given RVA.
        let view_at_rva = |rva: u32, min_size: usize| -> Option<&[u8]> {
            let raw = self.rva_to_offset(rva)?;
            if raw < export_sec.raw_offset as usize { return None; }
            let local = raw - export_sec.raw_offset as usize;
            if local > view.len() || min_size > view.len() - local { return None; }
            Some(&view[local..])
        };

        let dir_local = {
            let raw = self.rva_to_offset(self.export_directory_rva)?;
            if raw < export_sec.raw_offset as usize { return None; }
            raw - export_sec.raw_offset as usize
        };
        let exports: ImageExportDirectory = unsafe { pod_at(view, dir_local) }?;
        if exports.number_of_names == 0 || exports.number_of_functions == 0 { return None; }

        let names_view = view_at_rva(exports.address_of_names,
            exports.number_of_names as usize * 4)?;
        let ordinals_view = view_at_rva(exports.address_of_name_ordinals,
            exports.number_of_names as usize * 2)?;
        let functions_view = view_at_rva(exports.address_of_functions,
            exports.number_of_functions as usize * 4)?;

        for i in 0..exports.number_of_names as usize {
            let name_rva: u32 = unsafe { pod_at(names_view, i * 4) }?;
            let name_bytes = view_at_rva(name_rva, 1)?;
            let nul = name_bytes.iter().position(|&b| b == 0)?;
            let name = std::str::from_utf8(&name_bytes[..nul]).ok()?;
            if name != symbol_name { continue; }

            let ord: u16 = unsafe { pod_at(ordinals_view, i * 2) }?;
            if ord as u32 >= exports.number_of_functions { return None; }
            let func_rva: u32 = unsafe { pod_at(functions_view, ord as usize * 4) }?;
            if func_rva == 0 { return None; }

            let mut result = Export { rva: func_rva, forwarder: String::new() };
            let export_end = self.export_directory_rva.checked_add(self.export_directory_size)?;
            if func_rva >= self.export_directory_rva && func_rva < export_end {
                let fwd_bytes = view_at_rva(func_rva, 1)?;
                let nul = fwd_bytes.iter().position(|&b| b == 0)?;
                result.forwarder = std::str::from_utf8(&fwd_bytes[..nul]).ok()?.to_string();
            }
            return Some(result);
        }
        None
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn empty_buffer() {
        let b = ByteBuffer::new();
        assert!(b.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(b.len(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sized_buffer() {
        let b = ByteBuffer::with_size(64);
        assert_eq!(b.len(), 64);
        assert!(!b.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn section_rva_containment() {
        let s = Section {
            name: ".text".to_string(),
            virtual_address: 0x1000,
            virtual_size: 0x2000,
            raw_offset: 0x400,
            raw_size: 0x2000,
            characteristics: 0x6000_0020,
        };
        assert!(s.contains_rva(0x1000));
        assert!(s.contains_rva(0x2FFF));
        assert!(!s.contains_rva(0x3000));
        assert!(!s.contains_rva(0x0FFF));
        assert!(s.is_executable());
        assert!(!s.is_writable());
    }

    #[test]
    fn section_writable_flag() {
        let s = Section { characteristics: 0x8000_0000, ..Default::default() };
        assert!(s.is_writable());
        assert!(!s.is_executable());
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_image_path_is_not_valid() {
        let img = Image::new(Path::new("definitely-not-a-real-file.exe"));
        assert!(!img.is_valid());
        assert!(img.sections().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn export_forwarder_detection() {
        let e = Export { rva: 0x1234, forwarder: "KERNEL32.Sleep".to_string() };
        assert!(e.is_forwarder());
        let e2 = Export { rva: 0x1234, forwarder: String::new() };
        assert!(!e2.is_forwarder());
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn parses_kernel32() {
        // kernel32.dll is always present and has a full export table.
        let sysdir = crate::platform::dynamic_library::get_system_directory_path();
        if sysdir.is_empty() { return; }
        let path = Path::new(&sysdir).join("kernel32.dll");
        if !path.exists() { return; }

        let img = Image::new(&path);
        assert!(img.is_valid(), "kernel32.dll failed to parse");
        assert!(img.sections().len() > 1);
        assert!(img.has_section(".text"));

        let export = img.find_export("LoadLibraryW");
        assert!(export.is_some(), "LoadLibraryW not found in kernel32 exports");
        let e = export.unwrap();
        assert!(e.rva != 0);
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn rva_to_offset_round_trip() {
        let sysdir = crate::platform::dynamic_library::get_system_directory_path();
        if sysdir.is_empty() { return; }
        let path = Path::new(&sysdir).join("kernel32.dll");
        if !path.exists() { return; }
        let img = Image::new(&path);
        if !img.is_valid() { return; }

        // Pick the first section and a small offset inside it.
        let sec = &img.sections()[0];
        let rva = sec.virtual_address + 0x10;
        let raw = img.rva_to_offset(rva);
        assert!(raw.is_some());
        let back = img.raw_offset_to_rva(raw.unwrap());
        assert_eq!(back, Some(rva));
    }
}
