//! Process inspection. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Process.cpp`

use std::path::PathBuf;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ModuleInfo {
    pub path: String,
    pub native_path: PathBuf,
    pub size: u32,
    pub executable: bool,
}

// ─── Windows implementation ─────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use std::ffi::c_void;
    use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{
        CloseHandle, GetLastError, FILETIME, HANDLE, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{
        CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Module32FirstW, Module32NextW, MODULEENTRY32W,
        TH32CS_SNAPMODULE, TH32CS_SNAPMODULE32,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
        GetProcessTimes, OpenProcess, QueryFullProcessImageNameW,
        PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, PROCESS_VM_READ,
    };

    #[repr(C)]
    pub(super) struct ProcessBasicInformation {
        pub exit_status: i32,
        pub peb_base_address: *mut c_void,
        pub affinity_mask: usize,
        pub base_priority: i32,
        pub unique_process_id: usize,
        pub inherited_from_unique_process_id: usize,
    }

    type NtQueryInformationProcessFn = unsafe extern "system" fn(
        HANDLE, u32, *mut c_void, u32, *mut u32,
    ) -> i32;

    type NtQueryVirtualMemoryFn = unsafe extern "system" fn(
        HANDLE, *mut c_void, u32, *mut c_void, usize, *mut usize,
    ) -> i32;

    const PROCESS_BASIC_INFORMATION: u32 = 0;
    const WOW64_INFORMATION: u32 = 26;
    const MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION_CLASS: u32 = 0;

    fn resolve_ntdll(name: &str) -> *mut c_void {
        unsafe {
            let ntdll: Vec<u16> = "ntdll.dll".encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect();
            let h = windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::GetModuleHandleW(ntdll.as_ptr());
            if h.is_null() { return std::ptr::null_mut(); }
            let n = std::ffi::CString::new(name).unwrap_or_default();
            match windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::GetProcAddress(h, n.as_ptr() as *const u8) {
                Some(f) => f as *mut c_void,
                None => std::ptr::null_mut(),
            }
        }
    }

    fn open_process(pid: u32, access: u32) -> HANDLE {
        if pid == 0 { return std::ptr::null_mut(); }
        let h = unsafe { OpenProcess(access, 0, pid) };
        if h.is_null() {
            crate::ostp_debug!(
                "OpenProcess(pid={}, access=0x{:X}) failed (error={})",
                pid, access, unsafe { GetLastError() }
            );
        }
        h
    }

    fn wide_to_string(buf: &[u16]) -> String {
        String::from_utf16_lossy(buf)
    }

    pub(super) fn get_creation_time(pid: u32) -> Option<u64> {
        let h = open_process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION);
        if h.is_null() { return None; }
        let mut c: FILETIME = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let mut e: FILETIME = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let mut k: FILETIME = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let mut u: FILETIME = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let ok = unsafe { GetProcessTimes(h, &mut c, &mut e, &mut k, &mut u) };
        unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
        if ok == 0 {
            crate::ostp_debug!("GetProcessTimes(pid={}) failed (error={})", pid, unsafe { GetLastError() });
            return None;
        }
        Some(((c.dwHighDateTime as u64) << 32) | (c.dwLowDateTime as u64))
    }

    pub(super) fn get_image_path(pid: u32) -> Option<String> {
        let h = open_process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION);
        if h.is_null() { return None; }

        for cap in [260u32, 32768u32].iter() {
            let mut buf = vec![0u16; *cap as usize];
            let mut size: u32 = *cap;
            let ok = unsafe { QueryFullProcessImageNameW(h, 0, buf.as_mut_ptr(), &mut size) };
            if ok != 0 {
                buf.truncate(size as usize);
                unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
                return Some(wide_to_string(&buf));
            }
            let err = unsafe { GetLastError() };
            if err != 122 {
                crate::ostp_debug!("QueryFullProcessImageNameW(pid={}) failed (error={})", pid, err);
                unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
                return None;
            }
        }
        unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
        None
    }

    pub(super) fn enumerate_modules(pid: u32) -> Vec<ModuleInfo> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let snap = unsafe { CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPMODULE | TH32CS_SNAPMODULE32, pid) };
        if snap == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE {
            crate::ostp_debug!(
                "CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(pid={}) failed (error={})",
                pid, unsafe { GetLastError() }
            );
            return out;
        }

        let mut entry: MODULEENTRY32W = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        entry.dwSize = std::mem::size_of::<MODULEENTRY32W>() as u32;

        if unsafe { Module32FirstW(snap, &mut entry) } != 0 {
            loop {
                let nul = entry.szExePath.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(260);
                let path = wide_to_string(&entry.szExePath[..nul]);
                if !path.is_empty() {
                    out.push(ModuleInfo {
                        native_path: PathBuf::from(&path),
                        path,
                        size: entry.modBaseSize,
                        executable: false,
                    });
                }
                if unsafe { Module32NextW(snap, &mut entry) } == 0 { break; }
            }
        }
        unsafe { CloseHandle(snap); }
        out
    }

    pub(super) fn launch_detached_hidden(command_line: &str) -> bool {
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
            CreateProcessW, CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, PROCESS_INFORMATION,
            STARTUPINFOW, STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW,
        };

        let mut wide: Vec<u16> = command_line.encode_utf16().collect();
        wide.push(0);

        let mut si: STARTUPINFOW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        si.cb = std::mem::size_of::<STARTUPINFOW>() as u32;
        si.dwFlags = STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW;
        si.wShowWindow = 0;

        for extra in [CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB, 0u32] {
            let mut cmd = wide.clone();
            let mut pi: PROCESS_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            let ok = unsafe {
                CreateProcessW(
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    cmd.as_mut_ptr(),
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    0,
                    CREATE_NO_WINDOW | extra,
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    &si,
                    &mut pi,
                )
            };
            if ok != 0 {
                unsafe { CloseHandle(pi.hThread); CloseHandle(pi.hProcess); }
                return true;
            }
            crate::ostp_debug!(
                "launch_detached_hidden: CreateProcessW failed (extra=0x{:X}, error={})",
                extra, unsafe { GetLastError() }
            );
        }
        crate::ostp_warn!("launch_detached_hidden: could not launch '{}'", command_line);
        false
    }

    unsafe fn read_remote<T: Copy>(h: HANDLE, addr: *const c_void) -> Option<T> {
        let mut value: T = std::mem::zeroed();
        let mut read: usize = 0;
        let ok = windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::ReadProcessMemory(
            h,
            addr,
            &mut value as *mut T as *mut c_void,
            std::mem::size_of::<T>(),
            &mut read,
        );
        if ok == 0 || read != std::mem::size_of::<T>() { None } else { Some(value) }
    }

    const PEB_PROCESS_PARAMETERS_OFFSET: usize = 0x20;
    const PARAMS_COMMAND_LINE_OFFSET: usize = 0x70;
    const PARAMS_ENVIRONMENT_OFFSET: usize = 0x80;

    struct ParamsLocation {
        command_line: *const c_void,
        env_addr: *const c_void,
        env_len: usize,
    }

    unsafe fn resolve_params(h: HANDLE) -> Option<ParamsLocation> {
        let ptr = resolve_ntdll("NtQueryInformationProcess");
        if ptr.is_null() { return None; }
        let nt_qip: NtQueryInformationProcessFn = std::mem::transmute(ptr);

        let mut info: ProcessBasicInformation = std::mem::zeroed();
        let st = nt_qip(
            h,
            PROCESS_BASIC_INFORMATION,
            &mut info as *mut _ as *mut c_void,
            std::mem::size_of::<ProcessBasicInformation>() as u32,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        );
        if st < 0 || info.peb_base_address.is_null() { return None; }

        let params_addr = info.peb_base_address as usize + PEB_PROCESS_PARAMETERS_OFFSET;
        let params: *const c_void = read_remote::<*const c_void>(h, params_addr as *const c_void)?;
        if params.is_null() { return None; }

        let cmd_ptr_addr = params as usize + PARAMS_COMMAND_LINE_OFFSET;
        let env_ptr_addr = params as usize + PARAMS_ENVIRONMENT_OFFSET;

        let cmd_line_buf_addr = cmd_ptr_addr + 8;
        let cmd_line_buffer: *const c_void =
            read_remote::<*const c_void>(h, cmd_line_buf_addr as *const c_void)?;

        let env_addr: *const c_void =
            read_remote::<*const c_void>(h, env_ptr_addr as *const c_void)?;
        if env_addr.is_null() { return None; }

        let env_len = query_readable_region(h, env_addr).unwrap_or(0);
        if env_len < 4 { return None; }

        Some(ParamsLocation {
            command_line: cmd_line_buffer,
            env_addr,
            env_len,
        })
    }

    unsafe fn query_readable_region(h: HANDLE, addr: *const c_void) -> Option<usize> {
        let ptr = resolve_ntdll("NtQueryVirtualMemory");
        if ptr.is_null() { return None; }
        let nt_qvm: NtQueryVirtualMemoryFn = std::mem::transmute(ptr);

        #[repr(C)]
        struct Mbi {
            base_address: *mut c_void,
            allocation_base: *mut c_void,
            allocation_protect: u32,
            partition_id: u16,
            _pad1: u16,
            region_size: usize,
            state: u32,
            protect: u32,
            ty: u32,
            _pad2: u32,
        }

        let mut info: Mbi = std::mem::zeroed();
        let st = nt_qvm(
            h,
            addr as *mut c_void,
            MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION_CLASS,
            &mut info as *mut _ as *mut c_void,
            std::mem::size_of::<Mbi>(),
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        );
        if st < 0 || info.region_size == 0 { return None; }
        let base = info.base_address as usize;
        let cur = addr as usize;
        if cur < base { return None; }
        let off = cur - base;
        if off >= info.region_size { return None; }
        Some(info.region_size - off)
    }

    pub(super) fn get_environment_variable_value(pid: u32, name: &[u16]) -> Option<String> {
        let h = open_process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ);
        if h.is_null() { return None; }
        let r = unsafe {
            resolve_params(h).and_then(|p| read_env_from(h, p.env_addr, p.env_len, name))
        };
        unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
        r
    }

    /// ASCII-only uppercase for a UTF-16 code unit. Environment variable
    /// names are ASCII by convention; this matches Windows' case rules
    /// for those names without pulling in Unicode folding.
    #[inline]
    fn ascii_upper_u16(c: u16) -> u16 {
        if (0x61..=0x7A).contains(&c) { c - 0x20 } else { c }
    }

    unsafe fn read_env_from(
        h: HANDLE,
        env: *const c_void,
        len_bytes: usize,
        name: &[u16],
    ) -> Option<String> {
        let to_read = len_bytes.min(1024 * 1024);
        if to_read < 4 { return None; }
        let mut buf = vec![0u16; to_read / 2];
        let mut read: usize = 0;
        let ok = windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::ReadProcessMemory(
            h,
            env,
            buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
            to_read,
            &mut read,
        );
        if ok == 0 { return None; }
        buf.truncate(read / 2);

        let upper_name: Vec<u16> = name.iter().copied().map(ascii_upper_u16).collect();

        let mut offset = 0usize;
        while offset < buf.len() && buf[offset] != 0 {
            let end = buf[offset..].iter().position(|&c| c == 0)? + offset;
            let entry = &buf[offset..end];
            if entry.len() > upper_name.len() && entry[upper_name.len()] == b'=' as u16 {
                let matches = entry[..upper_name.len()]
                    .iter()
                    .zip(&upper_name)
                    .all(|(a, b)| ascii_upper_u16(*a) == *b);
                if matches {
                    let value = &entry[upper_name.len() + 1..];
                    return Some(String::from_utf16_lossy(value));
                }
            }
            offset = end + 1;
        }
        None
    }

    pub(super) fn get_process_command_line(pid: u32) -> Option<String> {
        let h = open_process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ);
        if h.is_null() { return None; }

        let result = unsafe {
            read_command_line_wow64(h).or_else(|| {
                resolve_params(h).and_then(|p| {
                    if p.command_line.is_null() { return None; }
                    read_unicode_string(h, p.command_line)
                })
            })
        };
        unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
        result
    }

    unsafe fn read_unicode_string(h: HANDLE, buf_addr: *const c_void) -> Option<String> {
        if buf_addr.is_null() { return None; }
        let mut buf = vec![0u16; 32768 / 2];
        let mut read: usize = 0;
        let ok = windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::ReadProcessMemory(
            h,
            buf_addr,
            buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
            buf.len() * 2,
            &mut read,
        );
        if ok == 0 { return None; }
        buf.truncate(read / 2);
        if let Some(nul) = buf.iter().position(|&c| c == 0) {
            buf.truncate(nul);
        }
        if buf.is_empty() { return None; }
        Some(String::from_utf16_lossy(&buf))
    }

    unsafe fn read_command_line_wow64(h: HANDLE) -> Option<String> {
        let ptr = resolve_ntdll("NtQueryInformationProcess");
        if ptr.is_null() { return None; }
        let nt_qip: NtQueryInformationProcessFn = std::mem::transmute(ptr);

        let mut peb32: usize = 0;
        let st = nt_qip(
            h,
            WOW64_INFORMATION,
            &mut peb32 as *mut _ as *mut c_void,
            std::mem::size_of::<usize>() as u32,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        );
        if st < 0 || peb32 == 0 { return None; }

        let params32_ptr_addr = (peb32 as usize + 0x10) as *const c_void;
        let params32: u32 = read_remote::<u32>(h, params32_ptr_addr)?;
        if params32 == 0 { return None; }

        let cmd32_len_addr = (params32 as usize + 0x40) as *const c_void;
        let cmd32_len: u16 = read_remote::<u16>(h, cmd32_len_addr)?;
        let cmd32_buf_addr = (params32 as usize + 0x44) as *const c_void;
        let cmd32_buf: u32 = read_remote::<u32>(h, cmd32_buf_addr)?;
        if cmd32_buf == 0 || cmd32_len == 0 { return None; }

        let chars = (cmd32_len / 2) as usize;
        if chars == 0 || chars > 32768 / 2 { return None; }
        let mut buf = vec![0u16; chars];
        let mut read: usize = 0;
        let ok = windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::ReadProcessMemory(
            h,
            cmd32_buf as *const c_void,
            buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
            chars * 2,
            &mut read,
        );
        if ok == 0 { return None; }
        buf.truncate(read / 2);
        Some(String::from_utf16_lossy(&buf))
    }
}

// ─── Public API ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub fn get_creation_time(pid: u32) -> Option<u64> { imp::get_creation_time(pid) }

pub fn format_creation_time(file_time: u64) -> String {
    if file_time == 0 { return "-".to_string(); }
    const EPOCH_DIFF: u64 = 116_444_736_000_000_000;
    if file_time < EPOCH_DIFF {
        return format!("filetime={}", file_time);
    }
    let since_unix_100ns = file_time - EPOCH_DIFF;
    let secs = since_unix_100ns / 10_000_000;
    let micros = (since_unix_100ns % 10_000_000) / 10;
    match chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(secs as i64, (micros * 1000) as u32) {
        Some(dt) => dt.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S%.3f").to_string(),
        None => format!("filetime={}", file_time),
    }
}

pub fn get_image_path(pid: u32) -> Option<String> { imp::get_image_path(pid) }
pub fn get_environment_variable_value(pid: u32, name: &[u16]) -> Option<String> {
    imp::get_environment_variable_value(pid, name)
}
pub fn get_process_command_line(pid: u32) -> Option<String> { imp::get_process_command_line(pid) }
pub fn enumerate_modules(pid: u32) -> Vec<ModuleInfo> { imp::enumerate_modules(pid) }

pub fn is_system_module_path(path: &str) -> bool {
    let windir = match std::env::var("WINDIR") {
        Ok(v) => v,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    let mut norm_dir = windir.to_lowercase().replace('/', "\\");
    if !norm_dir.ends_with('\\') { norm_dir.push('\\'); }
    let norm_path = path.to_lowercase().replace('/', "\\");
    norm_path.starts_with(&norm_dir)
}

pub fn launch_detached_hidden(command_line: &str) -> bool {
    imp::launch_detached_hidden(command_line)
}

mod tests {

    #[test]

    }

    #[test]

        let f = 116_444_736_000_000_000u64;
        let s = format_creation_time(f);
        assert!(s.starts_with("1970-01-01"));
    }

    #[test]

            assert!(!is_system_module_path("C:\\Users\\foo\\module.dll"));
        }
    }

    #[test]

        let windir = match std::env::var("WINDIR") {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(_) => return,
        };
        let probe = format!("{}/system32/kernel32.dll", windir.to_lowercase());
        assert!(is_system_module_path(&probe));
        let probe2 = format!("{}\\SYSTEM32\\KERNEL32.DLL", windir.to_uppercase());
        assert!(is_system_module_path(&probe2));
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]

    }

===== FILE: src\platform\remote_process.rs =====
//! Remote-process DLL injection. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/RemoteProcess.cpp`
//!
//! Classic `LoadLibraryW` injection:
//!   1. Open the target with `PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD | QUERY_INFORMATION |
//!      VM_OPERATION | VM_WRITE | VM_READ`.
//!   2. `VirtualAllocEx` a buffer for the wide library path.
//!   3. `WriteProcessMemory` the path.
//!   4. `CreateRemoteThread(kernel32!LoadLibraryW, path_addr)`.
//!   5. `WaitForSingleObject` + `GetExitCodeThread` -> the module handle,
//!      or zero on failure.
//!   6. `VirtualFreeEx` the path buffer.
//!
//! The C++ resolves `LoadLibraryW` by parsing kernel32's export table
//! from disk (`PE::Image::FindExport`) and adding `modBaseAddr`. We do
//! the same via `crate::platform::pe::Image` and
//! `crate::platform::process::enumerate_modules`.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Architecture { Unknown, X86, X64 }

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum InjectStatus {
    Ok,
    OpenProcessFailed,
    UnknownArchitecture,
    AllocFailed,
    WriteFailed,
    ResolveLoadLibraryFailed,
    CreateThreadFailed,
    WaitFailed,
    RemoteLoadFailed,
}

impl Architecture {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Architecture::Unknown => "Unknown",
            Architecture::X86 => "X86",
            Architecture::X64 => "X64",
        }
    }
}

impl InjectStatus {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            InjectStatus::Ok => "Ok",
            InjectStatus::OpenProcessFailed => "OpenProcessFailed",
            InjectStatus::UnknownArchitecture => "UnknownArchitecture",
            InjectStatus::AllocFailed => "AllocFailed",
            InjectStatus::WriteFailed => "WriteFailed",
            InjectStatus::ResolveLoadLibraryFailed => "ResolveLoadLibraryFailed",
            InjectStatus::CreateThreadFailed => "CreateThreadFailed",
            InjectStatus::WaitFailed => "WaitFailed",
            InjectStatus::RemoteLoadFailed => "RemoteLoadFailed",
        }
    }
}

// ─── Windows implementation ─────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use std::ffi::c_void;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{
        CloseHandle, GetLastError, WAIT_OBJECT_0,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::WriteProcessMemory;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::GetModuleHandleW;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        VirtualAllocEx, VirtualFreeEx, MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
        CreateRemoteThread, GetExitCodeThread, IsWow64Process, OpenProcess,
        WaitForSingleObject, PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION,
        PROCESS_VM_OPERATION, PROCESS_VM_READ, PROCESS_VM_WRITE,
    };

    const INJECT_ACCESS: u32 = PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD
        | PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION
        | PROCESS_VM_OPERATION
        | PROCESS_VM_WRITE
        | PROCESS_VM_READ;

    pub(super) fn detect_arch(h: *mut c_void) -> Architecture {
        let mut wow64: i32 = 0;
        let ok = unsafe { IsWow64Process(h, &mut wow64) };
        if ok == 0 { return Architecture::Unknown; }
        if wow64 != 0 {
            return Architecture::X86;
        }
        // Native process.
        #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "64")]
        { Architecture::X64 }
        #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")]
        { Architecture::X86 }
    }

    pub(super) fn get_architecture(pid: u32) -> Architecture {
        if pid == 0 { return Architecture::Unknown; }
        let h = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION_SAFE, 0, pid) };
        if h.is_null() {
            crate::ostp_debug!(
                "OpenProcess(pid={}) failed (error={})",
                pid, unsafe { GetLastError() }
            );
            return Architecture::Unknown;
        }
        let a = detect_arch(h);
        unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
        a
    }

    // PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION is 0x1000.
    const PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION_SAFE: u32 = 0x1000;

    fn wide_module_name(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    fn get_module_path(pid: u32, name: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        let mods = crate::platform::process::enumerate_modules(pid);
        mods.into_iter()
            .find(|m| {
                m.native_path
                    .file_name()
                    .and_then(|f| f.to_str())
                    .map(|f| f.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
                    .unwrap_or(false)
            })
            .map(|m| m.native_path)
    }

    fn find_remote_module_base(pid: u32, name: &str) -> Option<u64> {
        let mods = crate::platform::process::enumerate_modules(pid);
        // We did not keep base address in ModuleInfo. For injection we
        // need it; re-snapshot with Toolhelp directly.
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{
            CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Module32FirstW, Module32NextW, MODULEENTRY32W,
            TH32CS_SNAPMODULE, TH32CS_SNAPMODULE32,
        };
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
        let snap = unsafe { CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPMODULE | TH32CS_SNAPMODULE32, pid) };
        if snap == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE { return None; }
        let mut entry: MODULEENTRY32W = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        entry.dwSize = std::mem::size_of::<MODULEENTRY32W>() as u32;
        let mut result = None;
        if unsafe { Module32FirstW(snap, &mut entry) } != 0 {
            loop {
                let nul = entry.szModule.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(256);
                let mname = String::from_utf16_lossy(&entry.szModule[..nul]);
                if mname.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name) {
                    result = Some(entry.modBaseAddr as u64);
                    break;
                }
                if unsafe { Module32NextW(snap, &mut entry) } == 0 { break; }
            }
        }
        unsafe { CloseHandle(snap); }
        let _ = mods;
        result
    }

    /// Resolve `LoadLibraryW` in the target process.
    fn resolve_remote_load_library(pid: u32, arch: Architecture) -> Option<*mut c_void> {
        let _ = arch;
        // Get the on-disk path of kernel32 in the target.
        let k32_path = get_module_path(pid, "kernel32.dll")
            .or_else(|| get_module_path(pid, "kernelbase.dll"))?;
        let img = crate::platform::pe::Image::new(&k32_path);
        if !img.is_valid() { return None; }

        let export = img.find_export("LoadLibraryW")?;
        if export.is_fwd() {
            // Forwarder: parse "MODULE.Symbol" and try once more.
            let fwd = &export.forwarder;
            let dot = fwd.find('.')?;
            let mod_name = &fwd[..dot];
            let sym_name = &fwd[dot + 1..];
            if sym_name.starts_with('#') { return None; }
            let mod_file = if mod_name.contains('.') {
                mod_name.to_string()
            } else {
                format!("{}.dll", mod_name)
            };
            let p = get_module_path(pid, &mod_file)?;
            let img2 = crate::platform::pe::Image::new(&p);
            if !img2.is_valid() { return None; }
            let e2 = img2.find_export(sym_name)?;
            if e2.is_fwd() { return None; }
            let base = find_remote_module_base(pid, &mod_file)?;
            return Some((base + e2.rva as u64) as *mut c_void);
        }

        let base = find_remote_module_base(pid, "kernel32.dll")?;
        Some((base + export.rva as u64) as *mut c_void)
    }

    pub(super) fn inject_library(pid: u32, library_path: &Path) -> InjectStatus {
        if pid == 0 { return InjectStatus::OpenProcessFailed; }
        let h = unsafe { OpenProcess(INJECT_ACCESS, 0, pid) };
        if h.is_null() {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "OpenProcess(pid={}, access=0x{:X}) failed (error={})",
                pid, INJECT_ACCESS, unsafe { GetLastError() }
            );
            return InjectStatus::OpenProcessFailed;
        }

        let arch = detect_arch(h);
        if arch == Architecture::Unknown {
            unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
            return InjectStatus::UnknownArchitecture;
        }

        let load_library = match resolve_remote_load_library(pid, arch) {
            Some(f) => f,
            None => {
                unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
                return InjectStatus::ResolveLoadLibraryFailed;
            }
        };

        // Wide path with trailing NUL.
        let wide: Vec<u16> = library_path
            .as_os_str()
            .to_string_lossy()
            .encode_utf16()
            .chain(std::iter::once(0))
            .collect();
        let bytes = wide.len() * 2;

        let remote = unsafe {
            VirtualAllocEx(h, std::ptr::null(), bytes, MEM_COMMIT | MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE)
        };
        if remote.is_null() {
            crate::ostp_warn!("VirtualAllocEx(size={}) failed (error={})", bytes, unsafe { GetLastError() });
            unsafe { CloseHandle(h); }
            return InjectStatus::AllocFailed;
        }

        let mut written: usize = 0;
        let ok = unsafe {
            WriteProcessMemory(h, remote, wide.as_ptr() as *const c_void, bytes, &mut written)
        };
        if ok == 0 || written != bytes {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "WriteProcessMemory(size={}) failed (written={}, error={})",
                bytes, written, unsafe { GetLastError() }
            );
            unsafe {
                VirtualFreeEx(h, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
                CloseHandle(h);
            }
            return InjectStatus::WriteFailed;
        }

        let thread = unsafe {
            CreateRemoteThread(
                h,
                std::ptr::null(),
                0,
                Some(std::mem::transmute::<*mut c_void, unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void) -> u32>(load_library)),
                remote,
                0,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
            )
        };
        if thread.is_null() {
            crate::ostp_warn!("CreateRemoteThread failed (error={})", unsafe { GetLastError() });
            unsafe {
                VirtualFreeEx(h, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
                CloseHandle(h);
            }
            return InjectStatus::CreateThreadFailed;
        }

        let wait = unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(thread, 10_000) };
        if wait != WAIT_OBJECT_0 {
            crate::ostp_warn!("WaitForSingleObject(remote thread) returned {} (error={})", wait, unsafe { GetLastError() });
            unsafe {
                VirtualFreeEx(h, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
                CloseHandle(thread);
                CloseHandle(h);
            }
            return InjectStatus::WaitFailed;
        }

        let mut exit_code: u32 = 0;
        let ok = unsafe { GetExitCodeThread(thread, &mut exit_code) };
        if ok == 0 {
            crate::ostp_warn!("GetExitCodeThread failed (error={})", unsafe { GetLastError() });
            unsafe {
                VirtualFreeEx(h, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
                CloseHandle(thread);
                CloseHandle(h);
            }
            return InjectStatus::RemoteLoadFailed;
        }

        unsafe {
            VirtualFreeEx(h, remote, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
            CloseHandle(thread);
            CloseHandle(h);
        }

        if exit_code == 0 {
            crate::ostp_warn!("Remote LoadLibraryW returned 0 for '{}'", library_path.display());
            return InjectStatus::RemoteLoadFailed;
        }
        InjectStatus::Ok
    }
}

===== FILE: src\platform\steam_credential_store.rs =====
//! Steam per-app credential store (HKCU registry).
//! Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/SteamCredentialStore.cpp`
//!
//! `RegGetValueW` returns `WIN32_ERROR` (a `u32` in `windows-sys`),
//! not the `i32` that the Win32 header names `LSTATUS`. All the
//! helper types and constants here use `u32` accordingly.

use super::windows::handles::{UniqueRegKey, HKEY};

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Status {
    Ok,
    NotFound,
    Unsupported,
    Failed,
}

impl Status {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Status::Ok => "Ok",
            Status::NotFound => "NotFound",
            Status::Unsupported => "Unsupported",
            Status::Failed => "Failed",
        }
    }
}

// ─── Windows implementation ─────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use std::ffi::c_void;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Registry::{
        RegCreateKeyExW, RegGetValueW, RegSetValueExW, HKEY_CURRENT_USER, KEY_SET_VALUE,
        REG_OPTION_NON_VOLATILE, REG_SZ, RRF_RT_REG_BINARY, RRF_RT_REG_DWORD, RRF_RT_REG_SZ,
    };

    // windows-sys models LSTATUS as `u32`.
    const ERROR_SUCCESS: u32 = 0;
    const ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND: u32 = 2;
    const ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND: u32 = 3;
    const ERROR_NOT_FOUND: u32 = 1168;

    fn from_lstatus(status: u32) -> Status {
        match status {
            ERROR_SUCCESS => Status::Ok,
            ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND | ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND | ERROR_NOT_FOUND => Status::NotFound,
            _ => Status::Failed,
        }
    }

    fn to_wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    fn steam_app_key_path(app_id: u32) -> Vec<u16> {
        to_wide(&format!("Software\\Valve\\Steam\\Apps\\{}", app_id))
    }

    const ACTIVE_PROCESS_KEY_PATH: &str = "Software\\Valve\\Steam\\ActiveProcess";

    fn value_name(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        s.encode_utf16().collect()
    }

    unsafe fn read_binary_value(
        app_id: u32,
        value_name_str: &str,
        out: &mut Vec<u8>,
    ) -> u32 {
        let key_path = steam_app_key_path(app_id);
        let vname = value_name(value_name_str);

        let mut bytes: u32 = 0;
        let status = RegGetValueW(
            HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
            key_path.as_ptr(),
            vname.as_ptr(),
            RRF_RT_REG_BINARY,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            &mut bytes,
        );
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            let mapped = from_lstatus(status);
            if mapped == Status::NotFound {
                crate::ostp_debug!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: {} missing for appid={} status={}",
                    value_name_str, app_id, status
                );
            } else {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: failed to query {} size for appid={} status={}",
                    value_name_str, app_id, status
                );
            }
            return status;
        }
        if bytes == 0 {
            crate::ostp_debug!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: {} empty for appid={}",
                value_name_str, app_id
            );
            out.clear();
            return ERROR_SUCCESS;
        }

        let mut buf = vec![0u8; bytes as usize];
        let status = RegGetValueW(
            HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
            key_path.as_ptr(),
            vname.as_ptr(),
            RRF_RT_REG_BINARY,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
            &mut bytes,
        );
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: failed to read {} for appid={} status={}",
                value_name_str, app_id, status
            );
            return status;
        }

        buf.truncate(bytes as usize);
        *out = buf;
        crate::ostp_debug!(
            "SteamCredentialStore: read {} for appid={} bytes={}",
            value_name_str, app_id, out.len()
        );
        ERROR_SUCCESS
    }

    unsafe fn write_value(
        app_id: u32,
        value_name_str: &str,
        ty: u32,
        data: &[u8],
    ) -> u32 {
        let key_path = steam_app_key_path(app_id);
        let vname = value_name(value_name_str);

        let mut key = UniqueRegKey::new();
        let status = RegCreateKeyExW(
            HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
            key_path.as_ptr(),
            0,
            std::ptr::null(),
            REG_OPTION_NON_VOLATILE,
            KEY_SET_VALUE,
            std::ptr::null(),
            key.put(),
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
        );
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: failed to create/open app key appid={} status={}",
                app_id, status
            );
            return status;
        }

        let status = RegSetValueExW(
            key.get(),
            vname.as_ptr(),
            0,
            ty,
            data.as_ptr(),
            data.len() as u32,
        );
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: failed to write {} for appid={} bytes={} status={}",
                value_name_str, app_id, data.len(), status
            );
            return status;
        }

        crate::ostp_info!(
            "SteamCredentialStore: wrote {} for appid={} bytes={}",
            value_name_str, app_id, data.len()
        );
        ERROR_SUCCESS
    }

    pub(super) fn get_app_ticket(app_id: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let st = unsafe { read_binary_value(app_id, "AppTicket", &mut out) };
        match from_lstatus(st) {
            Status::Ok => Ok(out),
            other => Err(other),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn write_app_ticket(app_id: u32, data: &[u8]) -> Status {
        let st = unsafe { write_value(app_id, "AppTicket", RRF_RT_REG_BINARY, data) };
        from_lstatus(st)
    }

    pub(super) fn get_e_ticket(app_id: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let st = unsafe { read_binary_value(app_id, "ETicket", &mut out) };
        match from_lstatus(st) {
            Status::Ok => Ok(out),
            other => Err(other),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn write_e_ticket(app_id: u32, data: &[u8]) -> Status {
        let st = unsafe { write_value(app_id, "ETicket", RRF_RT_REG_BINARY, data) };
        from_lstatus(st)
    }

    pub(super) fn get_steam_id(app_id: u32) -> Result<u64, Status> {
        let key_path = steam_app_key_path(app_id);
        let vname = value_name("SteamID");

        let mut bytes: u32 = 0;
        let status = unsafe {
            RegGetValueW(
                HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
                key_path.as_ptr(),
                vname.as_ptr(),
                RRF_RT_REG_SZ,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                &mut bytes,
            )
        };
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            let mapped = from_lstatus(status);
            if mapped == Status::NotFound {
                crate::ostp_debug!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: SteamID missing for appid={} status={}",
                    app_id, status
                );
            } else {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: failed to query SteamID size for appid={} status={}",
                    app_id, status
                );
            }
            return Err(mapped);
        }
        if bytes < 2 {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: SteamID value too short for appid={} bytes={}",
                app_id, bytes
            );
            return Err(Status::NotFound);
        }

        let mut raw = vec![0u16; (bytes / 2) as usize];
        let status = unsafe {
            RegGetValueW(
                HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
                key_path.as_ptr(),
                vname.as_ptr(),
                RRF_RT_REG_SZ,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                raw.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
                &mut bytes,
            )
        };
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: failed to read SteamID for appid={} status={}",
                app_id, status
            );
            return Err(from_lstatus(status));
        }

        let chars = (bytes / 2) as usize;
        let trimmed = if chars > 0 { &raw[..chars - 1] } else { &raw[..0] };
        let s = String::from_utf16_lossy(trimmed);

        let parsed = s.parse::<u64>().ok().filter(|&v| v != 0);
        let parsed = match parsed {
            Some(v) => v,
            None => {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: SteamID value invalid for appid={}",
                    app_id
                );
                return Err(Status::NotFound);
            }
        };

        crate::ostp_debug!(
            "SteamCredentialStore: read SteamID for appid={} steamid={}",
            app_id, parsed
        );
        Ok(parsed)
    }

    pub(super) fn write_steam_id(app_id: u32, steam_id: u64) -> Status {
        let s = steam_id.to_string();
        let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity((s.len() + 1) * 2);
        for cu in s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)) {
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&cu.to_le_bytes());
        }
        let st = unsafe { write_value(app_id, "SteamID", RRF_RT_REG_SZ, &bytes) };
        from_lstatus(st)
    }

    pub(super) fn get_active_user() -> Result<(u32, String), Status> {
        let key_path = to_wide(ACTIVE_PROCESS_KEY_PATH);
        let vname_user = value_name("ActiveUser");

        let mut active_user: u32 = 0;
        let mut bytes: u32 = std::mem::size_of::<u32>() as u32;
        let status = unsafe {
            RegGetValueW(
                HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
                key_path.as_ptr(),
                vname_user.as_ptr(),
                RRF_RT_REG_DWORD,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                &mut active_user as *mut u32 as *mut c_void,
                &mut bytes,
            )
        };
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            let mapped = from_lstatus(status);
            if mapped == Status::NotFound {
                crate::ostp_debug!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: ActiveUser missing status={}",
                    status
                );
            } else {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: failed to read ActiveUser status={}",
                    status
                );
            }
            return Err(mapped);
        }
        if bytes != std::mem::size_of::<u32>() as u32 {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: ActiveUser has unexpected size bytes={}",
                bytes
            );
            return Err(Status::NotFound);
        }
        if active_user == 0 {
            crate::ostp_debug!("SteamCredentialStore: ActiveUser is zero");
            return Err(Status::NotFound);
        }

        let vname_universe = value_name("Universe");
        bytes = 0;
        let status = unsafe {
            RegGetValueW(
                HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
                key_path.as_ptr(),
                vname_universe.as_ptr(),
                RRF_RT_REG_SZ,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                &mut bytes,
            )
        };
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            let mapped = from_lstatus(status);
            if mapped == Status::NotFound {
                crate::ostp_debug!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: ActiveProcess Universe missing status={}",
                    status
                );
            } else {
                crate::ostp_warn!(
                    "SteamCredentialStore: failed to query ActiveProcess Universe size status={}",
                    status
                );
            }
            return Err(mapped);
        }
        if bytes < 2 {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: ActiveProcess Universe value too short bytes={}",
                bytes
            );
            return Err(Status::NotFound);
        }

        let mut raw = vec![0u16; (bytes / 2) as usize];
        let status = unsafe {
            RegGetValueW(
                HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
                key_path.as_ptr(),
                vname_universe.as_ptr(),
                RRF_RT_REG_SZ,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                raw.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
                &mut bytes,
            )
        };
        if status != ERROR_SUCCESS {
            crate::ostp_warn!(
                "SteamCredentialStore: failed to read ActiveProcess Universe status={}",
                status
            );
            return Err(from_lstatus(status));
        }

        let chars = (bytes / 2) as usize;
        let trimmed = if chars > 0 { &raw[..chars - 1] } else { &raw[..0] };
        let universe = String::from_utf16_lossy(trimmed);
        if universe.is_empty() {
            crate::ostp_warn!("SteamCredentialStore: ActiveProcess Universe is empty");
            return Err(Status::NotFound);
        }

        crate::ostp_debug!(
            "SteamCredentialStore: read ActiveUser accountid={} universe={}",
            active_user, universe
        );
        Ok((active_user, universe))
    }
}

//! Simple elapsed-time helper. Source: `OSTPlatform/include/Stopwatch.h`
//!
//! Rust's `Instant` is a monotonic clock with the same semantics as
//! `std::chrono::steady_clock`.

use std::time::Instant;

pub struct Stopwatch {
    start: Instant,
}

impl Stopwatch {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { start: Instant::now() }
    }

    pub fn elapsed_ms(&self) -> f64 {
        self.start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1000.0
    }
}

impl Default for Stopwatch {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::thread::sleep;
    use std::time::Duration;

    #[test]
    fn new_is_monotonic_nonzero_after_sleep() {
        let s = Stopwatch::new();
        sleep(Duration::from_millis(5));
        let elapsed = s.elapsed_ms();
        assert!(elapsed >= 4.0, "expected >= 4 ms, got {}", elapsed);
        assert!(elapsed < 500.0, "suspiciously large elapsed: {}", elapsed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn elapsed_grows() {
        let s = Stopwatch::new();
        let a = s.elapsed_ms();
        sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
        let b = s.elapsed_ms();
        assert!(b > a);
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\thread.rs =====
//! Thread helpers. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Thread.cpp`
//!
//! `start_detached` uses `std::thread` (equivalent to `CreateThread` +
//! immediate `CloseHandle`). `current_native_thread_handle` calls
//! `GetCurrentThread` on Windows; the returned pseudo-handle is
//! process-scoped and does not need closing, matching the C++ use.

use std::ffi::c_void;

pub type NativeThreadHandle = *mut c_void;

pub fn current_native_thread_handle() -> NativeThreadHandle {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    unsafe {
        windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentThread() as NativeThreadHandle
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        std::ptr::null_mut()
    }
}

/// Run `entry` on a detached thread. Returns false if the thread could
/// not be spawned (OS resource exhaustion).
pub fn start_detached<F>(entry: F) -> bool
where
    F: FnOnce() -> u32 + Send + 'static,
{
    std::thread::Builder::new()
        .spawn(entry)
        .map(|_h| true)   // handle dropped -> thread detached
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::thread::sleep;
    use std::time::Duration;

    #[test]
    fn detached_thread_runs() {
        let flag = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));
        let f = flag.clone();
        assert!(start_detached(move || { f.store(42, Ordering::SeqCst); 0 }));
        for _ in 0..50 {
            if flag.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == 42 { return; }
            sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
        }
        panic!("detached thread did not run");
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn current_native_thread_handle_is_nonnull() {
        // GetCurrentThread returns a pseudo-handle, always non-null.
        let h = current_native_thread_handle();
        assert!(!h.is_null());
    }

    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    #[test]
    fn current_native_thread_handle_is_null() {
        assert!(current_native_thread_handle().is_null());
    }
}


===== FILE: src\platform\trap.rs =====
//! Vectored-exception-handler support. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Trap.cpp`
//!
//! Real implementation on Windows. `AddVectoredExceptionHandler` is a
//! Win32 call; the CONTEXT struct from `windows-sys` gives typed access
//! to RCX/RDX/R8/R9/RSP/RIP/EFlags.

use std::ffi::c_void;

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ExceptionKind {
    Breakpoint,
    SingleStep,
    Other,
}

/// The x64 register context at the point of an exception.
pub struct Context {
    native: *mut c_void,
}

impl Context {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `ptr` must be a valid `CONTEXT*` that stays live for the duration
    /// of any use of the returned `Context`.
    pub unsafe fn from_native(ptr: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        Self { native: ptr }
    }

    pub fn instruction_pointer(&self) -> u64 {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            if self.native.is_null() { return 0; }
            unsafe {
                let ctx = self.native as *const windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::CONTEXT;
                (*ctx).Rip
            }
        }
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        { 0 }
    }

    /// Nth (1-based) integer/pointer argument under the x64 fastcall
    /// convention. Args 1-4 from RCX/RDX/R8/R9; 5+ from the stack.
    /// Only valid when the trap fired at the function's first instruction.
    pub fn argument(&self, index: i32) -> u64 {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            if self.native.is_null() || index <= 0 { return 0; }
            unsafe {
                let ctx = self.native as *const windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::CONTEXT;
                match index {
                    1 => (*ctx).Rcx,
                    2 => (*ctx).Rdx,
                    3 => (*ctx).R8,
                    4 => (*ctx).R9,
                    _ => {
                        // Stack slot: [RSP + 8*index]. The C++ computes
                        // RSP + index*8, and reads a u64 from there.
                        let slot = (*ctx).Rsp.wrapping_add((index as u64) * 8);
                        std::ptr::read_unaligned(slot as *const u64)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        {
            let _ = index;
            0
        }
    }

    pub fn enable_single_step(&mut self) {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            if self.native.is_null() { return; }
            unsafe {
                let ctx = self.native as *mut windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::CONTEXT;
                (*ctx).EFlags |= 0x100;
            }
        }
    }
}

/// VEH handler installed by the caller. Returning `true` requests
/// `EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION`; `false` lets the exception propagate.
pub type Handler = fn(ExceptionKind, &mut Context) -> bool;

/// Opaque handle to an installed handler.
pub type HandlerHandle = *mut c_void;

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicPtr, Ordering};
    // Both exception codes are exported from Win32::Foundation.
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT, EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::{
        AddVectoredExceptionHandler, RemoveVectoredExceptionHandler, EXCEPTION_POINTERS,
    };

    // The C++ installs exactly one global handler at a time; do the same.
    static HANDLER: AtomicPtr<c_void> = AtomicPtr::new(std::ptr::null_mut());

    unsafe extern "system" fn veh_thunk(info: *mut EXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> i32 {
        let h = HANDLER.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        if h.is_null() { return 0; }
        if info.is_null() { return 0; }

        let rec = (*info).ExceptionRecord;
        let ctx = (*info).ContextRecord;
        if rec.is_null() || ctx.is_null() { return 0; }

        let code = (*rec).ExceptionCode;
        let kind = if code == EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT {
            ExceptionKind::Breakpoint
        } else if code == EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP {
            ExceptionKind::SingleStep
        } else {
            ExceptionKind::Other
        };

        let mut ctx_wrapper = unsafe { Context::from_native(ctx as *mut c_void) };
        let f: Handler = unsafe { std::mem::transmute(h) };
        let handled = f(kind, &mut ctx_wrapper);

        if handled { -1 } else { 0 }  // CONTINUE_EXECUTION / CONTINUE_SEARCH
    }

    pub(super) fn add(handler: Handler) -> HandlerHandle {
        let ptr = handler as *const () as *mut c_void;
        HANDLER.store(ptr, Ordering::Release);
        let h = unsafe { AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, Some(veh_thunk)) };
        h as HandlerHandle
    }

    pub(super) fn remove(handle: HandlerHandle) {
        if handle.is_null() { return; }
        unsafe { RemoveVectoredExceptionHandler(handle as *mut c_void); }
        HANDLER.store(std::ptr::null_mut(), Ordering::Release);
    }
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
mod imp {
    use super::*;

    pub(super) fn add(_handler: Handler) -> HandlerHandle { std::ptr::null_mut() }
    pub(super) fn remove(_handle: HandlerHandle) { }
}

pub fn add_vectored_handler(handler: Handler) -> HandlerHandle {
    imp::add(handler)
}

pub fn remove_vectored_handler(handle: HandlerHandle) {
    imp::remove(handle);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn context_from_null_is_usable() {
        let mut ctx = unsafe { Context::from_native(std::ptr::null_mut()) };
        assert_eq!(ctx.instruction_pointer(), 0);
        assert_eq!(ctx.argument(1), 0);
        assert_eq!(ctx.argument(5), 0);
        assert_eq!(ctx.argument(0), 0);
        assert_eq!(ctx.argument(-1), 0);
        ctx.enable_single_step();
    }

    #[test]
    fn exception_kind_equality() {
        assert_eq!(ExceptionKind::Breakpoint, ExceptionKind::Breakpoint);
        assert_ne!(ExceptionKind::Breakpoint, ExceptionKind::SingleStep);
    }

    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    #[test]
    fn add_handler_stub_returns_null() {
        fn noop(_: ExceptionKind, _: &mut Context) -> bool { false }
        let h = add_vectored_handler(noop);
        assert!(h.is_null());
        remove_vectored_handler(h);
    }

    #[cfg(windows)]
    #[test]
    fn install_and_remove_handler() {
        fn noop(_: ExceptionKind, _: &mut Context) -> bool { false }
        let h = add_vectored_handler(noop);
        assert!(!h.is_null(), "AddVectoredExceptionHandler returned null");
        remove_vectored_handler(h);
    }
}

===== FILE: src\platform\windows\detours_ffi.rs =====
//! Raw FFI to the Microsoft Detours C API.
//!
//! Linked against the vendored `third_party/Detours` static library.
//! `build.rs` emits `cargo:rustc-link-search=native=.../lib.X64` and
//! `cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=detours`; this module only declares the
//! symbols.
//!
//! ## Calling convention
//!
//! Detours' prototypes are `WINAPI`, i.e. `__stdcall` on x86 and the
//! platform ABI on x64. `extern "system"` is correct on both.
//!
//! ## Contract
//!
//! Every `DetourAttach` / `DetourDetach` must happen between a
//! `DetourTransactionBegin` and a `DetourTransactionCommit` (or
//! `DetourTransactionAbort`) on the same thread.
//!
//! `DetourUpdateThread` enrols a thread's context in the transaction so
//! its instruction pointer is fixed up if it happens to be inside the
//! prolog of a hooked function. On x64, commit suspends the process and
//! does this automatically for every thread other than the caller; the
//! calling thread must be enrolled explicitly before the first attach
//! or detach in the transaction.

#![allow(non_snake_case)]

use std::ffi::c_void;

/// Detours' status type: `LONG`. `NO_ERROR` (0) means success.
pub type LONG = i32;
pub const NO_ERROR: LONG = 0;

extern "system" {
    /// Begin a transaction on the calling thread.
    pub fn DetourTransactionBegin() -> LONG;

    /// Abort a transaction, undoing every attach/detach registered in it.
    pub fn DetourTransactionAbort() -> LONG;

    /// Apply every attach/detach registered in the transaction atomically.
    /// Suspends the process, updates other threads, then patches.
    pub fn DetourTransactionCommit() -> LONG;

    /// Enrol a thread's context in the transaction. `thread` is a
    /// `HANDLE` as returned by `GetCurrentThread` or `OpenThread`.
    pub fn DetourUpdateThread(thread: *mut c_void) -> LONG;

    /// Attach a detour.
    ///
    /// `target` points to the caller's copy of the function-pointer
    /// slot. Detours overwrites `*target` with the trampoline address
    /// and patches the target function in place.
    pub fn DetourAttach(target: *mut *mut c_void, detour: *mut c_void) -> LONG;

    /// Remove a detour installed by `DetourAttach` with the same pair.
    pub fn DetourDetach(target: *mut *mut c_void, detour: *mut c_void) -> LONG;

    /// Restore the Detours runtime state after a DLL has been loaded.
    /// Called once from the injected DLL after `DllMain`.
    pub fn DetourRestoreAfterWith() -> LONG;
}


===== FILE: src\platform\windows\handles.rs =====
//! RAII wrappers for Win32 resources. Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/Handles.h`

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::marker::PhantomData;

pub type HANDLE = *mut c_void;
pub type HKEY   = *mut c_void;

/// `(HANDLE)-1`. The canonical "invalid" handle value returned by some
/// Win32 APIs (notably `CreateFileW`).
pub const INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE: HANDLE = !0usize as HANDLE;

// ─── HandlePolicy ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub trait HandlePolicy: Copy + Clone {
    fn is_valid(h: HANDLE) -> bool;
    fn close(h: HANDLE);
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct NullHandlePolicy;

impl HandlePolicy for NullHandlePolicy {
    fn is_valid(h: HANDLE) -> bool { !h.is_null() }
    fn close(h: HANDLE) {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle(h); }
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        { let _ = h; }
    }
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct InvalidHandlePolicy;

impl HandlePolicy for InvalidHandlePolicy {
    fn is_valid(h: HANDLE) -> bool {
        !h.is_null() && h != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE
    }
    fn close(h: HANDLE) {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle(h); }
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        { let _ = h; }
    }
}

// ─── UniqueHandleT<P> ───────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct UniqueHandleT<P: HandlePolicy> {
    handle: HANDLE,
    _policy: PhantomData<P>,
}

impl<P: HandlePolicy> UniqueHandleT<P> {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self { handle: std::ptr::null_mut(), _policy: PhantomData }
    }

    pub const fn from_raw(handle: HANDLE) -> Self {
        Self { handle, _policy: PhantomData }
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> HANDLE { self.handle }

    pub fn is_valid(&self) -> bool { P::is_valid(self.handle) }

    pub fn reset_to(&mut self, handle: HANDLE) {
        if P::is_valid(self.handle) {
            P::close(self.handle);
        }
        self.handle = handle;
    }

    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        self.reset_to(std::ptr::null_mut());
    }
}

impl<P: HandlePolicy> Default for UniqueHandleT<P> {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }
}

impl<P: HandlePolicy> Drop for UniqueHandleT<P> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if P::is_valid(self.handle) {
            P::close(self.handle);
        }
    }
}

pub type UniqueHandle     = UniqueHandleT<NullHandlePolicy>;
pub type UniqueFileHandle = UniqueHandleT<InvalidHandlePolicy>;

// ─── UniqueRegKey ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct UniqueRegKey {
    key: HKEY,
}

impl UniqueRegKey {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self { key: std::ptr::null_mut() }
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> HKEY { self.key }
    pub fn is_valid(&self) -> bool { !self.key.is_null() }

    pub fn put(&mut self) -> *mut HKEY {
        self.reset();
        &mut self.key
    }

    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        if !self.key.is_null() {
            #[cfg(windows)]
            unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::System::Registry::RegCloseKey(self.key); }
        }
        self.key = std::ptr::null_mut();
    }
}

impl Default for UniqueRegKey {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }
}

impl Drop for UniqueRegKey {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.reset();
    }
}

// ─── UniqueMapView ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct UniqueMapView {
    base: *const u8,
}

impl UniqueMapView {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self { base: std::ptr::null() }
    }

    pub const fn from_raw(base: *const u8) -> Self {
        Self { base }
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> *const u8 { self.base }
    pub fn is_valid(&self) -> bool { !self.base.is_null() }

    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        if !self.base.is_null() {
            #[cfg(windows)]
            unsafe {
                // UnmapViewOfFile takes a MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS wrapper
                // struct in windows-sys 0.59. The field is a *mut c_void.
                let addr = windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::MEMORY_MAPPED_VIEW_ADDRESS {
                    Value: self.base as *mut c_void,
                };
                windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::UnmapViewOfFile(addr);
            }
        }
        self.base = std::ptr::null();
    }
}

impl Default for UniqueMapView {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }
}

impl Drop for UniqueMapView {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.reset();
    }
}

// ─── ScopeExit<F> ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct ScopeExit<F: FnOnce()> {
    closure: Option<F>,
}

impl<F: FnOnce()> ScopeExit<F> {
    pub fn new(closure: F) -> Self {
        Self { closure: Some(closure) }
    }

    pub fn dismiss(&mut self) {
        self.closure = None;
    }
}

impl<F: FnOnce()> Drop for ScopeExit<F> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(f) = self.closure.take() {
            f();
        }
    }
}

// ─── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::cell::Cell;

    thread_local! {
        static CLOSE_COUNT: Cell<u32> = const { Cell::new(0) };
    }

    fn reset_count() { CLOSE_COUNT.with(|c| c.set(0)); }
    fn count()       -> u32 { CLOSE_COUNT.with(|c| c.get()) }

    #[derive(Copy, Clone)]
    struct SpyPolicy;

    impl HandlePolicy for SpyPolicy {
        fn is_valid(h: HANDLE) -> bool { !h.is_null() }
        fn close(_h: HANDLE) { CLOSE_COUNT.with(|c| c.set(c.get() + 1)); }
    }

    #[test]
    fn null_handle_default_is_empty() {
        let h = UniqueHandle::new();
        assert!(h.get().is_null());
        assert!(!h.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_handle_value_is_not_valid() {
        let h = UniqueFileHandle::from_raw(INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE);
        assert!(!h.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn null_handle_policy_accepts_null() {
        assert!(!NullHandlePolicy::is_valid(std::ptr::null_mut()));
        assert!(NullHandlePolicy::is_valid(0x1000 as HANDLE));
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_handle_policy_rejects_invalid_value() {
        assert!(!InvalidHandlePolicy::is_valid(INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE));
        assert!(!InvalidHandlePolicy::is_valid(std::ptr::null_mut()));
        assert!(InvalidHandlePolicy::is_valid(0x1000 as HANDLE));
    }

    #[test]
    fn spy_policy_close_runs_on_drop() {
        reset_count();
        {
            let _h = UniqueHandleT::<SpyPolicy>::from_raw(0x1000 as HANDLE);
        }
        assert_eq!(count(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn spy_policy_close_skipped_for_null() {
        reset_count();
        {
            let _h = UniqueHandleT::<SpyPolicy>::from_raw(std::ptr::null_mut());
        }
        assert_eq!(count(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn spy_policy_close_runs_on_reset_to() {
        reset_count();
        let mut h = UniqueHandleT::<SpyPolicy>::from_raw(0x1000 as HANDLE);
        h.reset_to(0x2000 as HANDLE);
        assert_eq!(count(), 1);
        drop(h);
        assert_eq!(count(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn spy_policy_close_runs_once_on_double_reset() {
        reset_count();
        let mut h = UniqueHandleT::<SpyPolicy>::from_raw(0x1000 as HANDLE);
        h.reset();
        h.reset();
        drop(h);
        assert_eq!(count(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn spy_policy_metadata_round_trips() {
        let h = UniqueHandleT::<SpyPolicy>::from_raw(0x1234 as HANDLE);
        assert_eq!(h.get() as usize, 0x1234);
        assert!(h.is_valid());
        std::mem::forget(h);
    }

    #[test]
    fn reg_key_default_is_empty() {
        let k = UniqueRegKey::new();
        assert!(k.get().is_null());
        assert!(!k.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn map_view_default_is_empty() {
        let m = UniqueMapView::new();
        assert!(m.get().is_null());
        assert!(!m.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn map_view_metadata_round_trips() {
        let m = UniqueMapView::from_raw(0x8000 as *const u8);
        assert_eq!(m.get() as usize, 0x8000);
        assert!(m.is_valid());
        std::mem::forget(m);
    }

    #[test]
    fn scope_exit_runs_on_drop() {
        let fired = Cell::new(false);
        {
            let _g = ScopeExit::new(|| { fired.set(true); });
        }
        assert!(fired.get());
    }

    #[test]
    fn scope_exit_dismiss_prevents_run() {
        let fired = Cell::new(false);
        {
            let mut g = ScopeExit::new(|| { fired.set(true); });
            g.dismiss();
        }
        assert!(!fired.get());
    }

    #[test]
    fn scope_exit_runs_exactly_once() {
        let counter = Cell::new(0u32);
        {
            let _g = ScopeExit::new(|| { counter.set(counter.get() + 1); });
        }
        assert_eq!(counter.get(), 1);
    }
}

===== FILE: src\platform\windows\nt_abi.rs =====
//! NtDLL ABI surface used for process inspection.
//! Source: `OSTPlatform/Windows/NtAbi.h`
//!
//! These structures are walked to read another process's PEB and
//! command line / environment. All offsets are checked against the
//! `static_assert`s in the C++ header.
//!
//! ## Stub phase
//!
//! Only the types are here. The functions that consume them
//! (`NtQueryInformationProcess`, `NtQueryVirtualMemory`) will be
//! resolved by `Process.cpp` in sub-batch 2f, which is where the FFI
//! bindings for `ntdll.dll` are added.

use std::ffi::c_void;

// ─── Windows ABI primitives ─────────────────────────────────────────

pub type BYTE      = u8;
pub type ULONG     = u32;
pub type ULONG_PTR = usize;
pub type LONG      = i32;
pub type NTSTATUS  = i32;
pub type SIZE_T    = usize;

pub type PVOID   = *mut c_void;
pub type PULONG  = *mut ULONG;
pub type PSIZE_T = *mut SIZE_T;

/// `HANDLE` - kept as a raw pointer for the same reason as in
/// [`super::handles`].
pub type HANDLE = *mut c_void;

// ─── Enums ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[repr(u32)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ProcessInfoClass {
    BasicInformation = 0,
    Wow64Information = 26,
}

#[repr(u32)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemoryInfoClass {
    BasicInformation = 0,
}

// ─── Return type ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// `NtSuccess` is a signed comparison: `NTSTATUS` is `LONG`, and values
// with the high bit set (`STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL = 0xC0000001`, etc.) are
// errors. `status >= 0` is the C++ rule; keep it identical.

#[inline]
pub const fn nt_success(status: NTSTATUS) -> bool {
    status >= 0
}

// ─── Structs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// All `#[repr(C)]`. Offset asserts below match the C++ `static_assert`s.

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ProcessBasicInformation {
    pub exit_status: NTSTATUS,
    // 4 bytes padding on x64 before the 8-byte pointer
    pub peb_base_address: PVOID,
    pub affinity_mask: ULONG_PTR,
    pub base_priority: LONG,
    // 4 bytes padding on x64 before the 8-byte ULONG_PTR
    pub unique_process_id: ULONG_PTR,
    pub inherited_from_unique_process_id: ULONG_PTR,
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct UnicodeString {
    pub length: u16,
    pub maximum_length: u16,
    pub padding: u32,
    pub buffer: PVOID,
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct UnicodeString32 {
    pub length: u16,
    pub maximum_length: u16,
    pub buffer: u32,
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Peb {
    pub reserved0: [BYTE; 0x20],
    pub process_parameters: PVOID,
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct RtlUserProcessParameters {
    pub reserved0: [BYTE; 0x70],
    pub command_line: UnicodeString,  // offset 0x70
    pub environment: PVOID,           // offset 0x80
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Peb32 {
    pub reserved0: [BYTE; 0x10],
    pub process_parameters: u32,
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct RtlUserProcessParameters32 {
    pub reserved0: [BYTE; 0x40],
    pub command_line: UnicodeString32,  // offset 0x40
    pub environment: u32,               // offset 0x48
}

// ─── Offset asserts (mirror the C++ static_asserts) ─────────────────

const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(Peb, process_parameters) == 0x20);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters, command_line) == 0x70);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters, environment) == 0x80);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(Peb32, process_parameters) == 0x10);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters32, command_line) == 0x40);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters32, environment) == 0x48);

// ─── Function pointer types ─────────────────────────────────────────

/// `NTAPI` is `__stdcall`. On x64 there is only one calling convention,
/// so `extern "system"` is correct on both targets.
pub type NtQueryInformationProcessFn = unsafe extern "system" fn(
    HANDLE,
    ProcessInfoClass,
    PVOID,
    ULONG,
    PULONG,
) -> NTSTATUS;

pub type NtQueryVirtualMemoryFn = unsafe extern "system" fn(
    HANDLE,
    PVOID,
    MemoryInfoClass,
    PVOID,
    SIZE_T,
    PSIZE_T,
) -> NTSTATUS;

// ─── Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use core::mem::{offset_of, size_of};

    #[test]
    fn process_info_class_values() {
        assert_eq!(ProcessInfoClass::BasicInformation as u32, 0);
        assert_eq!(ProcessInfoClass::Wow64Information as u32, 26);
    }

    #[test]
    fn memory_info_class_values() {
        assert_eq!(MemoryInfoClass::BasicInformation as u32, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn nt_success_matches_cpp_rule() {
        assert!(nt_success(0));
        assert!(nt_success(1));
        assert!(nt_success(0x7FFF_FFFF)); // STATUS_SUCCESS upper bound
        assert!(!nt_success(-1));
        // STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL = 0xC0000001 => as i32 it is negative
        assert!(!nt_success(0xC000_0001u32 as i32));
    }

    #[test]
    fn ntstatus_is_i32() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<NTSTATUS>(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ulong_and_long_are_4_bytes() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<ULONG>(), 4);
        assert_eq!(size_of::<LONG>(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ulong_ptr_and_size_t_match_pointer_width() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<ULONG_PTR>(), size_of::<usize>());
        assert_eq!(size_of::<SIZE_T>(), size_of::<usize>());
    }

    #[test]
    fn unicode_string_layout() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<UnicodeString>(), 16);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(UnicodeString, length), 0);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(UnicodeString, maximum_length), 2);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(UnicodeString, padding), 4);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(UnicodeString, buffer), 8);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unicode_string32_layout() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<UnicodeString32>(), 8);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(UnicodeString32, buffer), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn peb_layout() {
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(Peb, process_parameters), 0x20);
        assert_eq!(size_of::<Peb>(), 0x28);
    }

    #[test]
    fn peb32_layout() {
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(Peb32, process_parameters), 0x10);
        assert_eq!(size_of::<Peb32>(), 0x14);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rtl_user_process_parameters_layout() {
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters, command_line), 0x70);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters, environment), 0x80);
        assert_eq!(size_of::<RtlUserProcessParameters>(), 0x88);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rtl_user_process_parameters32_layout() {
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters32, command_line), 0x40);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(RtlUserProcessParameters32, environment), 0x48);
        assert_eq!(size_of::<RtlUserProcessParameters32>(), 0x4C);
    }

    #[test]
    fn process_basic_information_layout() {
        // exit_status(4) pad(4) ptr(8) ptr(8) long(4) pad(4) ptr(8) ptr(8) = 0x30
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(ProcessBasicInformation, exit_status), 0);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(ProcessBasicInformation, peb_base_address), 8);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(ProcessBasicInformation, affinity_mask), 16);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(ProcessBasicInformation, base_priority), 24);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(ProcessBasicInformation, unique_process_id), 32);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(ProcessBasicInformation, inherited_from_unique_process_id), 40);
        assert_eq!(size_of::<ProcessBasicInformation>(), 48);
    }

    #[test]
    fn function_pointers_are_pointer_sized() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<NtQueryInformationProcessFn>(), size_of::<usize>());
        assert_eq!(size_of::<NtQueryVirtualMemoryFn>(), size_of::<usize>());
    }

//! Callback structs the codebase intercepts or injects.
//! Source: `Steam/Callback.h`

#![allow(non_camel_case_types)]

use super::types::*;
use super::enums::EResult;

pub const K_ISTEAM_USER_CALLBACKS: i32 = 100;

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct EncryptedAppTicketResponse_t {
    pub m_eResult: EResult,
}

impl EncryptedAppTicketResponse_t {
    pub const K_ICALLBACK: i32 = K_ISTEAM_USER_CALLBACKS + 54;
}

/// Broadcast when app licenses change. Sent by CClientAppManager after
/// ProcessPendingLicenseUpdates.
///
/// Layout under the default C++ alignment (this struct is NOT packed):
///   bool      m_bReloadAll          0x00
///   bool      m_bIsFirstLoad        0x01
///   (2 bytes pad)
///   uint32    m_unRemainingPackets  0x04
///   uint32    m_unCount             0x08
///   AppId_t   m_rgAppsUpdated[64]   0x0C  (256 bytes)
///   (4 bytes pad to align u64)
///   uint64    m_unAppsAdded         0x110
/// Total: 0x118 bytes.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct AppLicensesChanged_t {
    pub m_bReloadAll: bool,
    pub m_bIsFirstLoad: bool,
    pub m_unRemainingPackets: u32,
    pub m_unCount: u32,
    pub m_rgAppsUpdated: [AppId_t; 64],
    pub m_unAppsAdded: u64,
}

impl AppLicensesChanged_t {
    pub const K_ICALLBACK: i32 = 1_020_094;
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use core::mem::size_of;
    use core::mem::offset_of;

    #[test]
    fn encrypted_app_ticket_response_layout() {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<EncryptedAppTicketResponse_t>(), 4);
        assert_eq!(EncryptedAppTicketResponse_t::K_ICALLBACK, 154);
    }

    #[test]
    fn app_licenses_changed_layout() {
        // The C++ header comments the exact offsets. Assert them.
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(AppLicensesChanged_t, m_bReloadAll), 0x00);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(AppLicensesChanged_t, m_bIsFirstLoad), 0x01);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(AppLicensesChanged_t, m_unRemainingPackets), 0x04);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(AppLicensesChanged_t, m_unCount), 0x08);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(AppLicensesChanged_t, m_rgAppsUpdated), 0x0C);
        assert_eq!(offset_of!(AppLicensesChanged_t, m_unAppsAdded), 0x110);
        assert_eq!(size_of::<AppLicensesChanged_t>(), 0x118);
        assert_eq!(AppLicensesChanged_t::K_ICALLBACK, 1_020_094);
    }
}


===== FILE: src\steam\enums.rs =====
//! All steamclient enums. Source: `Steam/Enums.h`
//!
//! Notes on the port:
//!  * `EMsg` is a newtype over `u32`, not a Rust enum, because the C++ enum
//!    contains aliased values (e.g. `k_EMsgBaseGeneral == k_EMsgGenericReply`).
//!    Every named value and alias is preserved as an associated const.
//!    Pattern-match via `msg.0` when you need to switch on a value.
//!  * `EAppOwnershipFlags`, `EAppState` and `EAppChangeFlags` are modelled
//!    with the `bitflags` crate because they are used as bitmasks in C++.
//!  * `EWebSocketOpCode : char` uses `#[repr(u8)]` - all defined values are
//!    non-negative. `char` on MSVC x64 is signed, but no negative values
//!    are used.

#![allow(non_camel_case_types)]
#![allow(non_upper_case_globals)]

use bitflags::bitflags;
use super::types::*;

mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use core::mem::size_of;

    #[test]
    fn e_result_spot_values() {

        assert_eq!(EResult::Fail as i32, 2);
